title: [tunnel-mcp-client] 1.2 System Requirements
description:
Turn the user requirements into technical constraints: API contracts, data model, performance, security, integration points. Pre-filled below: confirm or adjust, record in notes, close.

Arc specifics:
- services/tunnels.ts: send `transports: ["debugg","ngrok"]`; accept `transport`, `relayUrl` and
  `tunnelDomain`; a missing `transport` means ngrok.
- TunnelTransport interface { connect(localAddr, hostname, token, opts) → publicUrl; disconnect(publicUrl);
  probe?(path) }. ngrokTransport = today's code, including the ngrokAgentSession pre-warm. debuggTransport
  = protocol module plus `ws`. TunnelManager.connectWithRetry picks one from the provision response. The
  retry ladder, idle timer and session keys are unchanged.
- debuggTransport: connect with the Authorization, X-Tunnel-Id and protocol headers. On OPEN, dial ONLY the
  registered local origin (Caddy loopback; host.docker.internal in Docker, per the existing matrix).
  Reconnect with backoff on a drop or GOAWAY, keeping the same URL. A 401 is non-retryable and maps to
  today's auth-error path.
- Hostnames: replace the hardcoded `.ngrok.debugg.ai` in utils/urlParser.ts (replaceTunnelUrls,
  generateTunnelUrl) and tunnelManager.ts (isTunnelUrl, extractTunnelId, domain construction) with a list
  of known domains; sanitizeResponseUrls rewrites both.
- Health: for debugg tunnels, probeTunnelHealth uses the control-channel PROBE, because tunnel URLs are
  private and unreachable from the user's machine. Results map onto the existing TunnelHealthProbeResult codes.
- Errors: extractNgrokErrorCode recognizes the DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* markers. The tunnelDisposition allowlist adds
  DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE and DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN; UPSTREAM_REFUSED leaves the tunnel alone, like ERR_NGROK_8012.
- Revoke: debugg tunnels call POST api/v1/tunnels/<id>/revoke/.
- New dependency `ws`: pure JS, and engines.node >=20.20 has no stable global WebSocket.
- Telemetry: add a transport tag to the existing TUNNEL_* events.

Repo: debugg-ai-mcp. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §5. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.5.
notes:
1.2 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS: VERIFIED against the code (worktree tunnel/debugg-transport @ 5ee2768, 2026-09-19) Legend: [OK] = pre-filled claim confirmed. [C] = corrected by the code. [+] = added because the code or the design requires it. [D] = default chosen for an open point; the alternative is noted, and the owner can override. Baseline before any change: npm test gives 72 suites, 1126 passed, 1 skipped. ## R1. Provision: services/tunnels.ts - [OK] Request: POST api/v1/tunnels/ with body {purpose, transports:["debugg","ngrok"]}. - axiosTransport snake_cases request KEYS only. objToSnakeCase leaves non-object array entries untouched, so the string array reaches the wire intact. - [OK] Response: axiosTransport camelCases it, so the backend's relay_url and tunnel_domain arrive as relayUrl and tunnelDomain. - [C] provision() (tunnels.ts ~L143) REBUILDS its return object field by field and drops unknown fields. - Both the TunnelProvision interface and that literal must gain transport, relayUrl and tunnelDomain. - The "missing transport ⇒ 'ngrok'" default lives exactly there. TunnelProvision.transport is always set, to 'ngrok' or 'debugg'. - [+] Validation, all non-retryable TunnelProvisionError: - transport not in {ngrok, debugg}: we only advertised those two. - transport=debugg with relayUrl or tunnelDomain missing. - relayUrl not wss:. ws: is allowed only when the host is loopback (local backend, in-process test server). - tunnelDomain not a lowercase DNS name with at least 3 labels. It gets registered as a URL-rewrite domain (R6), so a value like "debugg.ai" would rewrite legitimate backend links into localhost. - [+] provisionWithRetry, classifyProvisionError and the retry semantics are unchanged. - [+] Existing exact-shape assertions in __tests__/services/tunnels.test.ts will go red at 4.1 BY DESIGN and must be updated then. These are `toHaveBeenCalledWith('api/v1/tunnels/', {purpose})` ×3 and `toEqual({tunnelId,tunnelKey,keyId,expiresAt})`. ## R2. Transport selection and data flow - [C] The provision fields never reach TunnelManager today. Handlers pass tunnelKey, tunnelId and keyId positionally: - tunnelContext.ensureTunnel(ctx, tunnelKey, tunnelId, keyId, revokeKey) → tunnelManager.ensureSessionTunnel(sessionKey, authToken, specificTunnelId, keyId, revokeKey). Called from probePage L208, triggerCrawl L151 and testPageChanges L286. - tunnelManager.acquireDedicatedTunnel(url, authToken, keyId, revokeKey). Called from runTestSuite L103. - [D] Add an optional trailing selection argument, {transport, relayUrl?, tunnelDomain?}, to ensureTunnel, ensureSessionTunnel and acquireDedicatedTunnel. - A TunnelProvision satisfies it structurally, so handlers pass the provision object. - Omitted means ngrok, so every existing call and test keeps its meaning. - Alternative rejected: a hidden module-level tunnelId → provision side channel that needs zero handler edits. That is hidden coupling. - [C] acquireDedicatedTunnel mints its own uuidv4() (L321) and DISCARDS the backend tunnelId. - Under debugg the token is bound to Tunnel.id: the server verifies {X-Tunnel-Id, tunnelKey}, and design §2 says "keyId is the Tunnel.id". A client-minted id would be rejected with 401. - So the debugg dedicated path MUST use provision.tunnelId, passed in the selection. - The ngrok dedicated path keeps minting a uuid, for parity. - [+] TunnelInfo and DirectTunnelInfo record their transport kind so that stop, disconnect, probe and telemetry route correctly. - Session reuse (findExistingTunnel) short-circuits before provision, so a live tunnel keeps its transport until it stops even if the backend flag flips. - [+] There is no client-side fallback from debugg to ngrok. The debugg token can't drive ngrok, and falling back would mask server outages. Rollback is the backend flag (design §2/§7). ## R3. TunnelTransport interface - [C] Pre-filled shape: {connect(localAddr, hostname, token, opts) → publicUrl; disconnect(publicUrl); probe?(path)}. - probe must be keyed by tunnel, because one process can hold a session tunnel AND dedicated tunnels, even on the same transport. It becomes probe?(publicUrl, path, {timeoutMs}). - connect opts must carry tunnelId (for X-Tunnel-Id) and relayUrl. - [C] The ladder in connectWithRetry is NOT transport-neutral today. Four ngrok-only steps are embedded in TunnelManager: - ensureInitialized(): `import('ngrok')` + getApi(). It runs at the top of createSessionTunnel (L499) and acquireDedicatedTunnel (L314), and in the attempt 1→2 reset (L673-675). - ensureAgentSession(): the pqgj pre-warm that spawns the agent through ngrokAgentSession.ts. It runs at the top of connectWithRetry (L604). - disconnectNgrok(): called in stopSessionTunnel and stopDirectTunnel. - maybeResetNgrokModule(): resets when no tunnels remain. It must count ONLY ngrok tunnels once both kinds coexist. - All four become ngrokTransport-internal, through optional hooks: pre-connect warm-up, reset-after-failed-attempt, and all-tunnels-stopped. - Requirement: on the debugg path, `ngrok` is never imported and agentSessionStarter is never called. - [OK] Unchanged: the retry ladder (3 attempts, connectBackoffMs [500,1500]), FaultInjector/TunnelTrace (DEBUGG_TUNNEL_FAULT_MODE), the idle timer, session keys, cold-start dedup, and the stopTunnel unconditional-removal ordering with Promise.allSettled. - [+] The public test seams connectBackoffMs, agentSessionStarter, agentSessionTimeoutMs, caddyFactory and idleTimeoutMs keep working. __tests__/services/tunnelManager.agentReadiness.test.ts drives agentSessionStarter. - Add a transport-injection seam in the same style (a public field) so tests can drive fake transports. ## R4. debuggTransport behaviour - [OK] Handshake headers: Authorization: Bearer , X-Tunnel-Id, X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol: 1, X-Client-Version (= config.server.version). The exact names are owned by protocol xkoh.1.2. - [OK] On OPEN, dial ONLY the localAddr registered at connect. Anything in the OPEN payload (host, port, address) is never used as a dial target. - [C] "Caddy loopback; host.docker.internal in Docker" is imprecise. - Session tunnels ALWAYS dial Caddy's loopback localOrigin (`http://127.0.0.1:`, caddyProxy.ts L548), even in Docker, because Caddy runs in the same container. - The Docker/HTTPS matrix applies only to Caddy's upstream (resolveDialAddress) and to the dedicated path, whose localAddr is one of `127.0.0.1:

`, `host.docker.internal:

`, `https://localhost:

` or `https://host.docker.internal:

` (tunnelManager L336-342). - So debuggTransport must accept all five forms. - https:// means a TLS dial to the local app with verification off. This matches Caddy's `insecure_skip_verify: true` for local self-signed certs (caddyProxy buildPatchBody). - [+] A local dial failure (ECONNREFUSED etc.) → RST with REFUSED on that stream, and the tunnel stays up. The server renders DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED, which is the ERR_NGROK_8012 equivalent. - [OK] Reconnect with backoff on a socket drop or GOAWAY, keeping the same tunnelId and public URL. - [D] Backoff: exponential with jitter, capped at about 10s. - Retry until stopTunnel or the idle timeout, or until a PERMANENT rejection (401/403/426, or the server reports the tunnel unknown or revoked). - On permanent rejection the transport reports the tunnel dead and TunnelManager evicts it through stopTunnel, so the next call re-provisions. - Streams open at the moment of a drop are lost. - [OK] Liveness (protocol-owned): PING every 20s; the peer is dead after 60s of silence. - [+] Process hygiene: ping and reconnect timers are unref()'d. Sockets are closed by stopAllTunnels, which index.ts gracefulShutdown calls on SIGINT/SIGTERM. The transport must not hold a process open longer than today's agent child does. ## R5. Errors and the retry ladder - [C] The auth classification is asymmetric today. - The ladder short-circuits on /authtoken|unauthorized|\b401\b|\b403\b/i (L644). - The user-facing wrapper "Failed to create tunnel: invalid auth token." fires only on msg.includes('authtoken') (L372, L559). - [D] The debugg 401/403 error message contains BOTH "authtoken" and the status, so it is not retried AND it gets today's wrapper text, with no change to the ngrok path. - Alternative: a typed error class plus a widened outer check. Existing tests at tunnelManager.test.ts L236/L540 pin current behaviour. - [+] 426 (unsupported protocol version) must be NON-retryable, but today's regex would retry it. [D] A transport error may carry `retryable:false`, and the ladder honours it in addition to the regex. The ngrok path is unaffected. - The message tells the user to update @debugg-ai/debugg-ai-mcp. - [+] Network errors, 5xx and handshake timeouts are retried through the existing ladder. ## R6. Hostnames and known domains - [C] Complete site list (7, not 5): - urlParser.replaceTunnelUrls regex (L114). - urlParser.generateTunnelUrl: it ALREADY takes a tunnelDomain param defaulting to 'ngrok.debugg.ai' (L154). The bug is its caller, tunnelManager L367, which never passes one. - tunnelManager isTunnelUrl (L455) and extractTunnelId (L459). Neither has a production caller, only tests, but both are fixed for correctness. - Domain construction at tunnelManager L322 (dedicated) and L502 (session). - services/ngrok/ngrokAgentInspector.ts L45 OWNED_TUNNEL_SUFFIX. It is DELIBERATELY left ngrok-only: no production importer, and it inspects the ngrok agent. - [OK] Known domains = {ngrok.debugg.ai, tunnel.debugg.ai}, plus any valid tunnelDomain received from a provision response (registered at runtime), so a server-side domain move can never leak URLs. - replaceTunnelUrls, isTunnelUrl and extractTunnelId handle every known domain. - sanitizeResponseUrls (tunnelContext) delegates to replaceTunnelUrls, so it needs no change of its own. ## R7. Health: probeTunnelHealth - [C] probeTunnelHealth(url, opts) is a free function taking only a URL, with 5 call sites: probePage L311, triggerCrawl L182, testPageChanges L330 and L811 (post-run re-probe), and runTestSuite L117. It has no handle on a transport. - [D] Route on the URL itself. For a host under a debugg tunnel domain, use the control-channel prober registered for that host by debuggTransport (registered on connect, removed on disconnect); otherwise fall back to the HTTP/1.1 fetch as today. This needs zero handler edits. - Alternative: handlers inject a prober through opts (5 edits). - The probe path is the URL's pathname + search. - [OK] Results map onto the EXISTING TunnelHealthProbeResult ({healthy, status, code, ngrokErrorCode, detail, elapsedMs}). [D] The field names are kept (see 1.1 non-goals): - marker M → {healthy:false, status, code:'NGROK_ERROR', ngrokErrorCode:M}. - 502/504 without a marker → BAD_GATEWAY. - Any other status → healthy:true. - PROBE_RESULT error indicating a timeout → TIMEOUT; any other error → NETWORK_ERROR. - No PROBE_RESULT within opts.timeoutMs (default 5000) → TIMEOUT, not retried. - Control channel currently reconnecting → transient, retried by the existing k6yq ladder; still down → NETWORK_ERROR (tunnel kept). - [D] No live debugg session in this process for that host → ngrokErrorCode 'DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN', so the disposition evicts any leftover state. - [+] ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND_CODES (L161, "confirm across the retry ladder before reporting gone") adds DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE and DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN, because the server holds requests briefly and reports offline during a reconnect. DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED is returned on the first sample, like 8012. ## R8. Markers and disposition - [OK] extractNgrokErrorCode learns the markers. [C] Use an EXPLICIT list (DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE | DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED | DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN), not /DEBUGG_TUNNEL_[A-Z_]+/, which would match the env var name DEBUGG_TUNNEL_FAULT_MODE. - ERR_NGROK_\d+ keeps working. - [C] Second consumer: testPageChangesHandler findNgrokErrorMarker (L76) scans RUN EVIDENCE for the marker and reclassifies to TunnelOfflineDuringRun. Parity means any DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* marker reclassifies, as any ERR_NGROK_* does today. - Its user copy (~L906-914, "ngrok's interstitial") must become transport-neutral. - [OK] tunnelDisposition ENDPOINT_GONE_CODES (L79) = ERR_NGROK_3200, DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE, DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN. - [C] The marker is DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED in full. It is NOT gone: the tunnel is kept, like 8012. - The export is named ENDPOINT_GONE_NGROK_CODES and keeps its name in v1. - __tests__/utils/tunnelDisposition.test.ts pins toEqual(['ERR_NGROK_3200']). That test goes red at 4.1 BY DESIGN ("adding a code must be a deliberate act") and is updated then; it is not a regression. ## R9. Revoke - [C] TunnelManager calls no endpoint. It calls the revokeKey CALLBACK stored on TunnelInfo. - The four handlers build that callback as `() => client.revokeNgrokKey(tunnel.keyId)`: probePage L213, triggerCrawl L156, testPageChanges L291, runTestSuite L107. - Each handler also revokes orphaned keys directly in `finally`: probePage L540, triggerCrawl L405, testPageChanges L1069, runTestSuite L177. - revokeNgrokKey is services/index.ts L586: POST api/v1/ngrok/revoke/ {ngrokKeyId}. - [D] Add a transport-aware revoke on TunnelsService (services/tunnels.ts), revoke(provision): - ngrok → api/v1/ngrok/revoke/ {ngrokKeyId: keyId}, exactly as today. - debugg → POST api/v1/tunnels//revoke/. - The 8 handler sites switch to it (mechanical). - revokeNgrokKey stays for compatibility. - [OK] stopTunnel for a debugg tunnel closes the websocket (no reconnect afterwards), unregisters the prober, and runs the revoke callback, under the same unconditional-removal + allSettled contract. ## R10. Telemetry - [+] Add a `transport` property ('ngrok' | 'debugg') to TUNNEL_PROVISIONED, TUNNEL_STOPPED, TUNNEL_EVICTED_PORT_CHANGED, TUNNEL_TEARDOWN_PARTIAL_FAILURE and TUNNEL_PROVISION_RETRY. - [C] TUNNEL_PROVISION_RETRY has TWO emitters: - tunnels.ts (backend provision, no stage). Transport is known only after a successful response. - connectWithRetry (stage:'ngrok_connect', L633/649/659). [D] The ngrok path keeps 'ngrok_connect' for dashboard continuity; debugg emits 'debugg_connect'. ## R11. Dependencies and build - [OK] ws is the only new runtime dependency. engines.node is >=20.20 with no stable global WebSocket. - [+] ws 8.18.3 is already present in node_modules transitively, but it is NOT in package.json, and @types/ws is ABSENT. - The protocol agent (package.json owner) must add `ws` to dependencies and `@types/ws` to devDependencies. Otherwise `npx tsc --noEmit` fails (TS7016) on any production import of ws. - Tests are unaffected: tsconfig isolatedModules:true makes ts-jest transpile-only, and tsc excludes __tests__. ## R12. Security - tunnelKey appears only in the Authorization header: never in a URL or query string, never logged, never in TunnelTrace, error text or telemetry. - Reject a non-wss relayUrl before sending the token (R1). - OPEN never selects a dial target (R4). - Honour the protocol's per-stream buffer and concurrency bounds. - The HTTP-mode cross-tenant isolation of the per-session-key tunnel is unchanged. A transport session belongs to exactly one tunnel. ## R13. Performance - No pre-warm on the debugg path. Target connect time: handshake + server verify < 1s p50 from the user's machine. - Multiplexed streams, with no websocket per request (54 requests per Next.js page, measured). - Flow control per protocol: 256 KiB initial window, 64 KiB max DATA, so HMR is never starved by a big chunk. ## CROSS-ARC RISK (for the owner; does not block this arc) - Design §2 says expires_at bounds connects AND RECONNECTS. - A session tunnel lives as long as it is used: the idle timer re-arms on every touch. - So any tunnel older than its token's expiresAt that receives a GOAWAY during a tunnel-server deploy cannot reconnect (401), and it dies mid-run, contrary to the "deploys don't fail runs" goal. - The MCP handles this safely (R4: evict, then re-provision on the next call). Whether the server should let a previously connected, unrevoked tunnel reconnect past expires_at, bounded by the 24h max, is a backend-arc decision. ## OPEN QUESTIONS (defaults chosen; none blocks 2.1) Q1. 4.1 needs mechanical edits outside this arc's listed files, in the 4 handlers and services/index.ts: pass the provision through (R2) and use the transport-aware revoke (R9). Default: yes, in 4.1. Q2. Keep the ngrok-named output field and code (ngrokErrorCode, 'NGROK_ERROR') for debugg results in v1 so the tool output shape is unchanged? Default: yes. Q3. The cross-arc risk above. ## ADDENDUM (2026-09-19, after the protocol spec landed on xkoh.1.2) A1. Handshake header names are X-Debugg-Tunnel-Id, X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol (a comma-separated list of versions the client speaks) and X-Debugg-Tunnel-Client-Version. R4's X-Tunnel-Id / X-Client-Version were renamed by the protocol arc for one greppable namespace, matching the existing X-Debugg-Tunnel-Error response header. The 101 echoes the selected version, and a missing or un-offered echo is a client-side PROTOCOL_ERROR. A2. R7 said the ladder-confirm set (ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND_CODES) gains OFFLINE and UNKNOWN. Corrected: it gains DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE only. UNKNOWN means the id is gone and re-probing cannot change that, so it is reported on the first sample. Both still belong in tunnelDisposition's teardown allowlist; UPSTREAM_REFUSED belongs in neither. A3. Terminal handshake statuses are 426, 400 and 401 (one 401 covers bad key, unknown id, revoked and expired — the server deliberately does not say which). 429, 5xx and network errors stay retryable, which is what R5's `retryable:false` flag expresses. A4. Two error codes beyond R4's list: UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE (6), which the client sends as RST when it cannot dial the local app and the server renders as DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED, and REVOKED (7), meaning never reconnect with this token. A5. PROBE_RESULT.error is a string ("TIMEOUT" | "RESET" | "CLOSED" | ...), the probe API never throws, and the client-side PROBE deadline is 5000ms — the same default TunnelHealthProbeOptions.timeoutMs already has.
close_reason: System requirements verified against code; 11 corrections recorded (revoke lives in handler callbacks + services/index.ts; dedicated path discards backend tunnelId; ngrok-only steps embedded in the ladder; asymmetric auth classification; probeTunnelHealth is URL-only; marker regex must be an explicit list; 7 hostname sites; ws types missing). Open questions carry defaults and do not block 2.1.

- __tests__/services/tunnelManager.transport.test.ts — 12 tests, 12 red.
  A debugg selection drives the transport (localAddr = Caddy loopback, hostname = <id>.tunnel.debugg.ai, token, relayUrl); the ngrok package is NEVER imported and the agent never pre-warmed; Docker still dials the in-container Caddy loopback; telemetry carries transport:'debugg'; the dedicated path uses the PROVISIONED tunnel id and the existing Docker/HTTPS matrix; a 401 is not retried and keeps today's "invalid auth token" message; an error flagged retryable:false (426) stops the ladder; a transient failure still gets the 3-attempt ladder; stopTunnel disconnects through the transport and revokes; a transport reporting permanent death evicts the tunnel.
  Failure reasons: the transport seam does not exist, so ngrok is still used — the sharpest one is "ngrok imports: expected 0, received 1".
- __tests__/utils/localReachability.probe.test.ts — 22 tests, 21 red, 1 green guard.
  extractNgrokErrorCode reads the three DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* markers and still reads ERR_NGROK_*, and must NOT match the env var name DEBUGG_TUNNEL_FAULT_MODE; probeTunnelHealth routes a debugg host through the registered control prober and never fetches the private URL; the PROBE path carries this caller's path+search; an ngrok URL still takes the HTTP path; a debugg host with no live control channel reports DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN; the full PROBE_RESULT mapping from xkoh.1.2 §9; OFFLINE is confirmed across the retry ladder while UNKNOWN and UPSTREAM_REFUSED return on the first sample.
  Failure reasons: "not implemented" from the probe registry stub, and markers not recognised.
- __tests__/services/debuggTransport.test.ts — 21 tests, 21 red ("not implemented" from createDebuggTransport).
  Handshake headers (Authorization: Bearer, X-Debugg-Tunnel-Id, X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol, X-Debugg-Tunnel-Client-Version) and no secret in the URL; a 101 with no protocol echo or a version we never offered is refused; 401/426/400 are terminal (retryable:false) while 5xx and socket errors are retryable; OPEN metadata cannot redirect the dial (the SSRF boundary, proved against a real loopback HTTP server, with the Host header preserved); local refusal produces RST(UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE) and keeps the tunnel up; GOAWAY(GOING_AWAY) dials a new connection make-before-break; an abrupt drop reconnects with backoff; GOAWAY(REVOKED) and a 401 on reconnect are permanent and call onDead; disconnect never reconnects; PROBE sends the path and resolves PROBE_RESULT, times out as {error:'TIMEOUT'} and never throws, and resolves pending probes as {error:'CLOSED'} on session close; the control prober is registered on connect and removed on disconnect.
  The websocket is faked through a socketFactory seam and frames are hand-encoded from the spec, so these tests need no `ws` server and no codec.

## Stub modules added (no logic)
- services/tunnel/transport.ts — TunnelTransportKind, TunnelTransportSelection, TunnelConnectOptions, TunnelTransportError, and the TunnelTransport interface: connect(localAddr, hostname, token, opts) -> publicUrl, disconnect(publicUrl), optional probe(publicUrl, path, opts), plus the ngrok-only hooks (prepare, resetAfterFailedAttempt, onAllTunnelsStopped) that the retry ladder needs so it can stay transport-neutral.
- services/tunnel/debuggTransport.ts — createDebuggTransport(options) throws 'not implemented'; declares DebuggSocketLike (structurally ws, widening the protocol module's WebSocketLike), DebuggSocketFactory and the options (clientVersion, socketFactory, reconnectBackoffMs, probeTimeoutMs).
- services/tunnel/probeRegistry.ts — registerControlProbe / unregisterControlProbe / getControlProbe, all throwing. This is the seam that lets probeTunnelHealth reach a control channel without changing its URL-only signature or its five call sites.

## Corrections to xkoh.5.2 from the protocol spec (xkoh.1.2)
1. Header names: the protocol renamed them for one greppable namespace. They are X-Debugg-Tunnel-Id, X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol (a comma-separated version list) and X-Debugg-Tunnel-Client-Version — not X-Tunnel-Id / X-Client-Version.
2. The ladder-confirm set (localReachability ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND_CODES) gets DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE only. R7 had said OFFLINE and UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN means the id is gone, which re-probing cannot change, so it is returned on the first sample. Both still belong in tunnelDisposition's teardown allowlist.
3. Terminal handshake statuses are 426, 400 and 401 (401 covers bad key, unknown id, revoked and expired — the server deliberately does not say which). 429, 5xx and network errors are retryable.
4. Two new error codes beyond the pre-filled list: UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE (6), which a client sends as RST when it cannot dial the local app and the server renders as DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED, and REVOKED (7), which means never reconnect with this token.
5. PROBE_RESULT.error is a string like "TIMEOUT" | "RESET" | "CLOSED"; the probe API never throws, which preserves probeTunnelHealth's existing contract.

## Known interactions for 4.1 (not regressions)
- Three existing assertions will go red when the implementation lands and must be updated deliberately: the exact request body and exact result object in __tests__/services/tunnels.test.ts, and the exact allowlist membership in __tests__/utils/tunnelDisposition.test.ts (that one is designed to force this decision).
- The debuggTransport tests that drive real streams (OPEN dial, RST, DATA) also need the protocol arc's session implementation (xkoh.1.7), so they stay red until both arcs land.

title: [tunnel-infra] 3.1 Technical Strategy
description:
With the failing suite as the definition of correct, decide: patterns (and why), build vs reuse, which tests go green first, risks and mitigations, and the rollback plan. Record with `--design`.

Arc specifics:
Decide: rc support vs terraform alongside rc vs the nginx-TLS fallback. Staging first. Rollback: remove the
nginx blocks and route rules; the backend flag keeps everyone on ngrok.

Repo: platform/sentinal. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §4. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.4.
design:
TECHNICAL STRATEGY - tunnel infra (nginx, DNS, cert, internal ALB, rc service)

== THE DECIDING FACT ==
rc (qosha1/remote-compose, pinned RC_REF e8c9f8fd; HEAD 0826cca is no different)
emits exactly ONE `load_balancer {}` block per public service, on its own
internet-facing ALB, and the ECS service's `lifecycle` ignores only
[task_definition] - not load_balancer. It also hardcodes `internal = false` on a
single aws_lb and creates no Route53 zone of any kind.

Consequence: a sidecar terraform module CAN create the internal ALB, its target
group, the cert and both zones, but it CANNOT attach the rc-managed nginx service
to that target group. An out-of-band attachment (console, CLI, or a second
terraform state) is silently REVERTED by the next `rc deploy`, which applies
terraform on every push to main since platform-0s2 - and the revert reads as a
normal nginx deployment, so the private data plane would go dark with a green CI.
That is the one thing that decides between the options.

== OPTIONS ==
(A) RECOMMENDED - sidecar terraform + ONE small rc feature.
    rc gains `services.<svc>.extra_target_groups: [{arn, container_port}]`, which
    renders extra `load_balancer {}` blocks. ~5 touch points in remote-compose
    (schema dataclass, parser, ServiceSpec, provider view, services.tf.j2) plus
    tests; back-compatible by construction (absent key => byte-identical HCL, the
    same contract rc's earlier network/IAM work used). Then deploy/prod/rc.yml
    names the TG arn the sidecar module outputs, and terraform attaches nginx.
    Everything else (zones, ACM, internal ALB, listener, TG, ALB SG) lives in
    deploy/prod/tunnel-edge/ with its own S3 state key - the shape
    deploy/shared-vpc-nat-route/main.tf already established for "infra rc cannot
    express, kept out of rc's state on purpose".
    Cost: one PR in another repo + an RC_REF bump.
    Win: ACM auto-renewal, ALB target draining and health checks, idle_timeout
    3600 for HMR, and the architecture the owner already chose.

(B) Sidecar terraform ALONE - rejected. It gets you everything except the
    attachment, i.e. everything except traffic. Listed only so the next reader
    does not re-derive it.

(C) FALLBACK, zero rc changes - nginx terminates TLS itself.
    Private zone wildcard -> nginx's Cloud Map name (nginx.debuggai-api.local),
    nginx serves the tunnel block with a Let's Encrypt wildcard renewed by DNS-01
    against the new public zone and kept in Secrets Manager.
    CORRECTION to the design doc: that listener must be :443, NOT :8443. The
    private record points browsers straight at nginx, and a browser opening
    https://<id>.tunnel.debugg.ai connects to 443; :8443 would have to appear in
    every tunnel URL and would break "going public needs no code change". 443 also
    happens to need no SG work at all - the copilot mesh SG already allows tcp 443
    from 10.0.0.0/16.
    Cost: we own cert issuance AND renewal (a scheduled job + IAM + an SM secret +
    an entrypoint that materialises the PEMs + an expiry alarm), which is MORE new
    machinery than (A), with a 90-day recurring failure mode. It also puts the data
    plane on Cloud Map DNS: nginx rolls on every sentinal deploy, and a browser that
    cached the old task IP keeps dialling a task that is going away, with no ALB to
    drain it.
    Take this only if the owner rules out touching remote-compose.

(D) A second, terraform-owned nginx ECS service for tunnel ingress - not
    recommended. It avoids the rc change and keeps ACM, but it forks the nginx
    deployment: the tunnel edge would not roll with `rc deploy`, so template changes
    would land on the public edge and not the private one until someone remembered.

== WHICH TESTS GO GREEN FIRST ==
1. nginx template (compose/production/nginx/service.conf.template + Dockerfile env
   defaults) -> the docker harness goes 15 red -> 0 (25/25). Safe to ship alone and
   ahead of everything: the template resolves upstreams at REQUEST time through the
   VPC resolver with a variable proxy_pass, so a tunnel upstream that does not exist
   yet cannot stop nginx from booting - it is a 502 on a hostname nobody can resolve.
2. deploy/prod/rc.yml + docker-compose.ecs.yml + task-secrets.json + the reconcile
   additions -> the static declaration tests go green. Lands WITH the server arc's
   Dockerfile (rc has to have an image to build; cross-arc dependency O3).
3. deploy/prod/tunnel-edge/ terraform: public zone first, then the MANUAL Namecheap
   NS step, then ACM validation, then private zone + internal ALB + TG.
   -> test_public_zone_is_delegated, the zone/ALB/cert/idle_timeout checks go green.
4. rc feature + RC_REF bump + extra_target_groups in rc.yml -> nginx registers in the
   internal TG -> test_internal_alb_has_healthy_nginx_targets and the whole in-VPC
   script go green.
Steps 1-2 are reversible config; step 3 is additive and inert until 4; step 4 is the
only one that changes how an existing service is wired.

== BUILD vs REUSE ==
Reuse: the existing nginx (one more listen port and three locations), the existing
public ALB for the control plane (no new public DNS, no new public cert), the
existing Cloud Map namespace, the existing reconcile script as the out-of-band
task-def writer, and deploy/shared-vpc-nat-route's standalone-module pattern.
Build: the tunnel-edge module, the rc extra_target_groups feature, and three
nginx blocks. Nothing here introduces a new deployment mechanism.

== RISKS AND MITIGATIONS ==
R1 RC_REF bump pulls 17 unrelated commits (multi-container task groups, network_mode,
   "stop dropping rc.yml fields"). deploy.yml's own history says an old-or-new pin
   that misreads rc.yml lets terraform "correct" live infra with CI green.
   -> bump alone, on a quiet deploy, with a `rc plan` read before it (owner-run, it
   takes the prod state lock), and RC_REF revert as the rollback.
R2 Attaching a second target group to the live nginx service triggers an ECS
   deployment of nginx. -> do it in a low-traffic window; it is the same roll every
   deploy already does.
R3 The 8443 containerPort will NOT reach the live nginx task def on its own:
   ignore_changes=[container_definitions] plus a --no-state roll that never
   re-registers means only deploy/prod/reconcile_task_secrets.py can put it there.
   ECS rejects a load_balancer whose container_port is not in the task def, so the
   port mapping must land in an EARLIER deploy than the attachment. Two-phase, in
   this order, or the apply fails.
R4 nginx sizing: 128/256 -> 512/1024 raises the EC2 memory reservation on a fleet
   holding ~24.75 GiB of 30.7 GiB usable. It fits; watch placement on the next roll.
R5 ACM only auto-renews while its DNS validation record stays resolvable - the
   Namecheap delegation is permanent, not a one-off.
R6 The /api/internal/ deny lands on the wildcard *.debugg.ai block too. Verified
   safe: the repo has no /api/internal/ route today (the tokens arc adds the first).

== ROLLBACK ==
Fastest first, each independent:
1. Backend transport flag stays on ngrok - no user is on a debugg tunnel at any point
   in this arc, so infra rollback is never user-visible.
2. Revert the nginx blocks and roll nginx (~2 min). The tunnel stops being routable;
   nothing else moves.
3. Drop extra_target_groups from rc.yml and deploy: nginx detaches from the internal
   TG. Revert RC_REF alongside if the bump is implicated.
4. The tunnel-edge module is `terraform destroy` on its own state - it shares nothing
   with rc's state, which is why it has its own key. Leaving it up costs an idle ALB
   (~$17/mo) and nothing else, so it is the last thing to undo, not the first.

== ENVIRONMENT (O1, open) ==
Staging was decommissioned 2026-09-18. "Staging first" therefore means either
rebuilding that stack or dark-launching in prod: the data plane is private and the
transport flag keeps every client on ngrok, so a prod dark-launch exposes nothing to
users and the 2.2 checks parameterise over either target. Owner picks.

== OWNER DECISION REQUIRED (O2) ==
(A) needs a small PR in qosha1/remote-compose plus an RC_REF bump in
.github/workflows/deploy.yml. If that is out of scope, the fallback is (C) with the
:443 correction, and the arc grows a cert-renewal job. The rest of the plan is
identical either way.
close_reason: Strategy recorded. Recommended: sidecar terraform module (deploy/prod/tunnel-edge, own S3 state key, following deploy/shared-vpc-nat-route) for the zones/cert/internal ALB/TG, PLUS one small rc feature (services.<svc>.extra_target_groups) because rc emits a single load_balancer block per service and does not ignore changes to it - so any out-of-band target-group attachment is silently reverted by the next deploy. Fallback with zero rc changes is the nginx-terminates-TLS option, corrected to listen on :443 rather than :8443 (a browser opening https://<id>.tunnel.debugg.ai has no port to spare). Also recorded: the two-phase order forced by ignore_changes on container_definitions (8443 portMapping must land a deploy BEFORE the TG attachment), the green-order, risks and a four-step rollback. Owner decision O2: is a remote-compose PR + RC_REF bump in scope?

title: [tunnel-infra] 3.2 Architecture & Interface Design
description:
Define module boundaries, interface contracts, data flow and file locations. Follow existing patterns in the target repo; don't invent new ones. Record with `--design`.

Arc specifics:
Record the exact resources and files: rc.yml (prod and staging), terraform, the nginx template, nginx
Dockerfile env defaults, task-secrets.json. Include the SG graph and the manual Namecheap NS step.

Repo: platform/sentinal. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §4. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.4.
design:
ARCHITECTURE & INTERFACES - tunnel infra. Everything below is the RECOMMENDED
option (A) from 3.1; the (C) delta is at the end. No file is committed yet.

== DATA FLOW ==
control plane (unchanged public edge)
  MCP client ──wss://api.debugg.ai/tunnel/v1/connect──▶ public ALB debuggai-api-alb
    (:443, cert 07293c8c, rule prio 100 Host=api.debugg.ai) ──▶ nginx:80
    ──location /tunnel/──▶ tunnel.debuggai-api.local:8080

data plane (new, private)
  browser-session task (VPC resolver) ──▶ Route53 PRIVATE zone tunnel.debugg.ai
    *.tunnel.debugg.ai ALIAS ──▶ internal ALB :443 (ACM *.tunnel.debugg.ai,
    idle_timeout 3600) ──▶ TG ip:8443 ──▶ nginx:8443 (tunnel server block)
    ──▶ tunnel.debuggai-api.local:8081

verify (service-to-service, never public)
  tunnel task ──▶ django.debuggai-api.local:8001 /api/internal/tunnels/verify/
  nginx returns 404 for /api/internal/ on every public server block.

== FILES ==
sentinal (repo debugg-ai/debuggai-api), branch tunnel/infra:
 M compose/production/nginx/service.conf.template   the three blocks below
 M compose/production/nginx/Dockerfile              ENV defaults for the new vars
 M deploy/prod/rc.yml                               tunnel service, nginx env +
                                                    size + extra_target_groups
 M docker-compose.ecs.yml                           tunnel service (8080/8081),
                                                    nginx port 8443
 M deploy/prod/task-secrets.json                    tunnel target, secrets:false,
                                                    stop_timeout 120
 M deploy/prod/reconcile_task_secrets.py            ensure_port_mappings +
                                                    ensure_stop_timeout
 M .github/workflows/deploy.yml                     RC_REF bump (option A only)
 A deploy/prod/tunnel-edge/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,versions.tf}
 A compose/production/nginx/tests/*                 harness (already written, 2.1)
 A backend/backend/core/tests/test_deploy_tunnel_infra.py   (already written, 2.1)
 A deploy/tests/{test_tunnel_infra_live.py,tunnel_invpc_check.py}  (2.2)
remote-compose (repo qosha1/remote-compose), option A only:
 M remote_compose/config/_schema_types.py, _schema_parser.py, provider/base.py,
   provider/ecs/provider.py, provider/ecs/templates/services.tf.j2 (+ tests)

== NGINX (validated: this exact shape takes the harness to 25/25) ==
New env vars, with Dockerfile defaults next to the existing ones:
  NGINX_TUNNEL_CONTROL_UPSTREAM=tunnel.debuggai-api.local:8080
  NGINX_TUNNEL_INGRESS_UPSTREAM=tunnel.debuggai-api.local:8081
  NGINX_TUNNEL_DOMAIN_RE=tunnel\.debugg\.ai
  NGINX_TUNNEL_PORT=8443
(NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^NGINX_ already covers them.)

1. In the api.debugg.ai server block, ABOVE the rate-limited location:
     location /api/internal/ { return 404; }
     location /tunnel/ {
         set $upstream_tunnel http://${NGINX_TUNNEL_CONTROL_UPSTREAM};
         proxy_pass $upstream_tunnel;
         proxy_http_version 1.1;
         proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
         proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;
         proxy_set_header Host $host;
         proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
         proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
         proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
         proxy_redirect off;
         proxy_buffering off;
         proxy_request_buffering off;
         proxy_connect_timeout 60s; proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
         proxy_read_timeout 3600s;  send_timeout 3600s;
     }
2. `location /api/internal/ { return 404; }` also in the <port>.vnc.debugg.ai block
   and the wildcard *.debugg.ai block (the default_server already 404s).
3. A :80 refusal block for tunnel hostnames, placed BEFORE the wildcard
   *.debugg.ai block - nginx takes the FIRST matching regex server_name in file
   order, so after it the wildcard would win and proxy a spoofed tunnel Host into
   django:
     server {
         listen 80; listen [::]:80;
         server_name "~^.+\.${NGINX_TUNNEL_DOMAIN_RE}$";
         location / { return 404; }
     }
4. The dedicated port, as two blocks (default_server first):
     server {                       # ALB health checks arrive with Host = target IP
         listen ${NGINX_TUNNEL_PORT} default_server;
         location /_deephealthcheck { return 200 'Health check success'; }
         location / { return 404; }
     }
     server {
         listen ${NGINX_TUNNEL_PORT};
         server_name "~^(?<tunnel_id>[a-z0-9-]+)\.${NGINX_TUNNEL_DOMAIN_RE}$";
         client_max_body_size 512M;
         location /api/internal/ { return 404; }
         location / {
             set $upstream_tunnel_ingress http://${NGINX_TUNNEL_INGRESS_UPSTREAM};
             proxy_pass $upstream_tunnel_ingress;
             proxy_http_version 1.1;
             proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
             proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;
             proxy_set_header Host $host;          # verbatim, the client needs it
             proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
             proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
             proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto https;   # TLS ended at the ALB
             proxy_redirect off;
             proxy_buffering off;
             proxy_request_buffering off;
             proxy_connect_timeout 60s; proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
             proxy_read_timeout 3600s;  send_timeout 3600s;
         }
     }
   No `upstream`/keepalive block anywhere: with `Connection $connection_upgrade`
   nginx closes the upstream connection after each non-upgrade request, so one
   upstream connection can never carry two tunnels' requests.

== rc.yml (deploy/prod/rc.yml) ==
  services.tunnel:
    cpu: 512, memory: 1024, type: application, replicas: 1, port: 8080
    (NO `public: true` - public would put it on the INTERNET-facing ALB)
    health_check: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/healthz || exit 1"]
      interval 30, timeout 5, retries 3, start_period 30
    env: TUNNEL_DOMAIN=tunnel.debugg.ai, CONTROL_PORT=8080, INGRESS_PORT=8081,
         CLOUD_MAP_NAME=tunnel.debuggai-api.local,
         VERIFY_URL=http://django.debuggai-api.local:8001/api/internal/tunnels/verify/,
         REDIS_URL=redis://redis.debuggai-api.local:6379/0, LOG_LEVEL=info
    env_from_secret: [{arn: arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-2:033937118837:secret:
         debuggai-api-prod/creds-Sv64xe, keys: [TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN]}]
    SGs/subnets: stack defaults (debuggai-api-tasks + the copilot mesh SG, private
      subnets). A per-service declared SG REPLACES those and would lose the route to
      django:8001, whose SG rules rc owns inline - so least-privilege SGs for this
      service are a follow-up that needs an rc change of its own.
    IAM: the shared ${project}-task role, which carries only execute-command perms.
  services.nginx: cpu 128->512, memory 256->1024; env gains the four NGINX_TUNNEL_*
    vars; extra_target_groups: [{arn: <tunnel-edge output>, container_port: 8443}]
  compose.exclude stays [mcp] - `tunnel` must NOT be excluded.

== docker-compose.ecs.yml ==
  services.tunnel: build context = the server arc's directory in THIS repo
    (O3 - agree the path with the server agent; if the code lands outside sentinal,
    use rc.yml `image:` instead and drop the build block),
    ports ["8080:8080", "8081:8081"]  -> rc: primary 8080 + extra_ports [8081]
  services.nginx.ports gains "8443:8443"  -> the containerPort the TG needs.

== deploy/prod/task-secrets.json + reconcile_task_secrets.py ==
  task_targets gains {family: debuggai-api-tunnel, service: tunnel,
                      secrets: false, stop_timeout: 120}
  `secrets: false` is deliberate: required_secrets is a GLOBAL list and the tunnel
  server, which terminates untrusted traffic, must not hold the 39-key prod bundle.
  reconcile gains two writers, in its existing additive/idempotent style:
    ensure_stop_timeout(td, target)  - rc has no stopTimeout field and ECS defaults
      to 30s, which is shorter than the GOAWAY drain.
    ensure_port_mappings(td, service, compose ports) - REQUIRED, not cosmetic: the
      task def carries ignore_changes=[container_definitions] and `rc deploy
      --no-state` never re-registers, so nginx's new 8443 containerPort can reach
      the live task def no other way, and ECS rejects a load_balancer whose
      container_port is missing. It must run at least one deploy BEFORE the
      target-group attachment.

== deploy/prod/tunnel-edge/ (terraform, own state) ==
  backend "s3": bucket 033937118837-rc-tfstate, key tunnel-edge/terraform.tfstate,
    region us-west-2, dynamodb_table rc-tfstate-locks  (rc's key is
    debuggai-api/prod/ecs.tfstate - never share it)
  provider aws region us-east-2
  aws_route53_zone.public   name tunnel.debugg.ai            # ACM validation only
  aws_route53_zone.private  name tunnel.debugg.ai, vpc { vpc_id =
                            vpc-0b6967a360d78cb81 }
  aws_acm_certificate.tunnel  domain *.tunnel.debugg.ai, SAN tunnel.debugg.ai,
                            validation_method DNS
  aws_route53_record.cert_validation (in .public) + aws_acm_certificate_validation
  aws_security_group.tunnel_ilb  ingress tcp 443 from 10.0.0.0/16;
                            egress tcp 8443 to sg-03b40268ea407f0eb
  aws_lb.tunnel_ilb  internal = true, type application,
                     subnets [subnet-0dfebb33a246ac146, subnet-067020c2c7d62a47c],
                     security_groups [aws_security_group.tunnel_ilb.id,
                                      "sg-03b40268ea407f0eb"],
                     idle_timeout 3600
  aws_lb_target_group.nginx_tunnel  port 8443, protocol HTTP, target_type ip,
                     vpc_id vpc-0b6967a360d78cb81,
                     health_check { path "/_deephealthcheck", matcher "200-499" },
                     deregistration_delay 60
  aws_lb_listener.https  port 443, protocol HTTPS, ssl_policy
                     ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06, cert = the validated ACM
                     arn, default_action forward -> that TG
  aws_route53_record.wildcard  in .private, name "*.tunnel.debugg.ai", type A,
                     alias -> the internal ALB
  outputs: target_group_arn (pasted into rc.yml), alb_dns_name, zone ids
  A header comment carries the MANUAL Namecheap step (the tests assert it is there).

== SECURITY-GROUP GRAPH ==
  browser-session task [sg-002f64af52589285b, sg-0c6dc0de46021134a, egress all]
      │ tcp 443
      ▼
  internal ALB [sg-tunnel-ilb: in 443 from 10.0.0.0/16] + member of
                sg-03b40268ea407f0eb (debuggai-api-tasks)
      │ tcp 8443     ← admitted by the tasks SG's existing all-ports `self` rule,
      ▼                which is why the ALB joins that group: rc renders the tasks
  nginx task [sg-012e574ae98dc3bd9 mesh, sg-03b40268ea407f0eb tasks]   SG with
      │ tcp 8081                                    INLINE ingress blocks, so an
      ▼                                             externally added rule would be
  tunnel task [same two SGs]                        deleted on the next apply.
      │ tcp 8001 (verify) / 6379 (revoke)           The alternative - a rule on the
      ▼                                             copilot mesh SG - is CFN-managed
  django / redis [same two SGs]                     legacy and drifts. Membership
                                                    touches nobody's rules.
  Public ALB [sg-02de18ff6142a25c1: 80/443 from 0.0.0.0/0] -> nginx:80 ONLY
  (its target groups are :80, :5555, :3000 - nothing on 8443).
  NOT expressible, and not the control: "nginx accepts 8443 only from the ILB SG".
  nginx sits on the shared tasks + mesh SGs. The privacy boundary is: no
  internet-facing listener or TG points at 8443; nginx has no public IP and sits in
  private subnets; the tunnel block is bound to 8443 only; the hostnames resolve in
  the private zone only.

== MANUAL STEP THE OWNER MUST DO (once, at Namecheap) ==
After `terraform apply` creates the PUBLIC zone, read its four NS records
(`aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <public zone id>`) and at Namecheap, on the
debugg.ai domain's Advanced DNS page, add four NS records:
    Type NS   Host "tunnel"   Value ns-XXXX.awsdns-XX.org.   TTL 30 min
    ... one row per nameserver (4 rows total)
Do NOT touch the debugg.ai apex NS - the rest of the domain stays at Namecheap.
Verify with `dig NS tunnel.debugg.ai @1.1.1.1` (expect the four AWS names), after
which ACM validates on its own within minutes. Nothing downstream - cert, listener,
private records - works until this is done, and ACM RENEWAL depends on it staying
in place. Optional cleanup spotted on the way: api.st.debugg.ai still CNAMEs to the
deleted debuggai-api-staging ALB (NXDOMAIN).

== DEPLOY ORDER ==
1. nginx template + Dockerfile defaults + rc.yml nginx env/size  -> deploy (harness
   green; the tunnel upstream simply does not resolve yet).
2. reconcile ensure_port_mappings + the 8443 compose port -> deploy (the live nginx
   task def gains containerPort 8443).
3. terraform apply in deploy/prod/tunnel-edge -> public zone -> MANUAL Namecheap NS
   -> ACM validates -> private zone, ILB, TG, listener.
4. rc.yml tunnel service + task-secrets + the server arc's image -> deploy.
5. RC_REF bump + extra_target_groups -> deploy. nginx registers in the internal TG;
   run deploy/tests/test_tunnel_infra_live.py and, from a task,
   `rc run django -- python deploy/tests/tunnel_invpc_check.py`.

== GOING PUBLIC LATER (no code change) ==
Add *.tunnel.debugg.ai to the PUBLIC zone aliased at the public ALB, attach the same
ACM cert to the public :443 listener as an SNI certificate, and let the tunnel server
block also listen on :80 (delete the :80 refusal block). No new target group, no new
service, no client change.

== IF THE OWNER PICKS FALLBACK (C) INSTEAD ==
Drop from the module: the ILB, its SG, TG and listener; keep both zones. The private
wildcard becomes a CNAME to nginx.debuggai-api.local. nginx listens `443 ssl` (NOT
8443 - the URL has no port to spare) with a Let's Encrypt wildcard from DNS-01 on the
public zone, stored in the SM bundle and written to disk by a new
/docker-entrypoint.d/15-tunnel-cert.sh. Add a scheduled renewal workflow (lego or
certbot with the route53 plugin, OIDC role scoped to the tunnel zone), an expiry
alarm, and a per-target secret-key subset in reconcile (the bundle's cert keys for
nginx only). No rc change, no RC_REF bump, and the mesh SG already allows tcp 443
from 10.0.0.0/16, so the SG graph above collapses to browser-session -> nginx:443.
Set NGINX_TUNNEL_PORT=443 and the same harness covers it unchanged.
close_reason: Architecture recorded: exact file list (nginx template + Dockerfile, rc.yml, docker-compose.ecs.yml, task-secrets.json, reconcile_task_secrets.py, deploy/prod/tunnel-edge/*.tf, deploy.yml RC_REF), the four nginx blocks in the shape proven green against the harness, the tunnel service block, the terraform resource list with its own S3 state key, the SG graph (internal ALB joins debuggai-api-tasks for membership rather than editing an rc-inline or CFN-managed SG), the manual Namecheap NS delegation step, the 5-step deploy order, the going-public delta and the fallback-(C) delta.

title: [tunnel-infra] 4.1 Core Implementation
description:
Write the minimum code to make the failing unit tests pass. Run the suite after each meaningful change. No extra features, refactors or 'improvements' beyond what the tests cover. Notes: X/Y unit tests passing.

Arc specifics:
Make the nginx template changes until the harness is green. Add the rc service definitions.

Repo: platform/sentinal. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §4. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.4.
notes:
CODE AND CONFIG ONLY. Nothing applied, deployed, committed or pushed. No AWS
mutation: the only AWS calls made were describe/list (the live checks) and
`terraform init -backend=false` + `validate`, which touch neither state nor the
lock table.

== WHAT LANDED (sentinal worktree, branch tunnel/infra, uncommitted) ==
M compose/production/nginx/service.conf.template
    * api.debugg.ai block: `location /api/internal/ { return 404; }` and
      `location /tunnel/` (the /ws/ shape + unbuffered both ways + 3600s, to
      NGINX_TUNNEL_CONTROL_UPSTREAM).
    * the /api/internal/ deny also on the <port>.vnc.debugg.ai block and the
      *.debugg.ai wildcard block (the default_server already 404s).
    * a :80 refusal block for tunnel hostnames, placed BEFORE the wildcard
      block - nginx takes the FIRST matching regex server_name in file order,
      so after it the wildcard swallows <id>.tunnel.debugg.ai into django. The
      server arc flagged this; the harness proves it.
    * the tunnel data plane on NGINX_TUNNEL_PORT: a `default_server` sibling
      answering /_deephealthcheck (an ALB health check arrives with Host = the
      target IP) plus the ingress block itself - Host verbatim, upgrade
      headers, X-Forwarded-Proto https, unbuffered both ways, 512M bodies,
      3600s, and no upstream{} block anywhere so no keepalive pool can let two
      tunnels share one upstream connection.
    * header rewritten: it claimed staging/prod resolvers of 10.60/10.61 that
      were never this stack's (live nginx has always carried 10.0.0.2), and
      staging no longer exists.
M compose/production/nginx/Dockerfile
    NGINX_TUNNEL_CONTROL_UPSTREAM / _INGRESS_UPSTREAM / _DOMAIN_RE / _PORT
    defaults + EXPOSE 8443; NGINX_RESOLVER default corrected to 10.0.0.2.
    VERIFIED by hand, because no test covers the defaults path: built the image
    and ran it with NO tunnel env at all - `nginx -t` passes and the rendered
    config reads `server_name "~^(?<tunnel_id>[a-z0-9-]+)\.tunnel\.debugg\.ai$"`
    with single backslashes (the Dockerfile's `\\.` collapses correctly; a
    collapse to a bare `.` would still MATCH and would have gone unnoticed).
M deploy/prod/rc.yml
    * new private `tunnel` service: 512/1024, replicas 1, port 8080 (8081 comes
      from compose), Cloud Map tunnel.debuggai-api.local, env per the server
      arc's config.ts contract (CLOUD_MAP_NAME, CONTROL_PORT, INGRESS_PORT,
      TUNNEL_DOMAIN, VERIFY_URL -> django's Cloud Map address, REDIS_URL,
      LOG_LEVEL), env_from_secret naming ONLY TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN.
      health_check is a node one-liner, not curl: tunnel-server/Dockerfile is
      node:22-slim and has no curl (server arc, xkoh.3.6).
    * nginx: 128/256 -> 512/1024, the four NGINX_TUNNEL_* vars, and the
      extra_target_groups attachment COMMENTED OUT with its two preconditions.
M docker-compose.ecs.yml  tunnel service (context ./tunnel-server, 8080+8081);
    nginx gains "8443:8443".
M deploy/prod/task-secrets.json  tunnel family target with
    `"secrets": ["TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN"]` and `"stop_timeout": 120`.
M deploy/prod/reconcile_task_secrets.py  three additions, in its existing
    additive/idempotent style:
    * resolve_secret_names(): `secrets` may now be true / false / a LIST. This
      is the security fix - required_secrets is GLOBAL, so a naive `true` for
      the tunnel family would wire all 42 prod keys (MAIN_DB_PASSWORD,
      AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY...) onto a process that
      terminates untrusted traffic from the internet.
    * load_port_mappings() + ensure_port_mappings(): nginx's 8443 containerPort
      can reach the live task def NO other way (ignore_changes=
      [container_definitions] + a --no-state roll that never re-registers), and
      ECS rejects a load_balancer whose container_port is absent.
    * ensure_stop_timeout(): rc has no such field and ECS defaults to 30s,
      shorter than the tunnel server's GOAWAY-and-drain.
A deploy/prod/tunnel-edge/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,versions.tf,.gitignore}
    Own S3 state key (tunnel-edge/prod/terraform.tfstate), never rc's. Public
    zone (ACM validation) + private zone associated with the VPC + wildcard
    alias, ACM *.tunnel.debugg.ai with DNS validation, ALB SG, internal ALB
    (idle_timeout 3600, both private subnets), ip target group on 8443 with the
    /_deephealthcheck check and a 60s deregistration delay, HTTPS:443 listener.
    Every value is a variable defaulting to prod. The manual Namecheap NS
    delegation is written into the header, next to the zone that depends on it.
    `terraform init -backend=false && terraform validate` -> valid;
    `terraform fmt -check` clean.
A backend/backend/core/tests/test_deploy_tunnel_infra.py  (2.1) extended with
    the secrets-subset unit test the coordinator asked for, a ports/stop-timeout
    unit test, and a cross-arc merge gate (below).
M deploy/tests/test_tunnel_infra_live.py  two checks for the health-probe path:
    the tunnel service registers in Cloud Map, and its own SGs + the ALB's
    ingress actually permit tunnel task -> internal ALB on 443 (the probe
    fetches https://<id>.tunnel.debugg.ai for real, so this is not implied by
    the browser-session story).

== rc FEATURE (local clone, NOT pushed) ==
/private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/remote-compose, branch

6 files, +101 lines: services.<svc>.extra_target_groups: [{arn, container_port}]
-> extra `load_balancer {}` blocks on the ECS service. General, not

== ORDERED APPLY SEQUENCE FOR THE OWNER ==
0. Land tunnel/infra and tunnel/server TOGETHER (or add `tunnel` to
   compose.exclude until the server lands). The merge-gate test says which.
1. Deploy. This deploy does two things and no more: nginx gets the tunnel
   blocks and containerPort 8443 (reconcile), and the tunnel service is
   created. The tunnel hostname resolves nowhere, so nothing routes yet.
2. `terraform apply` in deploy/prod/tunnel-edge (owner, first AWS mutation).
3. Add the four NS rows at Namecheap on host "tunnel" from
   `terraform output -json public_zone_name_servers`. ACM then validates.
4. `terraform output target_group_arn`.
5. Uncomment extra_target_groups in deploy/prod/rc.yml with that ARN AND bump
   RC_REF in .github/workflows/deploy.yml in the SAME commit. An old RC_REF
   ignores the key: green deploy, no attachment, no traffic.
6. Deploy. Then run deploy/tests/test_tunnel_infra_live.py and, from a task,
   `rc run django -- python deploy/tests/tunnel_invpc_check.py`.

title: [tunnel-infra] 1.1 User Requirements

    timeouts, pointing at NGINX_TUNNEL_CONTROL_UPSTREAM.

    `~^(?<tunnel_id>[a-z0-9-]+)\.tunnel\.debugg\.ai$`, upgrade headers, proxy_buffering off,
    proxy_request_buffering off, 3600 s timeouts, Host preserved, a large client_max_body_size and NO upstream

  nginx's second port and target group for the internal ALB, and raise nginx above 128 CPU / 256 MB.
- If rc can't express the internal ALB or the second port: run terraform alongside rc, or use the fallback
  (the private zone points at nginx's Cloud Map name, and nginx terminates TLS on :8443 with a Let's Encrypt
  wildcard renewed via DNS-01 on the new zone and kept in Secrets Manager). Plain HTTP is NOT acceptable:

- A new tunnel service with two ports + Cloud Map: EXPRESSIBLE. rc.yml `port: 8080` +
  compose ports 8080/8081 -> both portMappings; service_discovery.tf.j2 registers every
  service as an A record (tunnel.debuggai-api.local, ttl 10, MULTIVALUE) regardless of
  public/private; container health_check, replicas, env, iam_role, env_from_secret
  (rc-7yo) and per-service security_groups/subnets are all supported.
- stopTimeout: NOT expressible (no such field anywhere in rc). ECS default is 30s.
- Task-def drift rule that constrains everything above: rc.yml sets
  ignore_task_definition_changes: true, so the task-def resource carries
  ignore_changes=[container_definitions] and the service ignore_changes=[task_definition];
  and `rc deploy --no-state` only force-rolls, it never re-registers. Therefore, for an
  EXISTING service (nginx), changes to env land only through
  deploy/prod/reconcile_task_secrets.py (which today applies secrets, healthCheck, task
  size and env - NOT portMappings and NOT stopTimeout). A NEW service (tunnel) gets its
  full shape from terraform at creation, so its ports/health/stopTimeout only need to be
  right once - but stopTimeout still needs a writer.
=> Options: (a) rc feature = a small remote-compose change adding extra target-group
   attachments to a service; (b) terraform alongside rc for the zones/cert/ALB/TG/SG,
   which still needs (a) for the attachment; (c) the design's fallback, nginx terminates
   TLS itself. Decision + rationale go in 3.1 (bead .5).

== NGINX REQUIREMENTS (compose/production/nginx/service.conf.template + Dockerfile) ==
- `location /tunnel/` in the api.debugg.ai server block: a copy of /ws/ plus
  proxy_buffering off + proxy_request_buffering off, 3600s read/send timeouts, upgrade
  headers, Host $host, upstream $NGINX_TUNNEL_CONTROL_UPSTREAM (tunnel...local:8080).
- `location /api/internal/ { return 404; }` in EVERY public server block.
  [FIX] that means the api block AND the wildcard *.debugg.ai block (both proxy
  `location /` to django today); the VNC block proxies to a browser port rather than
  django, and the default_server block already 404s everything but /_deephealthcheck -
  but adding it to all four is cheap and is what the test asserts.
- A tunnel server block that listens ONLY on the dedicated port:
  server_name ~^(?<tunnel_id>[a-z0-9-]+)\.${NGINX_TUNNEL_DOMAIN_RE}$, upgrade headers,
  proxy_buffering off, proxy_request_buffering off, 3600s timeouts, Host $host preserved,
  large client_max_body_size, NO upstream keepalive, upstream
  $NGINX_TUNNEL_INGRESS_UPSTREAM (tunnel...local:8081). Plus a
  `listen <port> default_server` sibling on the same port serving /_deephealthcheck (200)
  and 404 for everything else, so an ALB health check (which sends Host = target IP)
  has something to hit and an unmatched Host cannot fall into the tunnel block.
- [FIX] the dedicated port depends on the option chosen in 3.1:
  * internal-ALB options (a)/(b): nginx :8443 plain HTTP, TLS terminated by the ALB.
  * fallback (c): nginx must listen on :443 with TLS, NOT :8443 - a browser opening
    https://<id>.tunnel.debugg.ai connects to port 443, and the private zone points
    straight at nginx with no ALB to move the port. (Using 8443 there would force
    :8443 into every tunnel URL and break "going public needs no code change".)
- New envs NGINX_TUNNEL_CONTROL_UPSTREAM / NGINX_TUNNEL_INGRESS_UPSTREAM /
  NGINX_TUNNEL_DOMAIN_RE get Dockerfile defaults (existing ENV + NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^NGINX_
  pattern) and explicit values in rc.yml's nginx env.
- nginx sizing: currently 128 cpu / 256 MB (live: memory 256, no task cpu on EC2). Tunnel
  bytes cross nginx twice, so raise it (proposed 512 cpu / 1024 MB) and watch it. On EC2
  memory is the placement reservation; ec2_capacity is min/desired/max 2 m5.xlarge with
  ~24.75 GiB already reserved of 30.7 GiB usable, so +768 MiB fits but is not free.

== SECURITY-BOUNDARY REQUIREMENT [FIX] ==
"nginx allows <tunnel port> only from the internal ALB's SG" is NOT achievable and is not
the real control: nginx carries the shared debuggai-api-tasks SG (ALL ports from the
public ALB SG and from itself) and the copilot mesh SG (ALL ports from mesh members,
from the browser-mgr env SG and from the browser-sessions SG, plus 443 from 10.0.0.0/16).
Per-service SGs in rc REPLACE the shared ones, which would cut nginx off from the public
ALB. The enforceable, testable boundary is:
  1. no internet-facing listener or target group points at the tunnel port (the public
     ALB has TGs on :80, :5555 and :3000 only, and forwards only to its TGs);
  2. nginx tasks have no public IP and sit in private subnets;
  3. the tunnel server block is bound to the dedicated port ONLY, never :80;
  4. the tunnel hostnames resolve only inside the VPC (private zone, no public record).
Internal-ALB SG requirement: a dedicated SG allowing tcp 443 in from 10.0.0.0/16
(the VPC CIDR - confirmed), egress to the nginx tasks; and, because rc's inline-rule
tasks SG cannot take an externally-added rule, the ALB also joins an SG the nginx task
already trusts (debuggai-api-tasks sg-03b40268ea407f0eb has an all-ports `self` rule),
which is membership only - no rule edit on an rc- or CFN-managed SG.

== TUNNEL SERVICE (rc.yml) REQUIREMENTS ==
- New service `tunnel` in deploy/prod/rc.yml + docker-compose.ecs.yml (ports 8080, 8081;
  build context = the server arc's directory INSIDE the sentinal repo - cross-arc
  dependency, see O3). Not in compose.exclude (currently [mcp]).
- type: application (private - no `public: true`, so no ALB target), replicas 1,
  health_check (container-level) hitting /healthz on the control port, Cloud Map name
  tunnel.debuggai-api.local, env TUNNEL_DOMAIN / VERIFY_URL / REDIS_URL / CONTROL_PORT /
  INGRESS_PORT / CLOUD_MAP_NAME, secret TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN.
- TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN must NOT come from task-secrets.json `required_secrets`: that list
  is global and is wired onto every target that is not `"secrets": false`, so adding it
  there would also put it on django and all the celery families. Use rc's per-service
  env_from_secret ({arn: bundle arn, keys: [TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN]}), which lands at
  creation - and add the tunnel family to task-secrets.json with `"secrets": false` so the
  reconcile still applies env/health/size but never the 39-key bundle.
- stopTimeout 120 has no rc field: it needs a small addition to
  deploy/prod/reconcile_task_secrets.py (the repo's existing out-of-band task-def writer).
- Least privilege: the tunnel task keeps the shared ${project}-task role, which only
  carries execute-command permissions (verified in the rendered iam.tf) - no AWS data
  access. Its SGs stay the stack defaults (tasks + mesh) because a declared per-service SG
  could not reach django:8001 for the verify call (django sits on the shared tasks SG,
  whose inline rules rc owns). Noted as a follow-up, not a v1 blocker.

== OPEN QUESTIONS ==
O1 (from 1.1): staging is gone - rebuild it, or dark-launch in prod behind the flag?
O2: the internal-ALB path needs a small feature in qosha1/remote-compose (extra target
    group on a service) plus an RC_REF bump. Is an rc change in scope, or do we take the
    nginx-terminates-TLS fallback that needs no rc change? (Decision recorded in 3.1.)
O3: where exactly does the tunnel server's Dockerfile/build context land in the sentinal
    repo? The rc service block must name it; `image:` is the alternative if the code ends
    up outside this repo.
close_reason: System requirements confirmed and corrected against live AWS + rc source. Key finding: rc cannot express an internal ALB, any Route53 zone, or a SECOND target group on a service (one load_balancer block, ignore_changes covers only task_definition), so an out-of-band TG attachment is reverted by every deploy; it CAN express the new two-port Cloud Map service and a second nginx container port. Also corrected: the fallback needs nginx on :443, not :8443; 'nginx allows the tunnel port only from the ALB SG' is not achievable (shared tasks + mesh SGs) so the boundary is stated as no internet listener/TG + no public IP + port-bound server block + private-only DNS. browser-mgr verified read-only as needing no change.
