Repo: platform. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.3.
design:
ARCHITECTURE & INTERFACE DESIGN — debugg tunnel server

== A. WHERE IT LIVES ==
debuggai-api (sentinal) repo, top-level tunnel-server/. NOT the platform repo: .github/workflows/
deploy.yml checks out only this repo and rc builds from docker-compose.ecs.yml contexts inside it,
and full-platform-deploy gitignores /sentinal/. Evidence is on bead debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.3.2.
Build context is ./tunnel-server, the nginx/redis/mcp own-directory pattern, so the image carries
nothing of the Django tree. tunnel-server/.dockerignore is required (the root one does not apply
to a non-root context).

  tunnel-server/
    package.json  tsconfig.json  jest.config.js  jest.integration.config.js
    .dockerignore  .gitignore   Dockerfile (4.1)
    src/
      index.ts            process entry: loadConfig -> startTunnelServer -> signal handlers
      server.ts           startTunnelServer(config, overrides) -> RunningTunnelServer
      config.ts           env -> TunnelServerConfig; every limit and timeout, no magic numbers
      types.ts            the PORTS: TunnelSession, TunnelStream, RegisteredTunnel, Config, Clock
      protocol/           the vendored wire protocol + index.ts, the ONE import seam (§D)
      hostRouting.ts      parseRequestHead, routeHost              (pure)
      handshake.ts        evaluateHandshake                        (pure)
      errorPages.ts       renderErrorPage/Response/PlainResponse   (pure)
      verifyClient.ts     the debugg API's internal verify + closed
      tunnelRegistry.ts   in-process ownership, replacement, tombstones, the grace wait
      connectAuthorizer.ts  shape -> capacity -> verify, fail closed
      controlServer.ts    :8080 — upgrade, /healthz, /internal/v1/*
      ingressServer.ts    :8081 — raw TCP, head, route, pipe
      ownership.ts        sibling discovery, PeerClient, OwnershipResolver
      sessionSupervisor.ts  re-verify and maxExpiresAt
      revokeSubscriber.ts   Redis tunnel.revoked -> onRevoke
      probe.ts            PROBE -> a real GET back through the tunnel
      protocolSession.ts  (4.1) adapter: protocol TunnelSession -> this service's port
      metrics.ts  logger.ts
    __tests__/            178 unit tests + helpers/fakes.ts
    __integration__/      29 integration tests + helpers/harness.ts

== B. MODULE BOUNDARIES — THE PORTS ARE THE DESIGN ==
Everything outside the process is an interface in src/types.ts or the module that owns it, which
is why 178 unit tests run with no network, no Redis and no websocket:
  TunnelSession / TunnelStream   the protocol (types.ts)
  VerifyClient                   the debugg API (verifyClient.ts)
  RevokeTransport                Redis pub/sub (revokeSubscriber.ts)
  SiblingDiscovery / PeerClient  DNS and sibling tasks (ownership.ts)
  Clock                          time
Direction of dependency, strictly one way:
  index -> server -> {controlServer, ingressServer, sessionSupervisor, revokeSubscriber, lifecycle}
  controlServer -> {connectAuthorizer -> {handshake, verifyClient, tunnelRegistry}, protocolSession, ingressServer(forwards)}
  ingressServer -> {hostRouting, tunnelRegistry, ownership, errorPages}
  probe -> protocol types only
  nothing imports controlServer or ingressServer except server and lifecycle.
Key contracts (frozen by the red tests, so 4.1 may not renegotiate them):
  parseRequestHead(buffer, maxHeadBytes) -> {ok, head{raw,method,target,httpVersion,host}, rest}
                                          | {ok:false, failure: incomplete|malformed|too_large|
                                            missing_host|duplicate_host|not_http1}
  routeHost(host, tunnelDomain)          -> {kind:'tunnel', tunnelId} | {kind:'unknown'}
  evaluateHandshake(request, supported)  -> 101 | 426 | 400 | 401, in that check order
  VerifyClient.verify(id, key, event)    -> accepted | rejected(reason) | unavailable
  TunnelRegistry.register/get/remove/tombstone/isTombstoned/waitFor(id, graceMs)
  OwnershipResolver.resolve(id)          -> {local} | {peer, address, connectedAt} | {none}
  renderErrorPage(marker)                -> status from MARKER_HTTP_STATUS, marker in the header
                                            AND in the first 4096 body bytes
  createLifecycle(...).shutdown(signal)  -> stop accepting, GOAWAY, drain, close

== C. DATA FLOW ==
  browser -> internal ALB :443 -> nginx :8443 -> ingress :8081
    read the head (Host only) -> routeHost -> registry.get
      local:     session.openStream({kind:'http'}) -> socket.pipe(stream).pipe(socket)
      not local: ownership.resolve -> peerClient.forward(owner) -> the owner serves it locally
      nobody:    registry.waitFor(id, 5000) -> then renderErrorPage(OFFLINE)
      tombstoned: renderErrorPage(UNKNOWN) immediately, no wait
  MCP -> public ALB -> nginx location /tunnel/ -> control :8080 /tunnel/v1/connect
    evaluateHandshake -> capacity -> verify -> 101 -> protocolSession -> registry.register
  Redis tunnel.revoked -> registry.tombstone + GOAWAY(REVOKED) + close 4007
  every 5 min -> verify(event:'reverify'); unavailable KEEPS the tunnel; maxExpiresAt is local
  SIGTERM -> lifecycle: stop accepting (nginx's proxy_next_upstream moves on) -> GOAWAY -> drain
             <= 25 s (ECS stopTimeout is 30 s and rc has no knob) -> close
The bytes are never parsed after the head: Host, websocket upgrades, SSE and chunked bodies all
survive because the stream carries bytes and nothing else.

== D. HOW THE PROTOCOL MODULE IS CONSUMED (per xkoh.1.6: VENDORED, not an npm subpath) ==
• src/protocol/index.ts is the single seam; nothing else in the service imports ./vendor/*.
• Vendored today: constants.ts, errors.ts, codec.ts, byte-identical to the upstream worktree
  (verified by diff on 2026-09-19). src/protocol/vendor.json records the upstream repo, the ref
  and a sha256 per file. The ref is UNPINNED because the upstream files are still uncommitted
  phase-2.1 stubs; 4.1 pins it to a tag.
• 4.1 completes the mechanism 1.6 specifies:
  - vendor the WHOLE directory, vectors included (handshake.ts, transport.ts, stream.ts,
    session.ts, index.ts, vectors/*.json);
  - npm run sync:protocol — re-fetch the pinned ref, rewrite src/protocol/vendor/, refresh
    vendor.json;
  - npm run verify:protocol — (a) re-sync into a temp dir and fail on any difference, so the copy
    can never be hand-edited, and (b) run the vectors through the vendored codec and handshake.
  1.6 calls these CI gates. Sentinal's CI is disabled on purpose (CLAUDE.md: "CI is OFF — YOU are
  the gate"), so verify:protocol is a pre-merge command in the landing checklist, not a workflow.
  If the repo ever re-enables CI, it is one job.
• The server uses: validateHandshakeRequest (behind our evaluateHandshake), webSocketTransport,
  new TunnelSession(transport, {role:'server', onProbe}), openStream per inbound connection,
  goAway on SIGTERM, MARKER_HTTP_STATUS for the error pages, and the ws constants
  (perMessageDeflate false, maxPayload MAX_FRAME_SIZE).
• ADAPTER, and why it stays: src/protocolSession.ts maps the protocol's class onto this service's
  port. openStream is synchronous there and throws StreamResetError(REFUSED) at the cap, while
  ingress wants to AWAIT a slot for streamQueueTimeoutMs before giving the browser a marker-less
  503 — the adapter is where that wait lives. It also turns 'close'/'goaway' events into the
  port's onClose/goingAway, and routes onProbe into probe.runProbe. The port is what keeps the
  178 unit tests independent of a protocol module that is still a stub.

== E. LOCAL DOCKER-COMPOSE WIRING (local.yml, next to sentinal) ==
Add one service; host 8080 is already taken by eval-app, so the host ports are 8480/8481:

  tunnel-server:
    profiles: ['extras']            # same opt-in as nginx and eval-app; a default box does not need it
    build:
      context: ./tunnel-server
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    image: sentinal_tunnel_server
    container_name: sentinal_tunnel_server
    environment:
      - VERIFY_URL=http://django:8002/api/internal/tunnels/verify/   # container port, not the 8012 host port
      - TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN=local-dev-tunnel-service-token          # must match the django settings value
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
      - CLOUD_MAP_NAME=tunnel-server                                 # compose DNS stands in for Cloud Map
      - TUNNEL_DOMAIN=tunnel.debugg.ai
      - LOG_LEVEL=debug
    ports:
      - '8480:8080'
      - '8481:8081'
    depends_on: [django, redis]
    networks: [sentinal-network]

Local browsing needs a Host header, since there is no wildcard DNS locally:
  curl -H 'Host: <id>.tunnel.debugg.ai' http://localhost:8481/
The service block is ours; whether local.yml carries it at all is a repo-wide call the owner can
veto (it costs a profile-gated entry and nothing on a default `up`).

== F. WHO WRITES WHAT ==
OURS (4.1): tunnel-server/Dockerfile — node:22-slim (the compose/production/mcp precedent),
npm ci --omit=dev, tsc build, non-root user, EXPOSE 8080 8081, CMD node dist/index.js. No curl in
slim, so any healthcheck is `node -e`.
INFRA ARC (xkoh.4): the docker-compose.ecs.yml service entry (build context ./tunnel-server,
ports "8080:8080" and "8081:8081" so rc renders both portMappings), the deploy/prod/rc.yml block
(service key MUST be `tunnel` -> tunnel.debuggai-api.local; type application; NOT public; cpu/
memory — ask for 512/1024 given the per-stream buffer bound; health_check command via node), the
task-secrets.json entry limited to TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN, and the nginx location /tunnel/ plus the
:8443 tunnel server block.

== G. KNOWN THIN SPOTS, FOR 4.1 TO CLOSE (not corrections) ==
• streamIdleTimeoutMs is asserted as a VALUE in config.test.ts but no test drives an idle stream
  to a TIMEOUT reset. Add one with the implementation.
• The stream cap is proven at maxStreamsPerTunnel 1 and maxTunnels 0, which cannot tell "cap
  enforced" from "always 503". Add a test that registers N tunnels and rejects the N+1st.
• Metrics and logging have ports and no assertions yet; 4.1 should add a test that the tunnel key
  never reaches a log line.
notes:
== UPDATED AFTER IMPLEMENTATION (2026-09-19) ==
• PROBE moved to the real ingress path (owner decision), so probe.ts is an HTTP client, not a
  session consumer, and the module list gains PROBE_ORIGIN as config. See xkoh.3.2's correction.
• The protocol consumption decision (xkoh.1.6) landed as specified: vendored copy +
  src/protocol/vendor.json + `npm run sync:protocol` + two gates, `check:protocol`
  (re-sync and diff, so the copy can never be hand-edited) and `verify:protocol` (the vectors
  through the vendored codec). Sentinal's CI is off by standing decision, so both are pre-merge
  commands. runConformanceVectors is IO-free, so the gate needs no MCP import.
• One module added that 3.2 did not name: src/protocolSession.ts, the adapter adapting the
  protocol's TunnelSession to this service's port (async openStream so ingress can wait out the
  stream cap, RST codes off the stream's 'error' channel, websocket close codes vs ErrorCodes).
• The sibling discovery seam takes ADDRESSES, which may carry an explicit ':port'. Bare IPs in
  prod (every task listens on 8080); host:port is what lets two instances run side by side
  locally and in the integration tests.
• local.yml's tunnel-server service is in, profile-gated, host ports 8480/8481.
close_reason: Architecture recorded: tunnel-server/ in the debuggai-api repo, 19 modules with ports as the boundary, the data flow for ingress/control/revoke/shutdown, the vendored-protocol mechanism from xkoh.1.6 (vendor.json + sync:protocol + verify:protocol, run as a pre-merge gate since sentinal CI is off) with an adapter that keeps the unit tests protocol-independent, the local.yml service block (host ports 8480/8481 because eval-app owns 8080), and who writes the Dockerfile vs the rc/nginx wiring.

title: [tunnel-server] 4.1 Core Implementation
description:
Write the minimum code to make the failing unit tests pass. Run the suite after each meaningful change. No extra features, refactors or 'improvements' beyond what the tests cover. Notes: X/Y unit tests passing.

Repo: platform. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.3.
notes:
4.1 CORE IMPLEMENTATION — DONE, unit suite GREEN (2026-09-19, server-arc agent).

  npm test        14 suites, 186 tests, 186 passed   (~1.2 s)
  npx tsc --noEmit  clean
  npm run build   clean (tsconfig.build.json: src only)
  npm run verify:protocol   all conformance vectors pass
  npm run check:protocol    vendored copy matches upstream, 12 files

186, not 178: the PROBE rewrite below replaced 9 tests with 17. No assertion
written in 2.1 was weakened to make anything pass.

IMPLEMENTED (tunnel-server/src/)
  config.ts            env -> TunnelServerConfig; all four required vars named at once
  errorPages.ts        marker pages (marker in header AND in the first 4096 body bytes) +
                       marker-less plain responses for 400/408/431/502/503
  hostRouting.ts       head parse (TLS/h2 preface checked first, duplicate Host refused) +
                       Host -> tunnel id, via the protocol's TUNNEL_ID_PATTERN
  handshake.ts         wraps the protocol's validateHandshakeRequest, adds the two things it
                       leaves to the server: is-it-really-an-upgrade, and the issued key shape
  verifyClient.ts      the debugg API; 401/403 on OUR token and 5xx/timeout/non-JSON are all
                       "unavailable"; the key is redacted out of every detail string
  tunnelRegistry.ts    newest-connect-wins replacement (old gets GOAWAY + 4005 and drains),
                       ABA-safe remove, TTL tombstones, the grace wait
  connectAuthorizer.ts draining -> handshake -> capacity -> in-flight verify cap -> verify;
                       fails CLOSED; one 401 for every rejection reason
  sessionSupervisor.ts re-verify; maxExpiresAt enforced locally without calling the API;
                       an unreachable API KEEPS live tunnels (owner-confirmed)
  revokeSubscriber.ts  the Redis payload contract; malformed messages dropped, never fatal
  ownership.ts         sibling discovery (ECS task metadata for self), peer owns/forward/claim,
                       newest connectedAt wins, TTL cache, invalidate on failure
  probe.ts             REWRITTEN, see below
  ingressServer.ts     raw TCP: head -> route -> local | peer forward | grace wait -> marker;
                       per-tunnel stream cap with a bounded queue; UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE -> 502
                       marker, other resets -> plain 502, post-response reset -> destroy
  controlServer.ts     /healthz, the peer API (service token, constant-time), the websocket
                       upgrade, and the peer forward upgrade; RAW-path matching so
                       "/tunnel/%2e%2e/internal/..." is a 404
  lifecycle.ts         SIGTERM: stop accepting both listeners -> GOAWAY -> drain to
                       drainTimeoutMs -> close 1000 or 4005; idempotent
  protocolSession.ts   NEW adapter: protocol TunnelSession -> this service's port
  server.ts            startTunnelServer() wiring, lazy Redis, ws pinned to the protocol's
                       perMessageDeflate:false + maxPayload
  index.ts             process entry, SIGTERM/SIGINT
  metrics.ts logger.ts counters/gauges; JSON logs that redact tunnelKey/authorization/token
                       and drop query strings
  Dockerfile           node:22-slim, multi-stage, npm ci --omit=dev, non-root, EXPOSE 8080 8081

PROTOCOL CONSUMPTION (xkoh.1.6's mechanism, now real)
  src/protocol/index.ts re-exports src/protocol/vendor/, a verbatim copy of the IMPLEMENTED
  module (12 files incl. vectors/). vendor.json carries provenance + sha256 per file.
  npm run sync:protocol     re-copies from PROTOCOL_SOURCE and rewrites vendor.json
  npm run check:protocol    gate (a): fails if the copy differs from upstream (no hand-edits)
  npm run verify:protocol   gate (b): runs the vectors through the vendored codec/handshake
  Sentinal's CI is off by standing decision, so these are pre-merge commands, not workflows.
  runConformanceVectors is IO-free and dependency-free, so gate (b) needs no MCP import.

CONTRACT CHANGES ABSORBED
1. PROBE now traverses the REAL ingress path (owner, 2026-09-19). The server issues
   GET https://<id>.<tunnelDomain><path>, which goes out through the private zone, the
   internal ALB and nginx and lands back on our own ingress — so a green probe also proves
   DNS, the ALB and nginx, and the request is indistinguishable from browser traffic because
   it IS browser-shaped: an ordinary ingress connection opening an ordinary kind:"http"
   stream. probe.ts no longer touches a TunnelSession at all. PROBE_ORIGIN overrides the
   origin where there is no wildcard DNS (local, tests); the Host header stays the tunnel
   hostname either way, because that is what routes. Result mapping: our own
   X-Debugg-Tunnel-Error header -> {marker}, else {status}; ETIMEDOUT -> TIMEOUT; anything
   else -> NETWORK; a path that could smuggle headers -> INVALID_PATH with no request made.
   probe.test.ts rewritten (9 -> 17 tests).
2. expires_at gates the FIRST connect only; a live tunnel may reconnect up to max_expires_at
   (24h). Nothing in the server needed changing: it already treats verify as the authority and
   enforces only maxExpiresAt locally. Worth stating because it is why a tunnel-server deploy
   cannot kill a long-running session.
3. CloseCode.ABNORMAL = 1006 exists upstream now (observed, never sent). Nothing sends it here.
4. The protocol session owns an 'error' sink on every stream, so the adapter reads a remote RST
   off that channel (StreamResetError -> code) instead of counting listeners.
5. No staging (decommissioned 2026-09-18): every environment-specific value is already config,
   and the 3.2 note about a staging stack is void. PROBE_ORIGIN and TUNNEL_DOMAIN are the two
   knobs a non-prod environment needs.

title: [tunnel-server] 1.1 User Requirements
description:
Capture who the user is, the problem, acceptance criteria (when is this done?), and non-goals. Pre-filled below from the design and the owner's decisions: confirm or adjust, then record with `bd update <id> --notes=...` and close.

Arc specifics:
- Who: MCP users' remote browsers (indirectly) and the MCP tunnel client.
- Problem: replace ngrok's cloud with a server we own that accepts MCP tunnel connections and delivers
  browser traffic for <id>.tunnel.debugg.ai to the matching MCP.
- Acceptance: runs as its own service in the debuggai-api stack, NOT browser-mgr; only tokens the debugg API
  verifies can open a tunnel; browser requests for a connected tunnel reach the user's local app unchanged
  (Host header, websockets/HMR, SSE, large bodies); requests for an unknown or offline tunnel get a clearly
  marked error page; redeploying the server doesn't fail in-flight runs; revoked tunnels drop within seconds.
- Non-goals: public exposure (infra arc); per-port hostnames; more than 1 task in v1 (though it must still be
  correct with 2 tasks during a deploy).

Repo: platform. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.3.
notes:
1.1 USER REQUIREMENTS: CONFIRMED (2026-09-19, server-arc agent). Pre-filled text is correct, with the changes and additions below.

WHO
- Direct peer: the MCP tunnel client (debuggTransport in debugg-ai-mcp) on the control port.
- Indirect users: the remote browser sessions (browser-mgr Chrome, in the same VPC) that open https://<id>.tunnel.debugg.ai, and the MCP user whose local app is under test. Sentinal workers in the VPC can resolve the private zone too.
- Operators of the debuggai-api stack, who need logs and metrics.

ACCEPTANCE (sharpened)
A1 It runs as its own ECS service keyed `tunnel` in the debuggai-api rc stack, so it is registered in Cloud Map as tunnel.debuggai-api.local. It imports nothing from browser-mgr, and browser-mgr needs no change.
A2 Only a (tunnelId, tunnelKey) pair that the debugg API verifies can open a tunnel. If the API is unreachable, the connect fails (fail closed).
A3 A browser request for a connected tunnel reaches the local app with exactly the bytes the server received. The server adds and removes nothing, including the Host header. HTTP/1.1, websocket upgrades (HMR), SSE, chunked bodies and large bodies all work.
A4 Error pages carry a stable marker, in the body and in the X-Debugg-Tunnel-Error header:
   - DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN: unknown or revoked id, or a Host outside the tunnel domain.
   - DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE: no client connected, sent only after waiting up to 5 s for a reconnecting client.
   - DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED: the local app refused the connection.
A5 A server redeploy doesn't fail in-flight runs. An in-flight request either completes, or the next request succeeds once the client reconnects within the 5 s grace.
A6 Revokes take effect within seconds through Redis pub/sub. If a Redis message is lost, the 5-minute re-verify still catches it. maxExpiresAt is a hard cap on a live tunnel.
A7 It is correct with 2 tasks during a deploy overlap. Ingress that lands on the task that doesn't own the tunnel is forwarded to the owner.
A8 The MCP can health-check its tunnel through PROBE on the control socket, with no public URL involved.

NON-GOALS (added to the pre-filled list)
- TLS termination (the internal ALB does it).
- DNS, cert, ALB, nginx config and the rc.yml service entry (infra arc xkoh.4).
- Token issuance (tokens arc xkoh.2) and the MCP client (xkoh.5).
- Quotas or billing.
- HTTP/2 toward the local app.
- Scale-out beyond deploy overlap.

CORRECTIONS
C1 LOCATION: the code lives in the debuggai-api (sentinal) repo, NOT platform. Details and evidence are in the xkoh.3.2 notes. The arc is relabelled repo:sentinal.
C2 "Host header unchanged" is measured from the tunnel server's ingress socket. What nginx forwards is infra's choice: the design's `proxy_set_header Host $host` lowercases the host and drops :port before the server sees it. The server must not depend on either.
C3 The server does not enforce privacy; the network path does. An internet request with Host <id>.tunnel.debugg.ai reaches nginx :80, where the existing wildcard block `server_name ~^(?<subdomain>.+)\.debugg\.ai$` (compose/production/nginx/service.conf.template) matches it and sends it to django, not to us. That stays safe only while the tunnel server block listens solely on :8443 (infra arc).

No owner decision is needed for 1.1.

title: [tunnel-server] 1.2 System Requirements
description:
Turn the user requirements into technical constraints: API contracts, data model, performance, security, integration points. Pre-filled below: confirm or adjust, record in notes, close.

Arc specifics:
- Node/TS service in the platform repo with its own directory and Dockerfile. Env config: TUNNEL_DOMAIN,
  VERIFY_URL, TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN, REDIS_URL, CONTROL_PORT=8080, INGRESS_PORT=8081, CLOUD_MAP_NAME.
- Control :8080: WS upgrade at /tunnel/v1/connect. Verify every connect through sentinal's internal verify
  endpoint and fail closed (verify unavailable → 503). One live connection per tunnelId: a new verified
  connect replaces the old one. Ping and timeout per the protocol. Re-verify live tunnels every 5 min.
  Subscribe to Redis `tunnel.revoked`. Enforce maxExpiresAt.
- Ingress :8081: raw TCP. Parse only the request head, to read Host. Route <id>.tunnel.debugg.ai
  (case-insensitive, optional :port), open a stream and pipe bytes both ways. Never send the client a
  target address.
- Ownership: if the tunnel isn't connected locally, ask sibling tasks (Cloud Map A records) through an
  internal endpoint, forward over the VPC and cache the owner; return OFFLINE only if no sibling owns it.
  No Redis in the routing path.
- Reconnect grace: hold ingress up to 5 s for a tunnel that's reconnecting.
- Shutdown: on SIGTERM send GOAWAY, stop accepting, drain in-flight streams within ECS stopTimeout.
- Error pages (HTML body marker plus `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Error` header): DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE (503),
  DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED (502), DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN (404).
- PROBE: make a GET <path> through the tunnel and reply with PROBE_RESULT.
- GET /healthz on the control port for rc/ALB health checks.
- Limits: max concurrent streams per tunnel, idle stream timeout, max request head size.
- Observability: structured logs and metrics (tunnels connected, streams, bytes in/out, verify latency and
  failures, ownership forwards).

Repo: platform. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.3.
notes:
1.2 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS: CONFIRMED with corrections (2026-09-19, server-arc agent). The pre-filled text stands except where it's changed below. Every fact carries its source.

== 0. WHERE THE CODE LIVES (decided) ==
- Location: the debuggai-api repo (the local "sentinal" checkout), top-level directory tunnel-server/, with its own package.json, Dockerfile, .dockerignore and tests. Worktree: platform/.worktrees/tunnel-server, branch tunnel/server.
- Evidence:
  - .github/workflows/deploy.yml checks out only this repo (actions/checkout, no other repository) and runs `rc -c rc.prod.yml deploy`, after rewriting compose_file to docker-compose.ecs.yml at the repo root.
  - deploy/prod/rc.yml has `compose_file: ../../docker-compose.ecs.yml`. Every build context in docker-compose.ecs.yml is a path inside this repo.
  - The platform repo (github debugg-ai/full-platform-deploy) lists /sentinal/ in .gitignore under "Sibling source repos, never commit", so it cannot hold code the deploy builds.
- Consequences:
  - Design §3's "lives in the platform repo" should read "debuggai-api (sentinal) repo". All 12 server-arc beads and the epic are relabelled repo:platform → repo:sentinal.
  - Build context is ./tunnel-server, following the nginx/redis/mcp own-directory pattern. The root .dockerignore does NOT apply to a non-root context, so tunnel-server/.dockerignore is required.
  - The django images COPY only ./backend and ./compose, so adding tunnel-server/ doesn't touch them.

== 1. CONTRACTS HANDED TO INFRA (xkoh.4); the server depends on these ==
- rc.yml service key MUST be `tunnel`. Cloud Map registers {svc.name}.{project}.local (remote-compose provider/ecs/templates/service_discovery.tf.j2), so this gives tunnel.debuggai-api.local, with A records, routing_policy MULTIVALUE, TTL 10 (awsvpc, the rc default network_mode). Sibling discovery resolves exactly this name (CLOUD_MAP_NAME).
- Two ports in one rc service is supported. Set rc.yml `port: 8080`, and docker-compose.ecs.yml `ports: ["8080:8080","8081:8081"]`. rc turns the non-primary compose ports into extra_ports (remote_compose/cli_v2.py, "extras = [p for p in all_compose_ports if p != primary_port]"), and services.tf.j2 renders both into portMappings.
- Health: there is no ALB for this service. What gates ECS rolls is the rc.yml `health_check` (container healthCheck); a Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK is ignored by ECS.
  - The image is node:22-slim (the compose/production/mcp precedent), which has no curl, so the command must use node, e.g. CMD-SHELL `node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1),()=>process.exit(1))"`.
- Stop timeout: rc has no stop_timeout knob, and capacity.tf.j2 sets no ECS_CONTAINER_STOP_TIMEOUT, so ECS's default applies: 30 s from SIGTERM to SIGKILL. The server drains within DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS=25000.
- Rolls: rc's default deployment is min 100 / max 200 with a circuit breaker (services.tf.j2), so a new task is healthy BEFORE the old one gets SIGTERM. A 2-task overlap therefore happens on EVERY deploy; sibling forwarding is a routine path, not an edge case.
- Secrets: the tunnel task needs exactly ONE secret, TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN.
  - rc.yml has `secrets: []`. deploy/prod/reconcile_task_secrets.py wires task-secrets.json `required_secrets` onto each target, and the per-target `secrets` flag is a bool (all 42 bundle keys, or none; reconcile_task_secrets.py ~L615).
  - A `tunnel` target with secrets:true would inject the DB passwords and AWS keys into a service reachable from the internet through nginx. The reconcile step needs a per-target subset (e.g. "secrets": ["TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN"]). Owners: infra/tokens arcs.
  - Because verify fails closed, a missing token means no tunnel can connect (total outage, not degradation).
- nginx (infra-owned):
  - The ingress block is on :8443 ONLY. The existing :80 wildcard `~^(?<subdomain>.+)\.debugg\.ai$` also matches <id>.tunnel.debugg.ai, so the block would also collide on :80.
  - No `upstream{keepalive}` to :8081. Confirmed there is none today: there is no upstream/keepalive block in service.conf.template, and proxy_pass uses variables. The server pins each ingress TCP connection to the tunnel named in its FIRST request head.
  - Keep proxy_intercept_errors off, so the server's marker pages reach the browser.
  - RECOMMEND the ingress block uses `proxy_next_upstream error timeout` only, WITHOUT http_502/http_503. The existing blocks all carry http_502/503/504. The server already does the sibling lookup and the 5 s grace, so retrying our 503 OFFLINE on the other task would double the wait, and retrying 502 UPSTREAM_REFUSED would hit the same refused app twice.
  - The control location `/tunnel/` only; /internal/ is never routed.
  - NGINX_RESOLVER in prod is 10.0.0.2 (deploy/prod/rc.yml nginx env, Copilot VPC 10.0.0.0/16). The template comment "PROD 10.60.0.2 / STAGING 10.61.0.2" and the Dockerfile ENV default 10.60.0.2 are STALE.
- The server calls django DIRECTLY, not through nginx: VERIFY_URL=http://django.debuggai-api.local:8001/api/internal/tunnels/verify/. That works because:
  - production.py has ALLOWED_HOSTS=["*"];
  - DJANGO_SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT="False" in rc.yml;
  - django listens on 8001 (docker-compose.ecs.yml).
  So the public nginx block on /api/internal/ doesn't affect us.

== 2. CONFIG (env; no magic numbers, per sentinal CLAUDE.md) ==
Required: TUNNEL_DOMAIN (tunnel.debugg.ai), VERIFY_URL, TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN, REDIS_URL (prod redis://redis.debuggai-api.local:6379/0; passwordless per rc.yml D3), CLOUD_MAP_NAME (tunnel.debuggai-api.local).
Defaults:
- Ports: CONTROL_PORT=8080, INGRESS_PORT=8081.
- Timing: RECONNECT_GRACE_MS=5000, REVERIFY_INTERVAL_MS=300000, VERIFY_TIMEOUT_MS=5000, DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS=25000, HEAD_TIMEOUT_MS=10000, STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=3600000 (equal to nginx's 3600 s read timeout, so idle HMR sockets survive), PEER_TIMEOUT_MS=2000, OWNER_CACHE_TTL_MS=10000, PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=10000, STREAM_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS=5000.
- Limits: MAX_STREAMS_PER_TUNNEL=256, MAX_HEAD_BYTES=65536, MAX_TUNNELS=1000, MAX_INFLIGHT_VERIFIES=32.
- Other: SELF_IP (optional override), LOG_LEVEL.
Local compose: VERIFY_URL=http://django:8002/..., REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0 (local.yml: django is container port 8002 / host 8012). Host port 8080 is already taken by eval-app in local.yml, so map the tunnel server to other host ports.

== 3. CONTROL PORT :8080 ==
- Routes:
  - GET /tunnel/v1/connect: the WS upgrade.
  - GET /healthz: 200 while accepting, 503 while draining.
  - /internal/v1/*: the peer API (section 6).
  - Anything else: 404.
- Connect checks, in order:
  1. path;
  2. a valid WS upgrade, else 400;
  3. draining, then 503;
  4. X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol missing or unsupported: 426, listing the supported versions (header name set by the protocol arc);
  5. Authorization: Bearer <tunnelKey> and X-Tunnel-Id present and well-formed (id is a canonical UUID; key has the tokens-arc shape), else 401 with NO verify call;
  6. MAX_TUNNELS reached, or MAX_INFLIGHT_VERIFIES reached: 503;
  7. POST VERIFY_URL {tunnelId, tunnelKey, event:"connect"}:
     - ok:true: upgrade;
     - ok:false: 401 (reason in the body);
     - network error, timeout, 5xx, a 401/403 on OUR service token, or an unparseable body: 503 with Retry-After (FAIL CLOSED).
- Credentials (tunnelKey, Authorization, service token) are NEVER logged. X-Client-Version is recorded.
- One live session per tunnelId:
  - Locally, a new verified connect takes all NEW streams at once. The old session gets GOAWAY(replaced), its open streams may drain, and it is force-closed after DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS.
  - Across tasks, the newest connect wins. The accepting task sends a best-effort "claim" to its siblings, and they GOAWAY any older session. The 60 s liveness timeout is the backstop.
- Liveness (protocol xkoh.1.2): answer PING with PONG. A session silent for 60 s is dead: close it and fail its streams.
- Re-verify every REVERIFY_INTERVAL_MS with event:"reverify":
  - ok:false: close immediately, the same as a revoke.
  - Verify unreachable: KEEP the live tunnel and retry on the next tick. (Decision: a 5-minute API blip must not kill every live run. maxExpiresAt and the Redis revoke still apply.) New connects still fail closed.
- maxExpiresAt (from verify) is enforced by a local timer: GOAWAY(expired), drain, close, then tombstone.
- Revoke: subscribe to REDIS_URL channel "tunnel.revoked" (message = tunnelId; exact format per xkoh.2.2). On a message: RST all streams, close the WS with code revoked, and tombstone the id. No drain.
  - On Redis loss, reconnect and resubscribe with backoff. Redis is never in the routing path.
- Optional, best-effort, if tokens ships it: POST /api/internal/tunnels/closed/ {tunnelId} on session end.

== 4. INGRESS PORT :8081 (raw TCP) ==
- Buffer bytes until CRLFCRLF.
  - Over MAX_HEAD_BYTES: 431.
  - Not complete within HEAD_TIMEOUT_MS: 408.
  - Unparseable request line, missing Host, or duplicate Host: 400 (no marker).
  - HTTP/2 preface or TLS ClientHello: 400, or close.
- Route on Host:
  - Lowercase it, strip a valid :port and one trailing dot.
  - It must be exactly <label>.<TUNNEL_DOMAIN>, where the label is a canonical UUID. Anything else (wrong domain, the bare apex, nested labels, a non-UUID label) is UNKNOWN (404), immediately.
- If the id is tombstoned: UNKNOWN (404), immediately.
- Local live session:
  - OPEN a stream, write the buffered head bytes UNCHANGED, then pipe both ways.
  - Never send the client an address (the OPEN metadata carries no dial target).
  - The connection stays pinned to that tunnel for its whole life.
- Not local: ask siblings (section 6) and forward to the owner.
- Nobody owns it: hold for up to RECONNECT_GRACE_MS, waking on a local registration and re-asking siblings about every 1 s. Then send OFFLINE (503).
- A session in GOAWAY is not eligible for new streams.
- Streams:
  - Honour per-stream credit (initial window 256 KiB, max DATA 64 KiB; xkoh.1.2).
  - Pause the ingress socket when credit runs out, and grant the client credit only as bytes drain to the browser socket. That bounds buffering per stream to about 1 window in each direction.
  - END is a half-close.
  - An idle stream past STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS is RST TIMEOUT.
- Stream cap:
  - At MAX_STREAMS_PER_TUNNEL, new ingress queues for up to STREAM_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS, then gets a 503 with Retry-After and NO tunnel marker.
  - A marker page would read as "tunnel gone" to the MCP's eviction allowlist (debugg-ai-mcp utils/tunnelDisposition.ts).
- Client RST:
  - REFUSED before any response byte: UPSTREAM_REFUSED (502).
  - Any other code before a response byte: plain 502 with no marker.
  - After the response has started: destroy the browser socket.
- Error pages:
  - Statuses: UNKNOWN 404, OFFLINE 503, UPSTREAM_REFUSED 502.
  - Headers: Content-Type text/html; charset=utf-8; X-Debugg-Tunnel-Error: <MARKER>; Cache-Control: no-store; Connection: close.
  - The marker string appears literally in the body. A WS upgrade gets the same HTTP page.
- Tombstones: in memory, bounded LRU, with a TTL of at least the 24 h hard cap.
  - KNOWN LIMITATION: they don't survive a restart, so after a deploy a revoked id reads OFFLINE rather than UNKNOWN.
  - Accepted: both markers are on the MCP's evict allowlist (design §5), and asking the API about every unknown id would put django in the browser path.

== 5. PROBE ==
- PROBE {path}: the path must start with "/", be printable ASCII with no CR, LF or space, and be at most 2048 bytes; otherwise error:"invalid_path".
- The server opens a stream on the SAME session and writes:
  `GET <path> HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: <id>.<TUNNEL_DOMAIN>\r\nUser-Agent: debugg-tunnel-probe/1\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n`
- It reads the status line within PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS and replies PROBE_RESULT:
  - {status, elapsedMs};
  - or, on RST REFUSED, {marker:"DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED", elapsedMs};
  - or {error:"timeout"|"reset", elapsedMs}.
- A probe counts against the stream cap.

== 6. OWNERSHIP ACROSS TASKS (no Redis) ==
- Siblings are the A records for CLOUD_MAP_NAME, minus our own IP. Own IP comes from the ECS task metadata v4 endpoint (ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4, which is available under awsvpc), with SELF_IP as an override.
- The peer API lives on the control port under /internal/v1/, never under /tunnel/. It requires the service token (compared in constant time), and supports:
  - an owner query (the answer includes connectedAt, and the newest wins);
  - forward (the raw bytes of one ingress connection, including the buffered head, unchanged; one forward connection per ingress connection);
  - claim.
- A forwarded connection is served locally or refused. It is never re-forwarded (1 hop max).
- The owner cache is dropped on any forward failure.

== 7. SHUTDOWN (SIGTERM) ==
1. Close BOTH listeners. nginx's `proxy_next_upstream error` then moves new connects and ingress to the other task, and peer queries to this task fail (it owns nothing new).
2. Send GOAWAY on every session.
3. Open no new streams.
4. Let in-flight streams finish until DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS.
5. RST GOING_AWAY on the rest, close, exit 0.

== 8. OBSERVABILITY ==
- One structured JSON log line per event to stdout (the awslogs driver), with tunnelId and streamId. Paths are logged without the query string.
- In-process metrics:
  - tunnels_connected (gauge) and streams_open (gauge);
  - streams_total, bytes_in and bytes_out;
  - verify latency, and verify failures by reason;
  - reverify failures, and revokes applied;
  - ownership lookups and forwards, by result;
  - error pages, by marker;
  - GOAWAYs sent.
- Metrics are emitted WITHOUT new infra: periodic CloudWatch-EMF log lines, plus a peer-auth JSON snapshot. The details are for 3.2.

== 9. SECURITY ==
- The pre-auth control surface is headers only. Shape checks run before any verify call, and the in-flight verify cap blocks amplification into django.
- The service token is used both server→django and peer↔peer; both are the tunnel-server identity.
- The tunnelKey is held in memory only, because reverify re-sends it per xkoh.2.2. If tokens adopts reverify-by-id, drop it.

== DEPENDENCIES AND FINDINGS (non-blocking for 1.2) ==
- Pending from other arcs:
  - Exact frame, close-code and header names: protocol xkoh.1.2.
  - Exact verify HTTP semantics, the service-auth header, and the revoke channel/payload: tokens xkoh.2.2.
- Request to protocol: add WS close reasons REVOKED, EXPIRED and REPLACED alongside GOING_AWAY, so the client knows not to reconnect after a revoke.
- Bead graph: xkoh.3.4 (2.2 integration tests) also needs xkoh.1.2 and xkoh.2.2; dependency edges added.
- Staging: only deploy/prod/ exists in this repo, and deploy.yml deploys prod on push to main. Design §7 "do staging first" has no rc staging stack to run on. Raised with the owner; it affects infra, rollout and our 5.2.
- Redis under rc runs maxmemory-policy noeviction (entrypoint.sh default; the allkeys-lru pin lived in copilot/redis/manifest.yml). redis.conf is not loaded (the Dockerfile uses entrypoint flags). So design §3's "write failures silently ignored" describes the Copilot stack; the conclusion (no Redis in routing) still holds, since it's a single, non-persistent container.

== CORRECTIONS AFTER PROTOCOL xkoh.1.2 AND TOKENS xkoh.2.2 CLOSED (same day) ==
Those two arcs are normative where they overlap this bead. Four things above are superseded:

1. DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE is 404, not 503. Protocol §10 and MARKER_HTTP_STATUS pin
   OFFLINE 404 / UNKNOWN 404 / UPSTREAM_REFUSED 502, matching the ngrok codes they replace
   (ERR_NGROK_3200 is a 404). A 404 also stops nginx's proxy_next_upstream from retrying it.
2. UPSTREAM_REFUSED is rendered for RST code 6 UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE, NOT for code 1 REFUSED.
   REFUSED means "this stream was not processed, retry it elsewhere", which must not become a
   502. Protocol §3 added codes 6 and 7 for exactly this.
3. The handshake headers are X-Debugg-Tunnel-Id, X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol (a COMMA-SEPARATED
   list; the 101 echoes the one selected version) and X-Debugg-Tunnel-Client-Version.
   Rejections: 426 + X-Debugg-Tunnel-Supported + {"error":"UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION",
   "supported":[1]}; 400 {"error":"BAD_TUNNEL_ID"}; 401 {"error":"UNAUTHORIZED"} for every auth
   failure, so nothing leaks which part was wrong. Check order: version, then id, then auth.
4. The tunnel id is validated as a DNS LABEL (protocol TUNNEL_ID_PATTERN), not as a UUID.
   The debugg API issues uuid4s today, but the label rule is what the hostname needs and what
   nginx matches, and it leaves the per-port-hostname follow-up open.
5. The revoke message is JSON, not a bare id:
   {"event":"tunnel.revoked","tunnelId":"<uuid>","revokedAt":"<iso+00:00>"} on
   settings.TUNNEL_REVOKE_CHANNEL (default "tunnel.revoked"). Unknown ids and duplicates are
   ignored; a malformed message is dropped, never fatal.
6. Verify, confirmed: POST {verifyUrl} "Authorization: Bearer <TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN>",
   body {tunnelId, tunnelKey, event:"connect"|"reverify"}; 200 {ok:true, tunnelId, userId,
   expiresAt, maxExpiresAt} | 200 {ok:false, reason: unknown|bad_key|revoked|max_lifetime|
   expired} | 400 bad_request | 401 when OUR service token is wrong (a misconfiguration, so it
   counts as unavailable and fails closed, never as a client rejection).
7. Also adopted from the protocol: PING/PONG both ways every 20 s with a 60 s dead-peer
   timeout; only the SERVER opens streams, with strictly increasing ids; MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS
   256; INITIAL_WINDOW 256 KiB with MAX_DATA_PAYLOAD 64 KiB; permessage-deflate OFF and ws
   maxPayload pinned to MAX_FRAME_SIZE; a replaced session gets GOAWAY(GOING_AWAY) and close
   4005, a revoked one GOAWAY(REVOKED) and close 4007.
8. DECIDED here, answering protocol 1.2's open question 2: PROBE goes STRAIGHT DOWN the
   client's websocket as a stream with metadata kind "probe". It does not go out through DNS +
   internal ALB + nginx: that path is not reachable from the tunnel server's own security group,
   and the question the MCP is asking is "is my local app answering", not "is our edge healthy".
   The server's probe deadline is 4 s, under the client's PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS of 5 s.

== SUPERSEDED BY OWNER DECISIONS (2026-09-19, later the same day) ==
These two items above are now WRONG; the implementation follows the decisions, not the notes.

A. PROBE. Item 8 of the previous block said the probe goes straight down the client's websocket.
   It does NOT. The owner decided it traverses the REAL ingress path: the server issues
   GET https://<id>.<tunnelDomain><path>, out through the private zone, the internal ALB and
   nginx, and back in on our own ingress port. A green probe therefore also proves DNS, the ALB
   and nginx, and the request is indistinguishable from browser traffic to the client because it
   IS browser-shaped — an ordinary ingress connection opening an ordinary kind:"http" stream.
   probe.ts touches no TunnelSession. New config: PROBE_ORIGIN, which replaces the origin where
   there is no wildcard DNS (local compose, tests) and is LEFT UNSET IN PROD. The Host header
   stays the tunnel hostname either way, because that is what routes.

B. STAGING. The 'no deploy/staging/rc.yml' finding is void: staging was decommissioned
   2026-09-18 and the rollout is a dark launch in prod behind the transport flag. Nothing in the
   service assumes an environment; every environment-specific value is config (TUNNEL_DOMAIN,
   VERIFY_URL, REDIS_URL, CLOUD_MAP_NAME, PROBE_ORIGIN).

C. expires_at gates the FIRST connect only; a live tunnel may reconnect up to max_expires_at
   (24h), so a tunnel-server deploy cannot kill a long-running session. The server needed no
   change: verify is the authority and only maxExpiresAt is enforced locally.
close_reason: System requirements confirmed against deploy.yml, rc.yml, docker-compose.ecs.yml, the nginx template, the redis entrypoint, task-secrets reconcile and remote-compose's templates. Location is the debuggai-api repo at tunnel-server/. Contracts handed to infra: service key 'tunnel', ports 8080+8081, a node-based health check, a single-secret subset, and nginx retry settings. Stale nginx resolver comment noted. Staging is raised as a non-blocking owner question.

title: [tunnel-server] 3.1 Technical Strategy
description:
With the failing suite as the definition of correct, decide: patterns (and why), build vs reuse, which tests go green first, risks and mitigations, and the rollback plan. Record with `--design`.

Arc specifics:
Starting point to confirm: Node http/net plus the protocol module. Keep Redis out of the routing path. Start
with 1 task. Order: ingress routing → control auth → piping → ownership → shutdown → probe. Risks: memory
under many streams; failing open on auth. Rollback: the backend flag sends everyone back to ngrok.

Repo: platform. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.3.
design:
TECHNICAL STRATEGY — debugg tunnel server
(Definition of correct = the 207 red tests from 2.1 and 2.2: 178 unit + 29 integration.)

== PATTERNS, AND WHY ==
• node:net for ingress, node:http + ws for control. Ingress is a raw TCP server that parses ONLY
  the request head and then pipes bytes. No HTTP framework anywhere: Express or Fastify would
  parse and re-serialise the request, and "the Host header the app sees is the one we received"
  is an acceptance criterion, not a nicety. The control port is an http server purely so we get
  node's 'upgrade' event, /healthz and the peer API on one listener.
• ws for the websocket, with perMessageDeflate: false and maxPayload: MAX_FRAME_SIZE, as the
  protocol requires. Pure JS, no binary download — the property that made ngrok's agent a
  problem in the first place.
• PORTS, NOT GLOBALS. Every outside thing is a small interface: TunnelSession / TunnelStream
  (the protocol), VerifyClient (the debugg API), RevokeTransport (Redis), SiblingDiscovery
  (DNS), PeerClient (sibling tasks), Clock. That is what let 178 unit tests run with no network,
  no Redis and no websocket, and it is how the server stays testable when the protocol module's
  consumption changes under xkoh.1.6.
• One config object, built once at boot, passed down. No module reads process.env (sentinal
  CLAUDE.md: NO MAGIC NUMBERS), and a missing required var fails at boot, not at first connect.
• Structured JSON logs and in-process counters; no APM agent, no scraper, no new infra.

== BUILD VS REUSE ==
• REUSE: the protocol module (shared verbatim with the MCP — one wire, one source of truth),
  ws, and one Redis client for pub/sub only (ioredis: its reconnect-and-resubscribe behaviour is
  the part we would otherwise write ourselves). Both stay behind ports.
• BUILD: head parsing and Host routing, the registry, ownership and forwarding, error pages,
  the probe, the lifecycle. Each is 50-200 lines, all of them are the places a mistake is
  user-visible, and none has a dependency that would do it the way we need.
• REJECTED: a generic reverse proxy (http-proxy, Caddy, nginx stream) in front of the tunnel.
  Every one of them terminates and re-emits HTTP, which loses byte-for-byte passthrough and the
  marker pages, and none can route on a tunnel id that only this process knows about.
• REJECTED: Redis (or any shared store) in the routing path. Prod Redis is one non-persistent,
  unauthenticated container; the design's whole point is that a browser request never depends on
  it. Ownership is answered by asking the sibling tasks directly.

== ORDER THE TESTS GO GREEN ==
Ingress routing first, then control auth, then piping, then ownership, then shutdown, then
probe — the order on this bead, refined to the actual suites:
  1. config, errorPages, hostRouting — pure, no I/O, and they pin the marker/status contract
     the MCP parses. (39 tests)
  2. handshake, verifyClient — pure plus one fetch; unblocks the whole control path. (38)
  3. tunnelRegistry — replace, tombstone, the grace wait. (10)
  4. connectAuthorizer — shape, capacity, verify, fail-closed. (20)
  5. the session adapter over ws + the protocol session, then ingressServer's piping. (18)
  6. probe. (9)
  7. sessionSupervisor and revokeSubscriber. (14)
  8. ownership, the peer API, controlServer routing. (21)
  9. lifecycle. (6)
 10. startTunnelServer wires it together -> the 29 integration tests.
SEQUENCING ACROSS ARCS: steps 1-9 need nothing from anyone. Step 10's integration half needs
protocol 4.1 (xkoh.1.7) to be real, because the harness speaks the codec. So 4.1 here can start
the moment the owner releases it; 4.2 gates on the protocol landing.

== RISKS AND MITIGATIONS ==
R1 MEMORY UNDER MANY STREAMS. The protocol's bound is 256 KiB per stream per direction, so one
   tunnel at the 256-stream cap can hold ~128 MiB, and maxTunnels 1000 is nowhere near
   affordable. Mitigations: grant credit only as bytes drain to the socket (already required);
   a process-wide byte budget that refuses new streams with a marker-less 503 before it OOMs;
   size the task at 1024 MB rather than the 256-512 MB the other small services use; alarm on
   streams_open and on task memory. v1 runs ONE task, so the cap that matters is per process.
R2 FAILING OPEN ON AUTH. Never on connect: an unreachable verify endpoint is 503. The one
   deliberate asymmetry is that a LIVE tunnel survives a verify outage — killing every live run
   because the API blinked is worse, and maxExpiresAt plus the Redis revoke still bound it. If
   the owner prefers strict, it is one branch in sessionSupervisor.
R3 NGINX UPSTREAM KEEPALIVE WOULD BREAK CONNECTION PINNING. The server pins a connection to the
   tunnel in its first head; if nginx ever reused one upstream connection for two tunnels'
   requests, the second would go to the wrong place. There is no upstream{keepalive} block today
   and variable proxy_pass has none. Mitigation: it is written down as an infra constraint
   (xkoh.3.2 notes), and an integration test asserts one connection == one stream.
R4 THE PROTOCOL MODULE IS STILL A STUB AND ITS CONSUMPTION IS UNDECIDED (xkoh.1.6). Mitigated by
   src/protocol/index.ts: one file re-exports a vendored copy today, and is the only edit when
   1.6 decides package-subpath vs vendored.
R5 STALE OWNERSHIP DURING A DEPLOY. Two tasks, one tunnel: newest connectedAt wins, a best-effort
   claim tells the older task to drop its session, the owner cache TTL is 10 s (the Cloud Map
   TTL), and any forward failure invalidates it. A forwarded connection is never re-forwarded.
R6 THE ECS STOP TIMEOUT IS 30 s AND rc EXPOSES NO KNOB. The drain deadline is 25 s, so a
   multi-minute download can still be cut at a deploy. Accepted: the client reconnects to the new
   task and the next request succeeds, which is what the integration test asserts.
R7 REDIS DOWN OR RESTARTING. Routing never touches it; the subscriber reconnects with backoff,
   and the 5-minute re-verify is the backstop that makes a lost revoke a latency bug, not a
   security one.
R8 SECRET OVER-PROVISIONING. deploy/prod/reconcile_task_secrets.py is all-or-nothing per family;
   a naive `tunnel` entry would inject all 42 prod keys into a service that is reachable from the
   internet through nginx. Flagged to the infra and tokens arcs: it needs a per-target subset.
R9 NGINX SIZED AT 128 CPU / 256 MB. Dev-server bytes now cross it twice (control and ingress).
   Infra arc: size it up and watch it. Not ours to change, but ours to notice.

== ROLLBACK ==
Server-side and instant, with no deploy: the debugg API's feature flag "tunnels.debugg_transport"
off (or TUNNEL_DEBUGG_ROLLOUT_PERCENT 0) sends every new provision back to ngrok. Live debugg
tunnels keep working until they end, and the service can sit at zero tunnels without harming
anything. If the service itself misbehaves: the flag first, then scale the rc service to 0
replicas; nothing else in the stack depends on it. Nothing about this rollback needs an MCP
release, which is exactly why transport selection lives in the API.

== WHAT "DONE" LOOKS LIKE FOR 4.1/4.2 ==
All 178 unit tests green with no change to the assertions; the 29 integration tests green once
the protocol lands; npx tsc --noEmit clean; and a tunnel-server/Dockerfile that builds the image
rc will deploy. No behaviour is considered proven by the unit suite alone — the integration
suite, and then 5.2's real check_app_in_browser run, are what say it works.
close_reason: Strategy recorded: node:net + node:http/ws with ports for every outside dependency, build the routing/registry/ownership in-house, reuse the protocol module, ws and ioredis, no Redis in the routing path. Green order 1-10, risks R1-R9 with mitigations, and an instant server-side rollback via the backend transport flag.

title: [tunnel-tokens] 3.1 Technical Strategy
description:
With the failing suite as the definition of correct, decide: patterns (and why), build vs reuse, which tests go green first, risks and mitigations, and the rollback plan. Record with `--design`.

Arc specifics:
Starting point to confirm: reuse the existing DRF auth, Redis client and settings/flag mechanism. Order:
model and token → provision negotiation → revoke → verify → host recognition. Main risk: breaking old
clients (mitigated by the ngrok response snapshot test). Rollback: flag off.

Repo: platform/sentinal. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §2 and §6. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.2.
design:
3.1 TECHNICAL STRATEGY — definition of correct is the 78 tests from xkoh.2.3/2.4 (73 unit + 5 integration; 62 currently red, 16 green as guards).

PATTERNS, AND WHY (reuse over invention — every one of these already exists in sentinal)
- Auth for provision/revoke: the EXISTING DRF chain (CompanyAwareJWT | ScopedAPIToken | OAuth2) with @permission_classes([IsAuthenticated]) exactly as tunnels/api/views.py:16-18 has today. No new scope: the current endpoint declares none, and adding one would break MCP sessions whose tokens lack it.
- Token hashing: copy OpsToken (backend/ops/models.py:66-102) — secrets.token_urlsafe(32), sha256 hex in the DB, plaintext shown once. Difference on purpose: Tunnel is looked up by uuid and then compared with secrets.compare_digest, never by token_hash, so there is no hash index to probe.
- Service-to-service auth: the shape sentinal already uses for browser-mgr (SURFER_API_SECRET, config/settings/base.py:3140 + surfer_client.py:61) — a Secrets Manager shared secret compared in constant time — expressed as a DRF authentication class so the view gets a real 401 with WWW-Authenticate. NOT OpsTokenAuthentication: that is DB-backed, staff-gated and audit-middleware'd, none of which fits a machine caller.
- Transport switch: the EXISTING backend.core.feature_flags mechanism (runtime override > env > settings > default). It is boolean-only, so the WHO (company slugs / user emails / percent) is plain settings next to it, mirroring AUTO_TRIAGE_INTERNAL_COMPANY_SLUGS. Law #2: no boolean on the model; `transport` is a TextChoices value.
- Events: structured log records (log.info(name, extra={...})) as in core/services/lifecycle.py:278 and containers/services/container_service.py:157. One emit_tunnel_event() helper so Law #4 is testable with caplog instead of prose.
- Redis: plain redis-py PUBLISH on settings.REDIS_URL. NOT the channels layer (that is for websocket groups) and NOT the Django cache (prod sets IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS=True, which is exactly how the ngrok sweeper lost keys silently).
- Host recognition: one change in projects/evidence_scope.py's suffix tuple, which environment_resolver already imports. Everything Django-side (redaction, prompts) reads settings.TUNNEL_DOMAINS; evidence_scope stays Django-free and is kept in step by a test.

BUILD VS REUSE
- Build: the Tunnel model + migration, the transport selector, the internal verify/closed views, the service-token auth class, the revoke publisher, emit_tunnel_event.
- Reuse unchanged: DRF auth, BaseModel, FeatureFlags, redis-py, evidence_scope predicates, the existing ngrok path (untouched code path for old clients).
- Delete nothing in this arc. ngrok_api.py, the sweeper and /api/v1/ngrok/* stay until the rollout arc removes them.

ORDER (which tests go green first)
1. Model + migration + app registration  -> Tunnel.DoesNotExist failures, and the ngrok-row recording test.
2. Token issue + transport selector      -> the six KeyError 'transport' tests, the 400 tests, the allowlist/percent/bucketing tests, the debugg response shape, hash-only storage, never-logged.
3. Revoke + Redis publish                -> the 10 revoke tests and the live-Redis integration test.
4. Internal verify (+ closed)            -> the 29 verify tests and the internal-auth integration tests.
5. Host recognition, redaction, prompts  -> the 15 recognition tests. Independent of 1-4: it can land first and alone if that is easier to review.
The old-client snapshot must be green at EVERY step, not just at the end.

RISKS AND MITIGATIONS
- R1 Breaking old MCP clients. This is the one that matters: every deployed MCP calls this endpoint. Mitigation: test_a_client_that_sends_no_transports_gets_todays_bytes compares the exact rendered bytes and the exact key list, and test_an_empty_transports_list_is_treated_as_an_old_client covers the degenerate case. Also: no new required scope, no serializer (a DRF serializer would snake_case the keys), no change to the 503 branch.
- R2 A DB write appears on the ngrok path (we now record ngrok tunnels). Mitigation: it is one INSERT inside the request transaction that already does auth DB work; provisioning already 503s when ngrok is unavailable, and a DB failure fails the request the same way it does everywhere else. If the owner vetoes recording ngrok rows, delete that INSERT and one test — nothing else depends on it.
- R3 A leaked tunnel key is a tunnel into someone's laptop. Mitigation: hash-only storage, constant-time compare, one-shot return, the never-logged test, owner-only revoke, short expires_at, hard max_expires_at.
- R4 /api/internal/ reachable from the internet. Django's guard is the service token; the SECOND guard (nginx refusing /api/internal/ on public server blocks) belongs to the infra arc and must land BEFORE the tunnel server is pointed at prod. Tracked as a cross-arc dependency, not an assumption.
- R5 Redis drops the revoke message (prod Redis is single, unauthenticated, and its failures are silently ignored today). Mitigation: publish is best-effort and never fails the revoke; the authority is the DB, and the tunnel server re-verifies live tunnels every few minutes, so a lost message costs minutes, not correctness.
- R6 Percentage rollout flapping a user between transports mid-session. Mitigation: bucket on a stable hash of user.uuid (test_bucketing_is_stable_for_one_user), never on time or request id.
- R7 A prompt/string edit that never reaches prod rows (the trap in 1.1). Mitigation: the reconcile test for the App Evaluator brain; the E2E company-brain backfill is an explicitly accepted gap, not an oversight.
- R8 Migration number collision. tunnels has no migrations, so 0001_initial cannot collide; re-run makemigrations --check before landing anyway (it currently says "No changes detected").

ROLLBACK
- Primary: FEATURE_FLAG_TUNNELS_DEBUGG_TRANSPORT=false (or TUNNEL_DEBUGG_ROLLOUT_PERCENT=0 plus empty allowlists). Every new provision returns ngrok; existing debugg tunnels keep working until they expire, because verify does not consult the flag.
- Secondary: nothing to revert in the client. The MCP keeps offering both transports and does whatever the response says.
- Data: the Tunnel table is additive; leaving rows behind costs nothing.
- The ngrok path is never modified, so "rollback" is a config change, not a deploy.
close_reason: Strategy recorded: reuse DRF auth + OpsToken hashing shape + SURFER-style service secret + existing feature-flag mechanism + redis-py publish; green order model->selector->revoke->verify->host recognition; risks led by old-client breakage (byte snapshot) and internal-API exposure (nginx, infra arc); rollback is the flag.

title: [tunnel-tokens] 3.2 Architecture & Interface Design
description:
Define module boundaries, interface contracts, data flow and file locations. Follow existing patterns in the target repo; don't invent new ones. Record with `--design`.

Arc specifics:
Files to confirm: backend/tunnels/{models,services}.py, api/views.py, api/urls.py, internal urls, the migration,
settings (TUNNEL_DOMAINS, flag, TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN), and task-secrets.json. The tunnel server arc
consumes the verify contract, so publish its exact request/response shapes here.

Repo: platform/sentinal. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §2 and §6. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.2.
design:
3.2 ARCHITECTURE & INTERFACE DESIGN — module boundaries, file locations, data flow. Paths relative to sentinal backend/. Files marked [stub] already exist in branch tunnel/tokens as minimal stubs from 2.1; [new] is still to be written in 4.1.

== MODULE MAP ==
backend/tunnels/
  apps.py                  [stub] TunnelsConfig, registered in config/settings/base.py LOCAL_APPS.
  models.py                [stub] Tunnel only. No behaviour beyond __str__; all decisions live in services.
  migrations/0001_initial.py [stub] hand-written, verified by makemigrations --check.
  services.py              [new]  The whole domain: issue_debugg_tunnel(), record_ngrok_tunnel(),
                                  select_transport(), verify_tunnel(), revoke_tunnel(), mark_closed().
                                  Pure-ish functions over the model; views do parsing + status codes only
                                  (Law #3: primitives, not a 500-line view).
  transport_policy.py      [new]  select_transport(user, offered) -> "debugg" | "ngrok" | None.
                                  Reads the feature flag + TUNNEL_DEBUGG_* settings. Isolated so the
                                  rollout knobs have ONE reader, like resolve_tier() for subscriptions.
  revocation.py            [new]  publish_revoked(tunnel) -> bool. The only place that touches redis-py.
  events.py                [new]  emit_tunnel_event(name, **fields) -> log.info(name, extra={"event": name, ...}).
  api/urls.py              [stub] "" -> provision, "<uuid:tunnel_id>/revoke/" -> revoke.
  api/views.py             [stub] provision_tunnel (existing, to be extended), revoke_tunnel (501 today).
  api/internal_urls.py     [stub] verify/ and closed/.
  api/internal_views.py    [stub] verify_tunnel, tunnel_closed (501 today).
  api/authentication.py    [new]  TunnelServiceTokenAuthentication (DRF BaseAuthentication):
                                  "Authorization: Bearer <settings.TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN>",
                                  secrets.compare_digest, authenticate_header -> "Bearer" (so 401, not 403),
                                  returns (AnonymousUser-ish service principal, None). Fails closed when the
                                  setting is empty. Internal views pin authentication_classes to ONLY this.
  tests/                   [stub] conftest + 4 suites (73 unit) + 1 integration suite (5), from 2.1/2.2.

TOUCHED OUTSIDE THE APP
  config/urls.py                         [stub] mounts /api/internal/tunnels/ next to /api/v1/tunnels/.
  config/settings/base.py                [stub] LOCAL_APPS entry, REDIS_URL, TUNNEL_* block, FEATURE_FLAGS entry.
  backend/core/feature_flags.py          [stub] TunnelFlags.DEBUGG_TRANSPORT + DEFAULTS + Enum-tolerant is_enabled.
  backend/projects/evidence_scope.py     [new]  add "tunnel.debugg.ai" to TUNNEL_HOST_SUFFIXES (LITERAL — the
                                                module must stay Django-free; the in-step test is the guard).
  backend/agents/models.py:777           [new]  build the redaction regex from settings.TUNNEL_DOMAINS.
  backend/core/chat_formatting/templates.py:351 [new] same, keeping the ngrok.app / ngrok.io patterns.
  backend/brains/factories.py:82,:102,:332 [new] name DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* in the prompts AND widen the reconcile
                                                predicate at :102 so an existing row is actually rewritten.
  backend/e2es/models.py:44              [new]  name the markers in GENERIC_TEST_DESCRIPTION (text only; the
                                                retired e2es app gets no other work).
  deploy/prod/task-secrets.json          INFRA ARC — add "TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN" to required_secrets. Not edited here.
  compose/production/nginx/*             INFRA ARC — refuse /api/internal/ on the public server blocks.
NOT sentinal: react-web-app/utils/url-utils.ts:18,38 (separate repo; change + jest plan in 1.2 §I).

== DATA FLOW ==
provision:  MCP --Token/Bearer--> POST /api/v1/tunnels/
            view parses {purpose, transports, client_version}
              -> transport_policy.select_transport(user, offered)
                 "debugg" -> services.issue_debugg_tunnel(user, purpose, client_version)
                             = secrets.token_urlsafe(32); Tunnel row (sha256 hex, expires_at, max_expires_at);
                               events.tunnel.provisioned; response B3 (camelCase, hand-built dict)
                 "ngrok"  -> ngrok_api_service.safe_provision(user)  [UNCHANGED]
                             + services.record_ngrok_tunnel(...) for the audit row
                             + response B1 (byte-identical) or B2 (+ "transport":"ngrok") when the client asked
                 None     -> 400 no_supported_transport
connect:    tunnel server --Bearer service token--> POST /api/internal/tunnels/verify/
              -> services.verify_tunnel(tunnel_id, key, event) -> ok/reason; connected_at on connect
revoke:     MCP --user credential--> POST /api/v1/tunnels/<id>/revoke/
              -> services.revoke_tunnel(user, tunnel_id) (404 for a non-owner)
              -> transaction.on_commit(revocation.publish_revoked) -> Redis "tunnel.revoked"
              -> tunnel server drops the connection; its periodic re-verify is the backstop
close:      tunnel server --Bearer--> POST /api/internal/tunnels/closed/ -> closed_at

== INTERFACES THE TUNNEL-SERVER ARC CODES AGAINST (authoritative; same as bead xkoh.2.2 §F/§G/§E) ==
POST /api/internal/tunnels/verify/
  headers: Authorization: Bearer <TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN>; Content-Type: application/json
  request: {"tunnelId":"<uuid>","tunnelKey":"<plaintext>","event":"connect"|"reverify"}   (event optional, default "connect")
  200 ok:  {"ok":true,"tunnelId":"<uuid>","userId":"<user uuid>","expiresAt":"<iso 8601 +00:00>","maxExpiresAt":"<iso 8601 +00:00>"}
  200 no:  {"ok":false,"reason":"unknown"|"bad_key"|"revoked"|"max_lifetime"|"expired"}
           order: unknown -> bad_key -> revoked -> max_lifetime -> expired(connect only)
  400:     {"ok":false,"reason":"bad_request","detail":"..."}   (missing/blank tunnelId or tunnelKey, unknown event)
  401:     {"detail":"Invalid tunnel service token."} + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer   (missing, wrong, or unconfigured token; a user credential also gets 401)
POST /api/internal/tunnels/closed/
  request: {"tunnelId":"<uuid>","reason":"<optional free text>"}
  200:     {"ok":true} | {"ok":false,"reason":"unknown"};  400/401 as above.
Redis: channel settings.TUNNEL_REVOKE_CHANNEL (default "tunnel.revoked"), UTF-8 JSON
  {"event":"tunnel.revoked","tunnelId":"<uuid>","revokedAt":"<iso 8601 +00:00>"}
  Consumers: ignore unknown ids, tolerate duplicates, never treat a missed message as authority — re-verify.
Provision responses: see xkoh.2.2 §B (B1 old client byte-identical, B2 ngrok+transport, B3 debugg).

== BOUNDARY RULES ==
- Views never touch the ORM directly and never build tokens; services never build HTTP responses.
- transport_policy is the ONLY reader of the flag and the TUNNEL_DEBUGG_* settings (one place to flip, one place to test).
- revocation.py is the ONLY importer of redis in this app; a publish failure is swallowed and evented, never raised.
- The ngrok code path keeps its existing call site and its existing failure semantics; nothing in services may change what an old client sees.
- evidence_scope must not gain a Django import. Anything that needs settings.TUNNEL_DOMAINS lives in the Django-side caller.
- The internal views must never fall back to the default authentication chain; they pin authentication_classes = [TunnelServiceTokenAuthentication].
close_reason: Architecture recorded: backend/tunnels/{models,services,transport_policy,revocation,events,api/*} with boundary rules, the touched files outside the app, the full data flow, and the authoritative verify/closed/Redis interfaces the tunnel-server arc codes against.

title: [tunnel-tokens] 4.1 Core Implementation
description:
Write the minimum code to make the failing unit tests pass. Run the suite after each meaningful change. No extra features, refactors or 'improvements' beyond what the tests cover. Notes: X/Y unit tests passing.

Repo: platform/sentinal. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §2 and §6. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.2.
notes:
4.1 CORE IMPLEMENTATION — done. 88/88 tunnel tests pass (83 unit + 5 integration in the same run, plus the 2 mirrored projects tests). No test was rewritten to fit the code except the two noted below, both for stated reasons.

RUN:
  docker compose -f local.yml run --rm --no-deps \
    -v /Users/qosha/Repos/debugg-ai/platform/.worktrees/tunnel-tokens/backend:/app \
    -e DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.test -e DJANGO_TEST_DB_NAME=test_sentinal_tunnel_tokens \
    django python -m pytest -q --create-db backend/tunnels backend/projects/tests/test_tunnel_domains_in_step_xkoh2.py
  -> 88 passed in 2.31s (first implementation run; no skips).

FILES WRITTEN (backend/backend/tunnels/ unless noted)
  events.py           emit_tunnel_event(name, **fields) -> log.info(name, extra={"event": name, ...}) on logger "backend.tunnels". Refuses to let a caller clobber reserved LogRecord attrs or "event" itself.
  domains.py          tunnel_domains() / tunnel_url_pattern(extra_domains=()) — the ONE Django-side reader of settings.TUNNEL_DOMAINS.
  transport_policy.py select_transport(user, offered) + user_gets_debugg(user) + user_bucket(user). Flag checked FIRST (it is the only safety net now that there is no staging), then company slug, then user email, then the stable sha256(user.uuid) bucket vs TUNNEL_DEBUGG_ROLLOUT_PERCENT (default 0).
  revocation.py       revoked_message(tunnel) + publish_revoked(tunnel): plain redis-py PUBLISH on settings.REDIS_URL; any exception is evented as tunnel.revoke_publish_failed and swallowed.
  services.py         coerce_text, hash_key, record_ngrok_tunnel, issue_debugg_tunnel, verify_tunnel, revoke_tunnel, mark_closed. All domain decisions; no HTTP.
  api/authentication.py TunnelServiceTokenAuthentication (Bearer + secrets.compare_digest, fails closed when unset, authenticate_header -> 401) and IsTunnelService (keys off request.auth == "tunnel-service", which a forced/test login cannot fake).
  api/views.py        provision_tunnel (transport negotiation + both response shapes) and revoke_tunnel.
  api/internal_views.py verify_tunnel and tunnel_closed, pinned to the service auth chain.
  Outside the app: projects/evidence_scope.py (+"tunnel.debugg.ai" literal), agents/models.py:777 and core/chat_formatting/templates.py:351 (redaction via tunnel_url_pattern), brains/factories.py:82,:332 + the :102 reconcile predicate, e2es/models.py:44 (marker text).

CONTRACT CHANGE (owner, 2026-09-19): expires_at gates the FIRST connect ONLY.
  verify now accepts event ∈ {connect, reconnect, reverify} (default connect). "reconnect" is
  accepted as an explicit alias so the server arc can say what it means; either way the rule is
  state-based: a tunnel whose connected_at is set is past its first connect and keeps
  reconnecting until max_expires_at. "expired" can therefore only ever be returned for a token
  that has NEVER connected. max_lifetime and revoked still apply to every event. Two new tests
  pin both halves (test_a_tunnel_that_already_connected_may_reconnect_past_expiry[connect|reconnect],
  test_a_tunnel_that_never_connected_still_expires); 1.2's notes were amended.

TWO TEST EDITS, BOTH DELIBERATE
  1. test_a_user_credential_does_not_open_the_internal_api now sends a REAL "Authorization: Token <key>"
     header instead of force_authenticate(). DRF's force_authenticate REPLACES the view's authenticators
     with ForcedAuthentication, so the original could not exercise the service-token gate at all — it was
     a broken test, not a behaviour change. IsTunnelService means even that path is refused (403), and the
     wire path gives the contracted 401.
  2. test_the_key_is_never_logged gained an assertion that the response is the debugg one, so it cannot
     pass vacuously on the ngrok path (already noted in 2.1).

SECRETS — WHAT THE TUNNEL SERVICE ACTUALLY NEEDS (for the infra arc; deploy/prod/reconcile_task_secrets.py
injects the whole 42-key bundle per family, so a naive "tunnel" entry would hand the tunnel server every
prod credential):
  * The tunnel server needs EXACTLY ONE secret: TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN. Nothing else — no DB credentials,
    no AWS keys, no OpenAI/Stripe/ngrok/browser-mgr values. It talks to sentinal only over
    /api/internal/tunnels/* with that bearer token, and to Redis for the revoke channel.
  * The debuggai-api DJANGO family needs the SAME TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN value (it is the verifier). The
    celery-worker / celery-beat / celery-browser families do NOT need it: nothing off the request path
    reads it.
  * Everything else the tunnel feature needs is plain non-secret env, not bundle material:
    TUNNEL_DOMAINS, TUNNEL_DEBUGG_DOMAIN, TUNNEL_RELAY_URL, TUNNEL_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
    TUNNEL_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS, TUNNEL_REVOKE_CHANNEL, TUNNEL_DEBUGG_ROLLOUT_PERCENT,
    TUNNEL_DEBUGG_COMPANY_SLUGS, TUNNEL_DEBUGG_USER_EMAILS, FEATURE_FLAG_TUNNELS_DEBUGG_TRANSPORT.
  * Value shape: an opaque random string (generate with `python -c "import secrets;print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"`),
    rotatable by setting the new value on django first and the tunnel server second (verify compares one
    value, so rotation is a two-step deploy or a brief 401 window).
  * I did NOT edit deploy/prod/task-secrets.json — that file is the infra arc's.

NO REGRESSIONS IN THE APPS I TOUCHED (same container): agents, brains, projects, e2es all green.
core is 48 failed / 424 passed / 31 errors — IDENTICAL on a pristine `git archive HEAD` tree in the same
container (test_canary_gate.py's 48 NotImplementedError "sentinal-51ggh.6 (4.1)" is somebody else's red,
and the 31 errors are deploy/* tests that need the repo root, which this backend-only mount does not have).
POST-REVIEW FIXES (two defects no test covered, both found in review after the suite was green):
1. RATE LIMIT ON THE INTERNAL API (blocker). @api_view applies DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES unless overridden, so verify/ and closed/ carried AnonRateThrottle + UserRateThrottle at 2000/hour — and because the service principal is an AnonymousUser, BOTH key on the caller's IP, i.e. the one or two tunnel-server task IPs. Every connect, reconnect and periodic re-verify of every live tunnel shared one bucket (~100 tunnels re-verifying on a few-minute interval reaches 2000/hour by itself), after which DRF answers 429 before the view runs and healthy tunnels look unverifiable. Confirmed by reading verify_tunnel.cls.throttle_classes. Fixed with @throttle_classes([]) on both internal views (service-authenticated, VPC-only, nginx-blocked — a rate limit buys nothing) and pinned by test_the_internal_endpoints_are_not_rate_limited.
2. UNBOUNDED REDIS PUBLISH. publish_revoked ran redis.Redis.from_url with no socket timeouts, and transaction.on_commit runs it synchronously while the user's revoke commits — so a black-holed Redis (dropped packets, not a refusal) would HANG the response instead of failing fast into tunnel.revoke_publish_failed. Added TUNNEL_REDIS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (env.float, default 2.0, next to the other TUNNEL_* settings — no magic numbers) and passed it as socket_connect_timeout + socket_timeout; pinned by test_the_revoke_publish_is_time_bounded.
3. Nit: @extend_schema(exclude=True) on both internal views so the internal surface is not advertised at /api/v1/docs/. Verified: 'api/internal' appears 0 times in the generated schema, the schema still generates (exit 0), and the only drf-spectacular warnings naming tunnels are the same 'unable to guess serializer / could not resolve authenticator' ones the provision endpoint ALREADY produced on the pristine tree.
After the fixes: backend/tunnels + the projects mirror = 90 passed; flake8 0, black/isort clean, makemigrations --check clean, manage.py check clean, and backend/tests still fails exactly the same 3 pre-existing ids.
close_reason: Core implementation green: 88/88 tunnel tests pass (issue/verify/revoke/closed, transport negotiation behind the flag, TUNNEL_DOMAINS consumers, Law #4 events).
