title: [tunnel-tokens] 1.1 User Requirements
description:
Capture who the user is, the problem, acceptance criteria (when is this done?), and non-goals. Pre-filled below from the design and the owner's decisions: confirm or adjust, then record with `bd update <id> --notes=...` and close.

Arc specifics:
- Who: MCP users (through the MCP) and the tunnel server.
- Problem: tunnel credentials come from ngrok today (a Service User plus an API key per session in
  core/services/ngrok_api.py, a shared-key fallback, and a sweeper that misses keys). The debugg API must
  issue and scope its own tunnel tokens, the way it scoped ngrok keys.
- Acceptance: the MCP still calls POST api/v1/tunnels/ with the user's API key and gets credentials the
  tunnel server accepts; tokens are scoped to the user, expire for new connects, and can be revoked only by
  their owner; the tunnel server can verify a token; old MCP clients keep getting ngrok until removal; the
  backend chooses the transport per request behind a flag, so rollout and rollback need no MCP release;
  every tunnel is recorded; tunnel.debugg.ai hosts are recognized everywhere ngrok.debugg.ai hosts are.
- Non-goals: public tunnels, per-port hostnames, removing ngrok code (rollout arc).

Repo: platform/sentinal. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §2 and §6. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.2.
notes:
1.1 USER REQUIREMENTS — CONFIRMED against sentinal origin/staging @ 5798f66c (worktree platform/.worktrees/tunnel-tokens, branch tunnel/tokens). Paths are relative to backend/.

WHO
- MCP users, through the MCP: MCP calls POST api/v1/tunnels/ with the user's API key (debugg-ai-mcp services/tunnels.ts:131; header "Authorization: Token <key>" or "Bearer <oauth>" per utils/axiosTransport.ts:42). The MCP transport snake_cases request bodies and camelCases responses (axiosTransport.ts:47,78).
- The debugg tunnel server (tunnel-server arc): verifies tokens on connect/reconnect, learns about revokes.
- Ops: needs to roll out / roll back the transport server-side and see what happened.

PROBLEM (verified)
- Today POST api/v1/tunnels/ (backend/tunnels/api/views.py:16-64, mounted config/urls.py:53) calls ngrok_api_service.safe_provision (core/services/ngrok_api.py:207) which creates an ngrok Service User per user (:68-107) and an ngrok API key per session (:113-178).
- Shared-key fallback: NGROK_TUNNEL_BOT_KEY when NGROK_ADMIN_API_KEY is unset (:129-136) or on any ngrok API error (:215-227).
- The sweeper misses keys (core/tasks.py:270, beat every 15 min at config/settings/base.py:745-747). Two concrete causes: (a) the tracking cache entry lives only ttl+300s (ngrok_api.py:162-166), so for a 1h key it expires 5 min after the key does, but the sweep runs every 15 min, so most expired keys lose their tracking entry before any sweep sees them; (b) prod cache has IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS=True (config/settings/production.py:100), so a failed tracking write is silently dropped.
- The tunnelId is str(uuid4()) generated in the view and thrown away (views.py:53); nothing records tunnels.
- Legacy revoke POST api/v1/ngrok/revoke/ (users/api/views.py:930-957, router config/api_router.py:270) revokes ANY key id with no ownership check. The MCP calls it with {ngrokKeyId} (debugg-ai-mcp services/index.ts:586-588).

ACCEPTANCE (confirmed, with corrections)
1. The MCP still calls POST api/v1/tunnels/ with the user's API key and gets credentials the debugg tunnel server accepts.
2. Tokens are scoped to the user, expire for NEW connects/reconnects (not for a live connection), and a live tunnel ends at revoke, client disconnect, or a hard max lifetime.
3. A tunnel can be revoked only by its owner (another user gets 404, same as not-found).
4. The tunnel server can verify a token through an internal, service-authenticated endpoint; the debugg API is the only authority on tokens.
5. Old MCP clients (no `transports` in the body) keep getting today's ngrok response UNCHANGED (same keys, same order, same value formats) until ngrok removal.
6. The backend picks the transport per request behind the existing flag/config mechanism, so rollout and rollback need no MCP release.
7. Every tunnel is recorded (decision: this includes ngrok provisions, see 1.2).
8. tunnel.debugg.ai hosts are recognized everywhere ngrok.debugg.ai hosts are (host recognition, redaction, brain prompt text).

CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD / DESIGN TEXT
- evidence_scope: TUNNEL_HOST_SUFFIXES is at projects/evidence_scope.py:39 (36 is the comment). The module is PURE ON PURPOSE (no Django import at module scope; scripts/dryrun_evidence_attribution_v6r5_4.py loads it by file path). A Django TUNNEL_DOMAINS setting therefore CANNOT drive it directly; see 1.2 for the resolution.
- environment_resolver has no host list of its own: it imports is_tunnel_host/is_local_target from evidence_scope (projects/services/environment_resolver.py:41-50, used at :84, :229, :543-544). One fix in evidence_scope covers both.
- Redaction regexes are at agents/models.py:777 (Message.static_get_cleaned_tickked_content; 775 is the comment) and core/chat_formatting/templates.py:351-353 (ChatTemplate.sanitize_content; 349 is the comment).
- Brain prompt text: e2es/models.py:44 (GENERIC_TEST_DESCRIPTION), brains/factories.py:82 (App Evaluator _CORRECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT) and :332 (E2E Test Executor template). TRAP: editing these strings does NOT reach existing DB rows. for_app_evaluation only rewrites the stored prompt when "call the done action IMMEDIATELY" is missing (factories.py:102), which the current prod prompt already contains; E2E brains are company-scoped copies of a template made once (factories.py:299-356; template copy at :352); GENERIC_TEST_DESCRIPTION is baked into each E2eTest.agent_task_description at save (e2es/models.py:202,282). Requirement therefore includes a reconcile/migration path, not just a string edit (see 1.2).
- react-web-app/utils/url-utils.ts:18,38 is NOT in sentinal: it is the separate repo github.com/debugg-ai/react-web-app (owner checkout platform/react-web-app on staging). Out of this worktree; change + test plan recorded in 1.2, flagged to owner.
- Not listed in the design, found by grep: e2es/services/target_url_resolver.py:120 and :421 (ngrok URL build + _is_default_ngrok) and e2es/consumers.py:313 ('ngrok' substring check). All are in the RETIRED e2es app (CLAUDE.md, 2026-08-06) and serve legacy flows that stay on ngrok -> no change (design §6 allows "leave them on ngrok until they're retired").
- Verified domain-agnostic, no change needed: graphs/models/page.py _host_is_internal_or_env_own uses the crawl's exact entry host (extra_env_hosts), not a domain list.
- tunnels is not a registered Django app today (not in LOCAL_APPS, config/settings/base.py:164-190; no apps.py/models.py/migrations). Adding the Tunnel model requires registering it.
- No test exists today for POST api/v1/tunnels/ (grep of backend/ for tunnels-provision/api/v1/tunnels in tests: none). The old-client guard must be written from scratch.

NON-GOALS (confirmed)

title: [tunnel-tokens] 1.2 System Requirements
description:
Turn the user requirements into technical constraints: API contracts, data model, performance, security, integration points. Pre-filled below: confirm or adjust, record in notes, close.

Arc specifics:
- Model `Tunnel` in backend/tunnels/: id (uuid, also the hostname label), user FK, purpose, token_hash
  (SHA-256), created_at, expires_at (default +1h; bounds connects and reconnects), max_expires_at (+24h hard
  cap), revoked_at, connected_at, closed_at, client_version. Follow sentinal Law #2: the transport switch uses
  the existing flag/config mechanism, not a boolean field.
- POST api/v1/tunnels/ {purpose, transports?}. If "debugg" is offered AND the flag selects it, return
  {tunnelId, tunnelKey, keyId=tunnelId, expiresAt, transport:"debugg",
  relayUrl:"wss://api.debugg.ai/tunnel/v1/connect", tunnelDomain:"tunnel.debugg.ai"}. Otherwise return
  today's ngrok response, unchanged.
- tunnelKey: 32 random bytes, url-safe, returned once, stored only as a hash, compared in constant time.
- POST api/v1/tunnels/<id>/revoke/: owner only (404 for anyone else), idempotent, sets revoked_at, publishes
  `tunnel.revoked <id>` on Redis (redis.debuggai-api.local).
- POST /api/internal/tunnels/verify/ {tunnelId, tunnelKey, event: connect|reverify} → {ok, userId, expiresAt,
  maxExpiresAt} or {ok:false, reason}. Service auth with TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN (Secrets Manager; add to
  deploy/prod/task-secrets.json). Sets connected_at on connect. The public nginx must ALSO block
  /api/internal/ (infra arc).
- Optional POST /api/internal/tunnels/closed/ from the tunnel server sets closed_at.
- A TUNNEL_DOMAINS setting (default ["ngrok.debugg.ai", "tunnel.debugg.ai"]) drives:
  projects/evidence_scope.py:36 TUNNEL_HOST_SUFFIXES; projects/services/environment_resolver.py; redaction in
  agents/models.py:775 and core/chat_formatting/templates.py:349; the brain prompt's tunnel-error text in
  e2es/models.py:44 and brains/factories.py:82,332 (name the DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* markers);
  react-web-app/utils/url-utils.ts:18,38.
- Law #4 events: tunnel.provisioned / connected / revoked / closed / verify_failed.

Repo: platform/sentinal. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §2 and §6. Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.2.
notes:
1.2 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS / PUBLISHED CONTRACTS — verified against sentinal @ 5798f66c. These shapes are what the tunnel-server arc (xkoh.3) and the MCP-client arc write tests against. Wire casing: request bodies from the MCP arrive snake_case (its axios transport snake_cases every body); the tunnels responses are hand-built camelCase and stay camelCase (the MCP camelCases responses, so camelCase in = camelCase out). The internal endpoints take camelCase (their client is the tunnel server, which has no case interceptor).

== A. DATA MODEL ==
backend/tunnels/models.py: class Tunnel(backend.core.models.BaseModel)  [BaseModel gives: int pk `id`, `uuid` (unique, default uuid4), `key`, `last_mod`, `timestamp` (auto_now_add) — `timestamp` IS created_at; `uuid` IS the tunnelId and the hostname label]
  user           FK(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=CASCADE, related_name="tunnels")
  transport      CharField(max_length=16, choices=Transport.choices)   # TextChoices NGROK="ngrok", DEBUGG="debugg" — a choice, NOT a boolean (Law #2)
  purpose        CharField(max_length=64, blank=True, default="")
  token_hash     CharField(max_length=64, blank=True, default="")      # sha256 hex of the plaintext; "" for ngrok rows. NOT indexed: lookup is by uuid, then constant-time compare.
  expires_at     DateTimeField()                                        # bounds CONNECTS/RECONNECTS, never a live connection
  max_expires_at DateTimeField()                                        # hard cap; a live tunnel is cut here
  revoked_at     DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
  connected_at   DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)                   # LAST successful connect verify
  closed_at      DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)                   # LAST close reported by the tunnel server
  client_version CharField(max_length=64, blank=True, default="")
  Meta: ordering ["-timestamp"]; Index(fields=["user", "timestamp"]).
Prereq: backend.tunnels must be registered (apps.py + LOCAL_APPS, config/settings/base.py:164-190) — it is only a urls+views include today. Migration: tunnels/migrations/0001_initial.py (new table, no rolling-deploy NOT NULL risk).
DECISION (owner may veto): EVERY provision writes a row, ngrok ones too (epic: "every tunnel is recorded"), which is what lets the rollout see when old clients are gone. ngrok rows: transport="ngrok", token_hash="", expires_at/max_expires_at from the same settings. The ngrok response bytes do not change.

== B. POST /api/v1/tunnels/  (provision — unchanged mount, unchanged auth: @permission_classes([IsAuthenticated]), default auth chain = JWT | Token | OAuth2, no required_token_scopes) ==
Request body (all optional): {"purpose": "workflow", "transports": ["debugg","ngrok"], "client_version": "3.7.1"}
 - transports = what the CLIENT supports, preference ignored (the server chooses). Unknown names are ignored.
 - transports absent, null, or [] == an OLD client.
 - transports present but not a list of strings -> 400 {"detail":"transports must be a list of strings"}.
 - purpose non-string or >64 chars -> 400 {"detail":"purpose must be a string of at most 64 characters"}.
Selection: debugg is chosen iff "debugg" is offered AND select_debugg_transport(user) is true (see D). Else ngrok, iff "ngrok" is offered or transports was absent/empty. Neither available (e.g. transports=["debugg"] with the flag off) -> 400 {"detail":"No supported tunnel transport offered","code":"no_supported_transport"}.

B1. OLD CLIENT (no transports) — 200, BYTE-IDENTICAL to today, exactly these four keys in this order:
{"tunnelId":"<uuid4 str>","tunnelKey":"<ngrok api key>","keyId":"<ak_... or null>","expiresAt":"<isoformat with +00:00, or null>"}
 - expiresAt is Python datetime.isoformat() on a UTC-aware datetime -> "2026-09-19T15:04:05.123456+00:00" (NOT "...Z" — the current view docstring and the design doc are both wrong about this; the ngrok path must not move).
 - No "transport" key. Adding one is the regression the snapshot test exists to catch.
 - 503 {"detail":"Tunnel provisioning is unavailable. Contact support if this persists."} when no ngrok token is configured — unchanged.

B2. NEW CLIENT, ngrok selected — 200, today's four keys PLUS "transport":"ngrok". (The client asked, so it is told.)

B3. NEW CLIENT, debugg selected — 200:
{"tunnelId":"<Tunnel.uuid>","tunnelKey":"<43-char url-safe secret>","keyId":"<same as tunnelId>","expiresAt":"<iso+00:00>","maxExpiresAt":"<iso+00:00>","transport":"debugg","relayUrl":"wss://api.debugg.ai/tunnel/v1/connect","tunnelDomain":"tunnel.debugg.ai"}
 - tunnelKey = secrets.token_urlsafe(32) -> 43 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; returned ONCE; only sha256 hex is stored; never logged.
 - The browser-facing URL the MCP builds is https://<tunnelId>.<tunnelDomain> (nginx matches ^[a-z0-9-]+\.tunnel\.debugg\.ai$, which a uuid4 satisfies).
 - relayUrl/tunnelDomain come from settings so staging/prod differ without a client change.
 - No ngrok call is made on this path.
Events: tunnel.provisioned {tunnel_id, user_id, transport, purpose, client_version, offered_transports}.

== C. POST /api/v1/tunnels/<uuid:tunnel_id>/revoke/  (same auth as provision; no body) ==
 200 {"tunnelId":"<uuid>","revoked":true,"revokedAt":"<iso+00:00>"}  — idempotent: a second call returns 200 with the ORIGINAL revokedAt and publishes nothing.
 404 {"detail":"Not found."} — unknown id OR owned by another user (indistinguishable); the row is not modified.
 401 when unauthenticated.
 First revoke only: revoked_at=now; for transport="debugg", publish on Redis (see E) via transaction.on_commit; event tunnel.revoked {tunnel_id,user_id,transport}. A publish failure never fails the request: event tunnel.revoke_publish_failed {tunnel_id,error} (the tunnel server re-verifies every few minutes, so Redis is only the fast path).
 ngrok rows: revoked_at is set, nothing is published, no ngrok API call (the legacy /api/v1/ngrok/revoke/ still owns ngrok keys).

== D. TRANSPORT SELECTION (the existing flag/config mechanism — Law #2: no boolean on the model) ==
 Master switch: backend.core.feature_flags flag "tunnels.debugg_transport" (FeatureFlags.DEFAULTS False; env FEATURE_FLAG_TUNNELS_DEBUGG_TRANSPORT; settings FEATURE_FLAGS entry; set_flag() runtime override for tests). OFF -> ngrok for everyone. That is the rollback.
 ON -> debugg for a user iff any of:
   - user.company.slug in settings.TUNNEL_DEBUGG_COMPANY_SLUGS  (list, default []; mirrors AUTO_TRIAGE_INTERNAL_COMPANY_SLUGS, config/settings/base.py:3486)
   - user.email (casefolded) in settings.TUNNEL_DEBUGG_USER_EMAILS (list, default [])
   - stable bucket of the user: int(sha256(str(user.uuid)).hexdigest()[:8],16) % 100 < settings.TUNNEL_DEBUGG_ROLLOUT_PERCENT (int, default 0). Same user -> same answer forever; 100 = everyone.
 OPEN QUESTION for the owner (does not change any wire contract): the existing flag mechanism is a global boolean only; percentage + allowlists above are the added config. Confirm "on/off + internal allowlist + percent" is what you want.

== E. REDIS REVOKE MESSAGE (tunnel-server arc consumes this) ==
 Connection: redis.Redis.from_url(settings.REDIS_URL) — prod REDIS_URL is the rc Cloud Map redis (redis.debuggai-api.local:6379/0, config/settings/production.py:75). NOTE: REDIS_URL is currently defined ONLY in production.py:75 and test.py:94, so base.py needs REDIS_URL = env("REDIS_URL", default=CELERY_BROKER_URL) or settings.REDIS_URL raises AttributeError under config.settings.local.
 Channel: settings.TUNNEL_REVOKE_CHANNEL, default "tunnel.revoked" (plain PUBLISH, not a channels group).
 Payload: UTF-8 JSON, compact separators, exactly:
   {"event":"tunnel.revoked","tunnelId":"<uuid>","revokedAt":"<iso+00:00>"}
 Consumers must ignore unknown tunnelIds and tolerate duplicates; a missed message is covered by re-verify.

== F. INTERNAL VERIFY (the tunnel server's only authority on tokens) ==
 POST /api/internal/tunnels/verify/
 Service auth: header "Authorization: Bearer <settings.TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN>", compared with secrets.compare_digest. The view pins its own authentication_classes (a user JWT/API token must NOT authenticate here) and returns 401 {"detail":"Invalid tunnel service token."} with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer on a missing/wrong/blank token or when TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN is unset (fail closed). TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN is a Secrets Manager value (bundle name for the infra arc: TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN in deploy/prod/task-secrets.json) — same shared-secret shape as the existing SURFER_API_SECRET (config/settings/base.py:3140). Never routed publicly: the public nginx server blocks must 404/403 /api/internal/ (infra arc) — the token is not the only guard.
 Request (camelCase): {"tunnelId":"<uuid>","tunnelKey":"<plaintext>","event":"connect"|"reverify"}  — event optional, default "connect".
 200 OK:      {"ok":true,"tunnelId":"<uuid>","userId":"<user.uuid>","expiresAt":"<iso+00:00>","maxExpiresAt":"<iso+00:00>"}
 200 rejected:{"ok":false,"reason":"<code>"}  with reason ∈ unknown | bad_key | revoked | max_lifetime | expired
   checked in this order: unknown (no such uuid, malformed uuid, or transport != "debugg") -> bad_key (constant-time mismatch) -> revoked -> max_lifetime (now >= max_expires_at, BOTH events) -> expired (now >= expires_at, event="connect" ONLY; a live tunnel is never cut at the hour).
 400 {"ok":false,"reason":"bad_request","detail":"..."} for a missing/blank tunnelId or tunnelKey or an unknown event value.
 Side effects: event="connect" and ok -> connected_at=now (last connect wins) + event tunnel.connected {tunnel_id,user_id}. Rejections -> event tunnel.verify_failed {tunnel_id,reason,event}. A successful reverify writes nothing and emits nothing (one call per tunnel every few minutes).

== G. INTERNAL CLOSED (optional in the bead; in v1 so closed_at is ever set) ==
 POST /api/internal/tunnels/closed/ — same service auth.
 Request: {"tunnelId":"<uuid>","reason":"<free text, optional>"}
 200 {"ok":true} (sets closed_at=now, last close wins, idempotent) | 200 {"ok":false,"reason":"unknown"} | 400 bad_request | 401 as above.
 Event: tunnel.closed {tunnel_id, reason}.

== H. LIFETIME / SETTINGS (no magic numbers) ==
 TUNNEL_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS      env.int, default 3600   -> expires_at = created + ttl
 TUNNEL_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS   env.int, default 86400  -> max_expires_at = created + max
 TUNNEL_RELAY_URL              env,     default "wss://api.debugg.ai/tunnel/v1/connect"
 TUNNEL_DEBUGG_DOMAIN          env,     default "tunnel.debugg.ai"
 TUNNEL_DOMAINS                env.list,default ["ngrok.debugg.ai","tunnel.debugg.ai"] (every tunnel domain sentinal must RECOGNIZE)
 TUNNEL_REVOKE_CHANNEL         env,     default "tunnel.revoked"
 TUNNEL_SERVICE_TOKEN          env,     default "" (secret)
 TUNNEL_DEBUGG_ROLLOUT_PERCENT env.int, default 0 ; TUNNEL_DEBUGG_COMPANY_SLUGS / TUNNEL_DEBUGG_USER_EMAILS env.list, default []
 FEATURE_FLAGS["tunnels.debugg_transport"] default False.

== I. HOST RECOGNITION (design §6) ==
 - projects/evidence_scope.py:39 TUNNEL_HOST_SUFFIXES gains "tunnel.debugg.ai" AS A LITERAL. The module is Django-free on purpose (a raw-psycopg prod script loads it by path), so settings.TUNNEL_DOMAINS cannot drive it — instead a test asserts every settings.TUNNEL_DOMAINS entry satisfies is_tunnel_host(), which keeps the two in step the same way _INTERNAL_HOST_SUFFIXES is kept in step with graphs.models.page. CONSEQUENCE: a per-env tunnel domain (e.g. a staging-only "tunnel.st.debugg.ai") would need the literal added too — flag to the infra arc: staging is expected to reuse tunnel.debugg.ai on its own private zone.
 - projects/services/environment_resolver.py needs NO domain change (it imports is_tunnel_host/is_local_target); its behaviour must be covered by tests anyway: a *.tunnel.debugg.ai target resolves to the project's "Local Development" environment and re-addresses it each session.
 - Redaction, both driven by settings.TUNNEL_DOMAINS: agents/models.py:777 (regex https://[a-zA-Z0-9-]+\.<domain>) and core/chat_formatting/templates.py:351-353 (keep the existing ngrok.app / ngrok.io patterns, add the TUNNEL_DOMAINS ones).
 - Brain prompt tunnel-error text names the markers DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE / DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED / DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN alongside ngrok, at brains/factories.py:82 and :332 and e2es/models.py:44. Because a string edit does not reach existing rows (1.1), the requirement includes: for_app_evaluation's reconcile predicate (factories.py:102) must also fire when the stored prompt lacks "DEBUGG_TUNNEL". Existing company-scoped E2E brains and already-saved E2eTest.agent_task_description rows are NOT back-filled in v1 (a data migration for the retired e2es surface is out of scope) — recorded as an accepted gap.
 - react-web-app (SEPARATE REPO github.com/debugg-ai/react-web-app, NOT sentinal) utils/url-utils.ts:18,38: ensureHttpsForNgrok/needsHttpsConversion match on url.includes("ngrok.app"|"ngrok.debugg.ai"|"ngrok.io"). Change: replace both inline lists with one exported const TUNNEL_DOMAINS = ["ngrok.app","ngrok.io","ngrok.debugg.ai","tunnel.debugg.ai"] and test it with jest (repo already runs `npm run test:unit`): a new utils/url-utils.test.ts asserting http://x.tunnel.debugg.ai is upgraded when window.location.protocol is https:, that ngrok hosts still are, and that an unrelated host is untouched. NOT done in this arc — no worktree taken (node_modules make one non-cheap); flagged to the owner.

== J. OBSERVABILITY (Law #4) ==
 Events are structured log records on logger "backend.tunnels" (helper emit_tunnel_event(name, **fields) -> log.info(name, extra={"event": name, **fields})), asserted in tests with caplog on record.event: tunnel.provisioned, tunnel.connected, tunnel.revoked, tunnel.revoke_publish_failed, tunnel.closed, tunnel.verify_failed. No event, log message or model field ever carries the plaintext tunnelKey.

== K. SECURITY / PERFORMANCE CONSTRAINTS ==
 - Plaintext token: 32 random bytes url-safe, returned once, stored only as sha256 hex, compared with secrets.compare_digest, never logged.
 - Verify is one DB read by uuid (+ one write on connect); roughly one call per session plus reconnects plus a re-verify every few minutes per live tunnel.
 - Provision adds one INSERT to a path that already does auth DB work; the ngrok path keeps its existing external call and its existing failure behaviour.
 - Revoke and verify are owner/service scoped; the 404-for-other-users rule must not leak existence.
CONTRACT CORRECTION (2026-09-19, after review) — §B: DELETE the rule '400 when purpose is not a string or is longer than 64 chars'. It was wrong and would have broken acceptance #5: provision_tunnel never reads purpose today, so ANY value returns 200 right now, and rejecting one would make a currently-working old-client request start failing. Worse, because every provision now records a Tunnel row and Tunnel.purpose is varchar(64) with no Django-side validation on .create(), an over-long purpose would have turned a 200 into a Postgres DataError 500.
CORRECT RULE: purpose and client_version are COERCED, never rejected — a non-string becomes "", anything longer than 64 characters is truncated to 64. Only `transports` can produce a 400 (an old client never sends it, so no old request can start failing).
Guarded by two tests added to backend/tunnels/tests/test_provision_contract.py: test_an_odd_purpose_is_coerced_not_rejected (200 + unchanged key list for a 200-char purpose, a dict, an int and null; stored purpose <= 64 chars) and test_an_odd_client_version_is_coerced_not_rejected. Both are red today only on the recorded-row assertion (Tunnel.DoesNotExist).
CONTRACT CHANGE (owner, 2026-09-19) — §F verify: expires_at gates the FIRST connect ONLY. A tunnel whose connected_at is set keeps reconnecting until max_expires_at; otherwise a tunnel-server deploy would kill every session whose token is older than an hour. Accepted events are now connect | reconnect | reverify (default connect); 'reconnect' is an explicit alias and the rule is state-based either way, so 'expired' can only be returned for a token that has NEVER connected. revoked and max_lifetime still apply to every event, and the check order is unchanged: unknown -> bad_key -> revoked -> max_lifetime -> expired(first connect only).
OPERATIONAL NOTE for the tunnel-server arc (from 4.1 review): /api/internal/tunnels/verify/ and /closed/ are NOT rate limited (throttle_classes([])), so the server may verify on every connect/reconnect and re-verify live tunnels on its own interval without hitting a 429. They are also excluded from the public OpenAPI schema. The revoke publish is bounded by TUNNEL_REDIS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 2.0s) — if Redis is slow or black-holed the publish is dropped and evented, so the server's periodic re-verify remains the real backstop.
close_reason: Contracts published and verified against the code: provision (old-client byte-identical vs debugg shape), revoke, internal verify + closed with Bearer service token, Redis tunnel.revoked message, Tunnel model, settings/flag, host-recognition plan. One non-blocking owner question recorded (flag granularity).

In debugg-ai-mcp: `npm test`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`.

title: [tunnel-protocol] 2.1 Write Failing Unit Tests
description:
Write a unit test for each system requirement (happy path, edge cases, errors). Tests compile but FAIL (red), because the implementation doesn't exist yet. Run them, paste the failure summary into notes.

Arc specifics:
- codec round-trips every frame type; truncated, oversized and unknown-type frames → PROTOCOL_ERROR
- encoding matches vectors/*.json byte-for-byte
- flow control: sender stops at window 0 and resumes on WINDOW; never sends past credit; memory stays
  bounded with a slow reader
- half-close in each direction; RST mid-stream frees the stream and errors both ends
- fairness: a 10 MB stream doesn't delay a 1 KB stream opened after it by more than one frame
- stream cap enforced (RST on overflow)
- PING/PONG; peer marked dead after 60 s silence (fake timers)
- GOAWAY: new OPENs refused, open streams drain
- handshake rejects an unsupported protocol version

Repo: debugg-ai-mcp. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3 (wire protocol). Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.1.
notes:
FAILING UNIT TESTS WRITTEN (red, for the right reason)

Files (all new):
- `__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol/helpers.ts`        test support, NOT a test file
- `__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol/codec.test.ts`               133 tests
- `__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol/handshake.test.ts`            46 tests
- `__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol/session.streams.test.ts`      21 tests
- `__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol/session.flowControl.test.ts`   8 tests
- `__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol/session.liveness.test.ts`     17 tests
Stubs added so the tests compile (types + signatures, every function throws
`not implemented`; constants.ts and errors.ts are data so they are complete):
  services/tunnel/protocol/{constants,errors,codec,transport,stream,session,handshake,index}.ts
Conformance vectors (real, hand-computed, not placeholders):
  services/tunnel/protocol/vectors/frames.json          32 vectors (29 encode+decode, 3 decode-only)
  services/tunnel/protocol/vectors/invalid-frames.json  41 vectors, each must raise PROTOCOL_ERROR
  services/tunnel/protocol/vectors/handshake.json       16 vectors

RESULT
  node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js `__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol`
  Test Suites: 5 failed, 5 total
  Tests:       224 failed, 1 passed, 225 total
The one pass is "has vectors for every frame type", which only reads the vector
file. Every one of the 224 failures traces to the stubs: a tally of the run's
error lines is 448 x "not implemented" (each failure prints it twice) plus 56 x
"Received constructor: Error" from `expect(...).toThrow(ProtocolError)` catching
the stub's plain Error. Zero TypeError / ReferenceError / timeout / module-
resolution failures, i.e. nothing fails because a test is broken.

Full suite: `npm test` -> Test Suites 13 failed, 72 passed; Tests 305 failed,
1136 passed, 1 skipped. The 13 failures are exactly the new red files: these 5
plus 8 belonging to the mcp-client arc (debuggTransport, tunnelManager.transport,
tunnels.transport, localReachability.probe, tunnelDisposition.debugg,
tunnelDomains, and 2 integration files). Every pre-existing suite still passes.
`npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.

ts-jest is transpile-only here (tsconfig has isolatedModules: true), and the repo
tsconfig EXCLUDES `__tests__`, so neither `npm test` nor `npx tsc --noEmit` type
checks a test file. Verified separately with a standalone tsconfig covering
`__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol/**` + services/tunnel/protocol/**: clean, and
confirmed it really covers those 14 files by planting a type error and watching
it fail. Worth knowing for 4.1: a type error in these tests is invisible to CI.

WHAT THE TESTS PIN (beyond the bead's list)
- codec: byte-for-byte vectors both ways; decode-only vectors for JSON whitespace
  and unknown-field dropping; every invalid vector raises ProtocolError with code
  PROTOCOL_ERROR; round trips incl. max DATA payload, max stream id, max u64
  nonce, unicode GOAWAY reason; the ENCODER refuses anything a peer would have to
  reject; decode honours a non-zero byteOffset (ws hands out pooled Buffers).
- SSRF: an OPEN carrying target/addr/host/port/upstream decodes to {kind} only,
  and the encoder drops those fields too. A PROBE whose path is an absolute URL
  (169.254.169.254) is a PROTOCOL_ERROR.
- handshake: header building (and that the key appears in no header but
  Authorization), version negotiation incl. a repeated header and a multi-version
  offer, all 16 server-side vectors, 426-before-401 ordering, and the client-side
  interpretation of 101/400/401/426/429/5xx incl. which are retryable.
- session/streams: id allocation, metadata whitelisting, half close in each
  direction, 64 KiB framing, RST with the code the resetter chose (incl.
  UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE), unknown RST codes normalising to RESET, frames for a
  closed stream discarded, DATA after END resetting only that stream, the 256
  cap in both directions, and 8 session-fatal protocol violations each checked to
  send GOAWAY(PROTOCOL_ERROR) and close 4004.
- session/flow control: stop at window 0 and resume on WINDOW, never exceed
  granted credit, MAX_UNACKED_SEND_BYTES bound on the socket, a piped producer
  held back instead of buffered, receive buffering capped at one window, an
  over-run window resetting just that stream, credit granted only as the app
  consumes, and fairness (a 10 MB stream delays a 1 KB stream by at most one
  frame).
- session/liveness: PONG echo, 20s self-ping, RTT, dead peer at 60s with fake
  timers (setImmediate left real so transports still deliver), any inbound frame
  proving life, GOAWAY drain-then-close-1000, drain deadline RSTs, REVOKED,
  refusing OPENs after our own GOAWAY, PROBE round trip / concurrent matching /
  TIMEOUT-never-hangs / server-side handler / handler failure, and an abrupt
  socket loss failing every stream and settling every pending call.

NOTE FOR 4.1: test helpers build and parse frames with plain Buffer arithmetic
straight from the spec, deliberately NOT through codec.ts, so a session failure
never means "the codec is broken" and the hand-rolled builder is a second opinion
on the codec.
close_reason: 225 unit tests across 5 files, 224 red because the stubs throw 'not implemented' (verified: no TypeError/ReferenceError/timeout in the run) and 1 green vector-coverage check. Conformance vectors are real and hand-computed. Pre-existing suite still fully green; tsc --noEmit clean; tests type-checked separately since ts-jest is transpile-only here.

title: [tunnel-protocol] 3.1 Technical Strategy
description:
With the failing suite as the definition of correct, decide: patterns (and why), build vs reuse, which tests go green first, risks and mitigations, and the rollback plan. Record with `--design`.

Arc specifics:
Starting point to confirm: build our own yamux-style mux on `ws` (there's no maintained pure-TS mux over
WS that fits, and yamux's semantics are proven). Make the codec green first, then flow control, then the
session. Main risk: backpressure bugs → unbounded buffers (mitigated by the memory-bound tests). Rollback:
none needed, this is a library with nothing deployed.

Repo: debugg-ai-mcp. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3 (wire protocol). Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.1.
design:
TECHNICAL STRATEGY — debugg tunnel wire protocol v1
(Definition of correct = the 232 red tests from 2.1/2.2: 225 unit + 7 integration.)

BUILD, NOT REUSE — confirmed, with the alternatives that were considered
- A yamux-style credit multiplexer over one websocket, written here in ~600 lines
  of TypeScript with zero runtime dependencies (node: built-ins only).
- Rejected: @chainsafe/libp2p-yamux — the right semantics, but it speaks libp2p's
  it-stream duplexes rather than node streams, drags in a libp2p dependency tree,
  and ties our tunnel to libp2p's release cadence. We need node Duplexes, because
  both ends do nothing but `socket.pipe(stream).pipe(socket)`.
- Rejected: node's own http2 as the multiplexer. It cannot run over a websocket,
  only over a raw TCP/TLS socket — and a raw socket is exactly what we are giving
  up to get through nginx and the ALB on 443.
- Rejected: multiplex / mux-demux / spdy-transport — unmaintained, and none has
  per-stream credit flow control, which is the one property this whole arc exists
  for.
- Rejected: socket.io / SockJS — message frameworks, not byte streams; they would
  make "raw bytes, Host header untouched" impossible.
- What we DO reuse is semantics, not code: yamux for window updates and stream
  states, HTTP/2 for the error-code vocabulary and for REFUSED meaning "not
  processed, safe to retry". Both are proven and both are documented, which is
  what makes an independent server-side implementation reviewable.

ORDER THE TESTS GO GREEN (each step is independently useful to a downstream arc)
1. codec.ts against vectors/frames.json + invalid-frames.json. No dependencies,
   and it freezes the wire for the server arc first. (133 tests)
2. handshake.ts against vectors/handshake.json. Pure functions; unblocks the
   server's upgrade path and the client's connect. (46 tests)
3. transport.ts (webSocketTransport) + the session skeleton: frame dispatch,
   direction checks, PING/PONG, dead-peer timer, protocol policing, close paths.
   (most of session.liveness + the policing half of session.streams)
4. stream.ts as a real node Duplex + the session's stream table: OPEN/DATA/END/
   RST, the 256 cap, metadata whitelisting. (session.streams)
5. Flow control: send credit, WINDOW generation on consumption, receive-window
   enforcement. (session.flowControl, first three)
6. The write scheduler: round-robin one frame per stream, control frames ahead of
   DATA, MAX_UNACKED_SEND_BYTES in flight. (the fairness and un-acked tests)
7. GOAWAY drain and PROBE.
8. The integration file last — it needs all of the above at once.

KEY IMPLEMENTATION CHOICES
- TunnelStream extends node's Duplex rather than being a hand-rolled queue, so
  node's own high-water-mark machinery provides producer backpressure and `pipe`
  just works at both ends. Our credit accounting then only has to gate _write.
- The session never touches a websocket: it owns a FrameTransport. That seam is
  what makes the unit tests able to drive frames by hand and to run the 60 s
  dead-peer test under fake timers, and it is also how the tunnel server will
  plug in its own socket without inheriting any client assumptions.
- One writer: all outbound frames go through a single scheduler, so ordering
  invariants (OPEN before its DATA, END after it, control frames ahead of queued
  DATA) live in exactly one place.
- The module imports nothing from this repo outside its own directory — no
  logger, no config, no ws. Diagnostics surface as events. That is a hard rule,
  not a preference: config/index.ts validates DEBUGGAI_API_KEY at import time and
  would fail a tunnel server that merely imported the protocol.

RISKS AND MITIGATIONS
R1 Backpressure bugs buffer a dev server's whole bundle in the heap, silently.
   Mitigated by four memory-bound unit tests plus the integration slow-consumer
   test that asserts on max(produced - consumed), and by leaning on Duplex rather
   than a bespoke buffer.
R2 Fairness vs throughput. One-frame round robin with a 256 KiB un-acked bound
   could cost throughput if the ws send callback is slow. MAX_UNACKED_SEND_BYTES
   is a constant, not a wire field, so it can be tuned against the 200-stream
   integration test without touching the protocol.
R3 Per-stream throughput is capped at window/RTT, about 2.5 MB/s at 100 ms to
   us-east-2. Aggregate scales with concurrency, so a dev page is fine; a single
   huge chunk is the bad case. If it bites, raise INITIAL_WINDOW in v2 through
   the version negotiation that already exists — never by hand-tuning one side.
R4 Stream-state races: a WINDOW or DATA frame in flight when we RST. Handled by
   the spec rule that frames for a closed-but-previously-used id are discarded,
   which is safe because the websocket gives us total ordering. Pinned by a test.
R5 Node stream traps: a Duplex that emits 'error' with no listener throws.
   The session always attaches its own handler, and both consumer arcs must too;
   the tests model that.
R6 ws specifics: pooled Buffers (decode honours byteOffset — pinned), text
   frames (session-fatal), maxPayload, perMessageDeflate off, and send-callback
   semantics for the un-acked bound. All are in the transport adapter, which is
   the only file that knows ws exists.
R7 Drift between this copy and the tunnel server's copy. Answered in 3.2 by
   conformance vectors plus version negotiation.

TEST-FIRST DISCIPLINE FOR 4.1
The vectors are the specification. Implementation may not edit vectors/*.json to
make code pass — a vector change is a protocol change, and once the server has
shipped it needs a version bump. Same for the constants: they are the contract
the server arc is already reading.

ROLLBACK
None required. Nothing imports this module and nothing is deployed, so the
rollback for a bad v1 library is "don't merge it". The deployed-era escape hatch
is the handshake's version list: a server can speak 1 and 2 at once while clients
migrate, which is why negotiation is in v1 rather than deferred.
close_reason: Strategy recorded: build a yamux-style credit mux over ws in-house (libp2p-yamux, http2, multiplex and socket.io each rejected with reasons), green order codec -> handshake -> transport/session skeleton -> streams -> flow control -> scheduler -> GOAWAY/PROBE -> integration, seven risks with mitigations, and the no-rollback-needed position plus the version-negotiation escape hatch.

title: [tunnel-protocol] 3.2 Architecture & Interface Design
description:
Define module boundaries, interface contracts, data flow and file locations. Follow existing patterns in the target repo; don't invent new ones. Record with `--design`.

Arc specifics:
Modules to confirm: codec.ts, stream.ts (a Node Duplex per stream), session.ts, constants.ts, vectors/.
DECIDE AND RECORD how the tunnel server consumes this module: a package subpath export from
@debugg-ai/debugg-ai-mcp, or a vendored copy that must pass the same vectors. The server and
mcp-client arcs depend on this decision.

Repo: debugg-ai-mcp. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3 (wire protocol). Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.1.
design:
ARCHITECTURE AND INTERFACE DESIGN — debugg tunnel wire protocol v1

=== A. MODULE MAP (services/tunnel/protocol/, all files exist as stubs today) ===
  constants.ts   ~230 lines, DATA ONLY and already complete. Versions, frame
                 types, error codes, close codes, limits, timers, header names,
                 tunnel-id pattern, the DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* markers and their HTTP
                 statuses. One source of truth for both repos.
  errors.ts      ProtocolError / StreamResetError / SessionClosedError. Data only,
                 already complete.
  codec.ts       encodeFrame / decodeFrame / frameTypeName, plus the Frame union
                 and the OpenMetadata, ProbeRequest and ProbeResult shapes. Pure
                 and synchronous: no state, no IO, no timers. It is also where the
                 OPEN metadata whitelist lives, so no address can survive a decode.
  handshake.ts   buildHandshakeHeaders / negotiateProtocolVersion /
                 validateHandshakeRequest / interpretHandshakeResponse. Pure
                 functions over header bags. Shape only — it never decides whether
                 a token is real.
  transport.ts   The FrameTransport seam plus webSocketTransport(ws). The ONLY
                 file that knows a websocket exists, and it knows it structurally
                 (a `WebSocketLike` interface), so the package still compiles with
                 no `ws` types present.
  stream.ts      TunnelStream extends node:stream Duplex. One inbound browser
                 connection. Owns its own credit, its half-close state and its
                 metadata.
  session.ts     TunnelSession extends node:events EventEmitter. Owns the
                 transport, the stream table, the write scheduler, flow-control
                 accounting, liveness timers, GOAWAY state and probe correlation.
  index.ts       The public surface. Consumers import from here and nowhere deeper.
  vectors/       frames.json (32), invalid-frames.json (41), handshake.json (16).

Dependency direction is strictly acyclic and inward:
  constants <- errors <- codec <- {handshake, stream, session}
  transport <- session ;  stream <- session ;  everything <- index
No file in this directory imports anything outside it except `node:` built-ins.
That is enforceable by review and is the property that makes both the vendoring
decision below and the tunnel server's embedding safe.

=== B. INTERFACE CONTRACTS (frozen by the 2.1/2.2 tests) ===
codec.ts
  type Frame = OPEN | DATA | END | RST | WINDOW | PING | PONG | GOAWAY | PROBE | PROBE_RESULT
  encodeFrame(frame: Frame): Uint8Array        // throws ProtocolError on anything illegal
  decodeFrame(bytes: Uint8Array): Frame        // throws ProtocolError; honours byteOffset
handshake.ts
  buildHandshakeHeaders({tunnelId, tunnelKey, clientVersion?, versions?}): Record<string,string>
  negotiateProtocolVersion(offered, supported?): number | null
  validateHandshakeRequest(headers, supported?): HandshakeAccepted | HandshakeRejected
  interpretHandshakeResponse(status, headers): UpgradeResponseOk | UpgradeResponseFailure
transport.ts
  interface FrameTransport { send(frame, cb); close(code, reason); terminate(); setHandlers(h) }
  interface TransportHandlers { onFrame(bytes); onInvalidMessage(detail); onClose(code, reason) }
  webSocketTransport(ws: WebSocketLike): FrameTransport
stream.ts
  class TunnelStream extends Duplex { readonly id; readonly metadata; reset(code?) }
session.ts
  new TunnelSession(transport, { role, pingIntervalMs?, deadPeerTimeoutMs?, onProbe? })
  get activeStreamCount / get closed
  openStream(metadata?): TunnelStream          // server role
  ping(): Promise<number>
  probe(path, { timeoutMs? }): Promise<ProbeResult>   // client role; never rejects
  goAway({ code?, reason?, drainTimeoutMs? }): Promise<void>
  close(code?, reason?): void
  events: 'stream' (client), 'goaway', 'close', 'error'

=== C. DATA FLOW ===
  browser -> internal ALB -> nginx :8443 -> tunnel server :8081 (ingress)
    the ingress reads only enough to know the Host, then:
      serverSession.openStream({kind:'http'})  ->  socket.pipe(stream).pipe(socket)
  -> OPEN/DATA frames over the one websocket (nginx `location /tunnel/`, :8080)
  -> clientSession emits 'stream'
      -> stream.pipe(net.connect(caddyLoopbackPort)).pipe(stream)
  -> Caddy -> the user's dev server, and the same path in reverse.
The protocol never parses HTTP. The Host header, upgrades, SSE and chunked bodies
all survive because the streams carry bytes, nothing else.
Who dials is the security boundary: the client picks the address from what
TunnelManager registered, NEVER from anything the server sent. codec.ts drops
address-shaped OPEN metadata so the dialling code can't even see it.

=== D. HOW THE TUNNEL SERVER CONSUMES THIS MODULE — DECISION ===
DECISION: a VENDORED COPY in the server's repo, gated by the same conformance
vectors. Not an npm subpath export of @debugg-ai/debugg-ai-mcp.

Why, concretely:
1. The MCP package would drag its whole dependency tree into the tunnel server's
   image, and two of those dependencies download BINARIES in a postinstall:
   `ngrok` (postinstall.js fetches the ngrok agent) and
   `@radically-straightforward/caddy` (fetches the caddy binary). A tunnel server
   whose job is to REPLACE ngrok would pull the ngrok binary at build time — and
   it cannot stop, because ngrok does not leave the MCP's dependencies until
   rollout step 7, which is after the server ships. It would also inherit the MCP
   SDK, axios, posthog-node, winston and zod for a module that needs none of them.
2. The package is not shaped to be imported. It has no `main` and no `exports`; it
   ships a `bin` and `files: ["dist", ...]`. Making the subpath work means adding
   an `exports` map, which also RESTRICTS resolution for anything that deep-imports
   `@debugg-ai/debugg-ai-mcp/dist/...` today, and adding a build step so
   vectors/*.json ends up in dist (tsc doesn't copy JSON).
3. Deploy coupling. With a subpath, the server can only take a protocol change
   after an MCP npm release, and the MCP releases often for reasons that have
   nothing to do with the tunnel. Vendoring lets the two repos ship on their own
   schedules — which the protocol is versioned for in the first place.
4. Engines: the MCP declares node >=20.20; the existing node service in sentinal
   runs node:18-slim. A dependency edge makes that somebody's problem; a copy
   doesn't.
5. The copy is genuinely self-contained: this module's only imports are `node:`
   built-ins (rule A above), so vendoring it is a file copy, not a fork of a
   dependency graph.
The cost of vendoring is drift, and drift is exactly what the conformance vectors
were built to catch — so the trade is: take the risk the tests already cover,
avoid the risk they don't.

MECHANISM (what the server arc, xkoh.3, has to build)
- Source of truth stays debugg-ai/debugg-ai-mcp at `services/tunnel/protocol/`,
  pinned by tag. The repo is public, so the server's CI needs no credentials.
- The server vendors the directory verbatim, vectors included, into its own tree
  (e.g. `tunnel-server/src/protocol/`), alongside a `vendor.json` recording the
  upstream repo, the pinned ref and a sha256 per file.
- `npm run sync:protocol` in the server repo re-fetches the pinned ref, rewrites
  the directory and refreshes vendor.json. Bumping the protocol is a one-line ref
  change plus that command.
- Two CI gates in the server repo, both required:
    (a) re-sync into a temp dir and fail if the vendored tree differs, so nobody
        can hand-edit the copy;
    (b) run the vendored vectors through the vendored codec and handshake — the
        same test bodies as `__tests__/services/tunnel/protocol/codec.test.ts` and
        handshake.test.ts — so a copy that is subtly wrong fails the build.
  The MCP repo already runs those vectors in `npm test`, so any tag is conformant.
- Change protocol: edit here, bump PROTOCOL_VERSION only for an incompatible wire
  change, tag, re-sync in the server, and deploy the SERVER FIRST so it speaks
  both versions before any client offers the new one. The handshake's version list
  plus the 426 rejection is what makes that ordering safe.

RECOMMENDATION, NOT PART OF THIS DECISION: if a third consumer ever appears — a
VS Code extension, a non-MCP client, a second server — publish
`@debugg-ai/tunnel-protocol` as its own tiny zero-dependency package and have all
three depend on it. That removes the copy without importing the MCP's dependency
tree. It is not worth a new package, a new release pipeline and a new set of
secrets for exactly two consumers today.

=== E. WHAT EACH CONSUMER ARC TOUCHES ===
tunnel server (xkoh.3): validateHandshakeRequest in the http 'upgrade' handler,
  webSocketTransport, `new TunnelSession(transport, {role:'server', onProbe})`,
  openStream per inbound browser connection, RST codes -> DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* markers
  (MARKER_HTTP_STATUS gives the statuses), GOAWAY on SIGTERM, and the constants
  for ws maxPayload / perMessageDeflate. A working reference for the upgrade path
  is startTunnelServer() in `__tests__/integration/tunnelProtocol.test.ts.`
mcp client (xkoh.5): buildHandshakeHeaders + interpretHandshakeResponse around
  its ws connect, webSocketTransport, `new TunnelSession(transport,
  {role:'client'})`, 'stream' -> dial the registered Caddy loopback origin only,
  'goaway' -> reconnect make-before-break, probe() for probeTunnelHealth, and the
  marker constants for extractNgrokErrorCode / tunnelDisposition.
Neither arc imports below services/tunnel/protocol/index.ts.

=== F. WHAT 4.1 MUST NOT DO ===
Change vectors/*.json or the constants to make code pass. They are the contract
the other two arcs are already building against; a change there is a protocol
change, not a fix.

=== G. THE VENDORED UNIT CARRIES ITS OWN CONFORMANCE RUNNER (added after review) ===
Gate (b) above said "the same test bodies as codec.test.ts / handshake.test.ts",
but those bodies and helpers.ts live in `__tests__/`, OUTSIDE the directory the
sync script copies. The server repo would have to hand-copy test files the sync
never touches — drift on day one, in the very mechanism meant to prevent drift.
So the vendored unit gains one more file, and 4.1 must write it:
  services/tunnel/protocol/conformance.ts
    export interface ConformanceFailure { file: string; vector: string; detail: string }
    export function runConformanceVectors(vectors: {
      frames: unknown; invalidFrames: unknown; handshake: unknown;
    }): ConformanceFailure[]
  - Dependency free, like the rest of the directory: the CALLER reads the three
    JSON files and passes them in, so the function needs no fs and works in any
    bundler or runtime.
  - It exercises encodeFrame / decodeFrame / validateHandshakeRequest against
    every vector and returns the failures rather than throwing, so both callers
    can report them their own way.
  - The MCP's codec.test.ts and handshake.test.ts call it (alongside their own
    per-vector it.each cases, which give better failure output locally), and the
    server's CI gate (b) calls exactly the same function on the vendored copy.
    One checker, copied by the same `npm run sync:protocol` as the code it checks.
4.1 file list therefore: codec.ts, handshake.ts, transport.ts, stream.ts,
session.ts, conformance.ts. constants.ts, errors.ts, index.ts and vectors/ are
already complete.
close_reason: Architecture recorded: 8-module map with an acyclic inward dependency order and the hard rule that nothing outside node: built-ins is imported; the interface contracts the 2.1/2.2 tests froze; the data flow and where the SSRF boundary sits. DECISION on server consumption: a VENDORED COPY gated by the same conformance vectors, not an npm subpath export — an npm dependency would pull ngrok's and caddy's binary-downloading postinstalls plus the MCP SDK/axios/posthog/winston/zod into the tunnel server image, needs a new exports map (which restricts today's deep imports) and a build change to ship the vectors, and would couple server deploys to MCP npm releases across a node 18 vs 20.20 engine gap. Sync + two CI gates specified; a separate @debugg-ai/tunnel-protocol package recorded as the future path if a third consumer appears.

title: [tunnel-protocol] 4.1 Core Implementation
description:
Write the minimum code to make the failing unit tests pass. Run the suite after each meaningful change. No extra features, refactors or 'improvements' beyond what the tests cover. Notes: X/Y unit tests passing.

Repo: debugg-ai-mcp. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3 (wire protocol). Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.1.
notes:
CORE IMPLEMENTATION DONE — all 228 protocol unit tests green.

  node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js `__tests__`/services/tunnel/protocol
  Test Suites: 5 passed, 5 total
  Tests:       228 passed, 228 total   (225 written in 2.1, + 3 for the conformance runner)
`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx eslint services/tunnel/protocol` clean.

FILES IMPLEMENTED (services/tunnel/protocol/)
  codec.ts       encode/decode, JSON whitelisting, every rejection rule. Green on
                 the vectors first try.
  handshake.ts   header building, version negotiation, server validation, client
                 interpretation.
  stream.ts      TunnelStream as a Duplex. The one non-obvious bit is the read()
                 override: node's flowing mode goes through the public read(), so
                 overriding it is how the session learns how many bytes the
                 application actually CONSUMED, which is what it grants back.
  session.ts     stream table, single write scheduler, flow control, liveness,
                 GOAWAY drain, probe correlation, teardown.
  conformance.ts the vector runner (3.2 section G). Dependency free and IO free:
                 the caller passes the three parsed JSON docs in, it returns a
                 list of failures. codec.test.ts and handshake.test.ts call it,
                 and so will the tunnel server's CI on its vendored copy.
  index.ts       re-exports conformance.ts too.

THREE THINGS FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING

1. A BROKEN TEST, not a bug (fixed): "stops at the initial window and resumes
   when credit arrives" wrote 300 KiB and then waited for INITIAL_WINDOW + 65536
   = 327680 bytes on the wire — more than the payload, so it could never pass.
   Raised the fixture to 400 KiB, which is what makes "resumed, and only by as
   much as it was granted" observable. Behaviour under test unchanged. This is
   exactly the failure mode of writing tests against stubs, and the reason 2.1's
   notes flag that CI never type checks a test file.

2. SPEC ADDITION: CloseCode.ABNORMAL = 1006. RFC 6455's "connection dropped with
   no close frame" — never sent, only observed, and the sessions report it on
   'close' and in SessionClosedError. 1.2's notes listed only the codes we send.

3. SPEC CLARIFICATION, and the subtlest thing in the arc: THE SESSION ATTACHES
   ITS OWN 'error' SINK TO EVERY STREAM IT CREATES.
   A node Duplex that emits 'error' with no listener throws and kills the
   process, and a tunnel dropping is routine, not exceptional. Worse, node's own
   pipe() installs an 'error' listener on its destination and RE-EMITS when it is
   the only one — so "only report if someone is listening" is not implementable
   by counting listeners, which is how this first showed up (a crash in a test
   that pipes into a stream). 3.1's risk R5 already called for the sink; this
   makes it normative: the session always destroys a stream with its reason, and
   the sink guarantees that can never throw. A consumer's own listener still gets
   the error; one that only listens for 'close' simply doesn't see it.
   The mcp-client and tunnel-server arcs both get this for free.

Two related teardown rules worth knowing when reading session.ts: a pending write
callback is settled with NULL during teardown (handing it an error makes node
emit a SECOND 'error' for a teardown the stream is already reporting), and a
write to a stream whose record is already gone settles the same way.

IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS NOT PINNED BY A TEST
- A stream is freed from the session's table as soon as both ENDs have been
  exchanged, NOT when the Duplex finally destroys itself. Otherwise a stream
  whose response the application has not finished reading would keep holding a
  slot against the 256 cap and keep a GOAWAY drain open indefinitely. The Duplex
  stays alive for the application to read what it buffered.
- goAway() keeps the socket open when there is nothing to drain: the peer may
  still have OPENs in flight and they must be REFUSED rather than dropped. It
  closes when the last stream finishes, or at drainTimeoutMs
  (DEFAULT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 30s, and a server should pass its ECS stopTimeout).
- The automatic 20s PING carries no pending promise, so a closing session has no
  dangling rejection to leak.
close_reason: codec, handshake, stream, session and conformance implemented; all 228 protocol unit tests green, tsc and eslint clean. One broken test fixed (an arithmetically impossible expectation), CloseCode.ABNORMAL added, and the session-owned stream error sink made normative after node's pipe() re-emit behaviour proved listener-counting unworkable.
