title: [tunnel-protocol] 1.1 User Requirements
description:
Capture who the user is, the problem, acceptance criteria (when is this done?), and non-goals. Pre-filled below from the design and the owner's decisions: confirm or adjust, then record with `bd update <id> --notes=...` and close.

Arc specifics:
- Who: the MCP tunnel client and the debugg tunnel server; indirectly, every MCP user testing localhost.
- Problem: one versioned protocol has to carry a remote browser's traffic to the user's localhost over a
  single outbound connection (WSS on 443, so it works behind corporate proxies).
- Acceptance: carries HTTP/1.1, websocket upgrades (HMR), SSE and large chunked bodies; a big download
  never blocks small concurrent streams; pure TS with no binaries; versioned so client and server can
  change independently; one module used by both sides, checked with conformance vectors.
- Non-goals: HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 to the local target, UDP, generic TCP tunnels.

Repo: debugg-ai-mcp. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3 (wire protocol). Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.1.
notes:
CONFIRMED USER REQUIREMENTS (verified against code 2026-09-19)

WHO
- Direct: the MCP tunnel client (the future services/tunnel/debuggTransport.ts, mcp-client arc xkoh.5) and the debugg tunnel server (a new Node/TS service in the debuggai-api rc stack, server arc xkoh.3).
- Indirect: every MCP user whose check_app_in_browser / probe_page / trigger_crawl targets http(s)://localhost:*, i.e. every call that goes through TunnelManager today.

PROBLEM
- A remote browser (browser-session task in our VPC) has to reach the user's localhost. The only connection allowed is one the MCP opens outbound.
- Today: ngrok agent -> ngrok cloud. Verified: TunnelManager.connectWithRetry(localAddr, tunnelDomain, authToken) calls ngrok.connect({proto:'http', addr, hostname, authtoken}), and addr is always Caddy's loopback origin http://127.0.0.1:<proxyPort> (caddyProxy.ts currentHandle()).
- The new protocol replaces that hop. It needs one outbound WSS connection per tunnel on 443: wss://api.debugg.ai/tunnel/v1/connect -> public ALB -> nginx location /tunnel/ -> tunnel server :8080.

ACCEPTANCE (done when)
1. It carries raw HTTP/1.1 byte streams unchanged: websocket upgrades (HMR), SSE, chunked and large bodies, and https://localhost through Caddy. The protocol is payload-agnostic: it never parses or rewrites HTTP, so the Host header and every other byte pass through as-is.
2. Head-of-line isolation: a large download on one stream never blocks a small stream opened after it. Per-stream credit flow control plus round-robin frame scheduling, with frames of at most 64 KiB.
3. Memory is bounded on both sides with a slow reader: backpressure crosses the socket, with no unbounded buffers.
4. Pure TypeScript, no binaries. The only new runtime dependency is `ws` (Node >=20.20 has no stable global WebSocket; verified engines.node ">=20.20.0").
5. Versioned: the client and server negotiate the protocol version at the handshake, so they can ship independently. An unsupported version gets a clear rejection that lists the supported versions.
6. One module used by both sides. services/tunnel/protocol/ in debugg-ai-mcp, with JSON conformance vectors that any copy must pass byte-for-byte.
7. Security: the server can never choose what the client dials. OPEN carries no target address, and the client dials only the loopback origin TunnelManager registered, which blocks SSRF into the user's network. The tunnel key never appears in a URL (it rides in the Authorization header).
8. Liveness: dead peers are detected within 60 s, and idle tunnels survive the public ALB's idle_timeout = 60 (verified sentinal terraform/alb.tf:15).
9. Graceful server deploys: GOAWAY stops new streams while open streams drain, so a tunnel-server deploy mid-run doesn't fail the run.
10. Health probe over the control channel (PROBE/PROBE_RESULT), replacing probeTunnelHealth's public fetch, which can't work once tunnel URLs are VPC-private.

NON-GOALS (v1)
- HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 to the local target; UDP; exposing generic TCP tunnels to users. The streams carry arbitrary bytes, but the server only ever feeds them HTTP/1.1 ingress.
- Client-initiated streams. Every stream is opened by the server for an inbound browser connection.
- Resuming streams across reconnects. Streams die with their websocket; the browser retries its HTTP request.
- Compression (permessage-deflate is off), a session-level (whole-connection) flow-control window, and more than one tunnel per websocket.

CORRECTIONS TO THE PRE-FILLED TEXT
- "Works behind corporate proxies" is only partly true. WSS on 443 passes egress firewalls that allow 443, but an explicit HTTP(S) CONNECT proxy needs client support. The MCP has none today (no HTTPS_PROXY or proxy-agent handling anywhere in services/, utils/ or handlers/), and `ws` doesn't read proxy env vars. That's a client-arc (xkoh.5) concern, not a protocol one. Flagged there; it doesn't block this arc.
- "54 requests per Next.js dev page" is the owner's measurement, recorded only in the design doc. I couldn't re-verify it from code. It motivates multiplexing and is consistent with the 256 stream cap (see 1.2).
close_reason: User requirements confirmed against code (TunnelManager/ngrok connect path, Caddy loopback origin, ALB idle_timeout 60, engines.node). Two corrections recorded in the notes: proxy support is a client-arc concern, and the 54-request figure isn't re-verifiable. No owner decisions needed.

title: [tunnel-protocol] 1.2 System Requirements
description:
Turn the user requirements into technical constraints: API contracts, data model, performance, security, integration points. Pre-filled below: confirm or adjust, record in notes, close.

Arc specifics:
- Transport: one WebSocket (binary messages) per tunnel. Handshake headers: `Authorization: Bearer <tunnelKey>`,
  `X-Tunnel-Id`, `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol: 1`, `X-Client-Version`. Unsupported version → server rejects with
  426 and lists supported versions.
- Frame: type (u8) | streamId (u32 BE) | payload. Types: OPEN (server→client; JSON metadata, NEVER a target
  address), DATA, END (half-close), RST (u16 code), WINDOW (u32 credit), PING/PONG (u64 nonce), GOAWAY
  (reason; no new OPENs, open streams drain), PROBE (JSON {path}) / PROBE_RESULT (JSON {status?, marker?, error?, elapsedMs}).
- The server allocates stream ids. Cap concurrent streams per tunnel (e.g. 256) and RST on overflow.
- Flow control: per-stream credit, initial window 256 KiB, max DATA payload 64 KiB; never send past granted
  credit; bounded buffering per stream.
- Liveness: PING every 20 s (below the ALB's 60 s idle timeout); peer is dead after 60 s of silence.
- Enumerated RST and close codes: REFUSED, RESET, TIMEOUT, PROTOCOL_ERROR, GOING_AWAY.
- Location: debugg-ai-mcp services/tunnel/protocol/, vectors in services/tunnel/protocol/vectors/*.json.

Repo: debugg-ai-mcp. Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md §3 (wire protocol). Arc epic: debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.1.
notes:
CONFIRMED SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS — debugg tunnel wire protocol v1
(Standalone: the server arc xkoh.3.3 and client arc xkoh.5.3 can implement/test from this alone.
 Code lives at debugg-ai-mcp services/tunnel/protocol/, vectors at services/tunnel/protocol/vectors/*.json.)

=== 0. TRANSPORT ===
- One WebSocket per tunnel, client -> server, to the `relayUrl` from POST api/v1/tunnels/
  (wss://api.debugg.ai/tunnel/v1/connect -> public ALB -> nginx `location /tunnel/` -> tunnel server :8080).
- DECIDED: exactly one protocol frame per WebSocket BINARY message. No length prefix — the
  WS message boundary is the frame boundary. "Truncated" therefore means a message shorter
  than the frame's fixed fields.
- A TEXT message, or any message the codec rejects, is a session-fatal PROTOCOL_ERROR.
- DECIDED: permessage-deflate MUST be disabled on both ends (`perMessageDeflate: false` on the
  ws client and the ws server). Dev-server payloads are already compressed, and deflate's
  per-connection buffers break the bounded-memory property below.
- DECIDED: both ends set ws `maxPayload` = MAX_FRAME_SIZE (65541). Larger inbound is a ws-level
  1009 close; nothing legal exceeds it.
- No secret ever goes in the URL (nginx/ALB logs URLs, not headers).

=== 1. HANDSHAKE (HTTP upgrade request) ===
Request headers (client -> server), DECIDED with a consistent X-Debugg-Tunnel-* prefix
(the pre-filled `X-Tunnel-Id` / `X-Client-Version` were renamed for one grep-able namespace,
matching the existing `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Error` response header):
  Authorization: Bearer `<tunnelKey>`                 (required; `tunnelKey` from provision)
  X-Debugg-Tunnel-Id: `<tunnelId>`                    (required; the uuid = hostname label)
  X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol: 1                       (required; COMMA-SEPARATED list of versions
                                                     the client speaks, best first. v1 sends "1")
  X-Debugg-Tunnel-Client-Version: debugg-ai-mcp/4.3.0   (optional, informational -> Tunnel.client_version)
Responses:
  101 + `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol: <selected>`  — the server echoes the one version it picked
      (highest mutually supported). A client that gets no echo, or an echo it didn't offer,
      closes with PROTOCOL_ERROR.
  426 + `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Supported: 1` + JSON body `{"error":"UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION","supported":[1]}`
      — no mutually supported version, or the header is missing/unparseable.
  400 JSON `{"error":"BAD_TUNNEL_ID"}` — id missing or not a DNS label `/^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$/`
      (it has to be a hostname label for `<id>.tunnel.debugg.ai`, and nginx matches `[a-z0-9-]+`).
  401 JSON `{"error":"UNAUTHORIZED"}` — Authorization missing/not Bearer/empty, or the key fails the
      debugg-API verify call. ONE status for bad key / unknown id / revoked / expired: don't leak which.
  Check order: version (426) -> tunnel id (400) -> auth (401).
Client retry policy: 426/400/401 are terminal for this token (re-provision or upgrade — never loop);
  429/5xx/network are retryable with backoff.
The protocol module only validates header PRESENCE and SHAPE. Token verification is the server
arc's call to the debugg API (POST /api/internal/tunnels/verify/).

=== 2. FRAME LAYOUT ===
  offset 0, 1 byte : type (u8)
  offset 1, 4 bytes: streamId (u32 big-endian)
  offset 5, N bytes: payload (N = message length - 5)
  HEADER_SIZE = 5. streamId 0 is RESERVED for session-level frames.

  type  name          dir   streamId       payload
  0x01  OPEN          S->C  != 0, new      UTF-8 JSON object, 2..16384 bytes
  0x02  DATA          both  != 0           1..65536 raw bytes (empty DATA is illegal)
  0x03  END           both  != 0           empty
  0x04  RST           both  != 0           u16 BE error code (exactly 2 bytes)
  0x05  WINDOW        both  != 0           u32 BE credit increment, 1..2147483647 (exactly 4)
  0x06  PING          both  == 0           u64 BE nonce (exactly 8 bytes)
  0x07  PONG          both  == 0           u64 BE nonce, echoed (exactly 8)
  0x08  GOAWAY        both  == 0           u16 BE code + UTF-8 reason, 0..1024 bytes of reason
  0x09  PROBE         C->S  != 0 probe id  UTF-8 JSON `{"path":"/..."}` , <= 16384 bytes
  0x0A  PROBE_RESULT  S->C  != 0 probe id  UTF-8 JSON `{status?,marker?,error?,elapsedMs}`, <= 16384
  0x00 and 0x0B..0xFF are invalid -> PROTOCOL_ERROR.
Codec-level (direction-agnostic) rejection -> PROTOCOL_ERROR: bad length, wrong payload size,
streamId 0 where != 0 is required (and vice versa), invalid UTF-8, JSON that isn't an object,
JSON missing a required field or with a wrong-typed known field, WINDOW increment 0 or > 2^31-1,
PROBE path that doesn't start with "/" or is > 2048 chars, PROBE_RESULT without a finite
elapsedMs >= 0 or with status outside 100..599.
JSON objects: unknown fields are DROPPED on decode (forward compatible); known fields with the
wrong type are a PROTOCOL_ERROR. Canonical encoding = JSON.stringify of the known fields in
spec order, no whitespace (this is what the byte-for-byte vectors pin); decoders accept any
equivalent JSON text.
OPEN metadata v1 known fields (both informational): `kind` ("http" | "probe", string <= 32 chars)
and `requestId` (string <= 128 chars, for correlating both sides' logs).
  SECURITY (load-bearing): OPEN NEVER carries a target address, and no receiver may derive a dial
  target from any metadata field. The decoder's whitelist enforces it — an OPEN carrying
  target/addr/host/port decodes to `{kind}` only. The client dials ONLY the loopback origin
  TunnelManager registered (Caddy's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`). This is the SSRF boundary.

=== 3. ERROR CODES (u16; used in RST, GOAWAY, and as WS close code 4000+code) ===
  1 REFUSED              stream was NOT processed — cap reached, or an OPEN arrived after the
                         receiver sent GOAWAY. The opener may retry it on another session.
  2 RESET                stream aborted by an endpoint (browser went away, local socket error).
  3 TIMEOUT              a deadline expired (dead peer, drain deadline).
  4 PROTOCOL_ERROR       the peer violated this spec.
  5 GOING_AWAY           sender is shutting down (SIGTERM/deploy, client disconnect, session
                         replaced by a newer connection for the same tunnel id) — reconnect.
  6 UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE client could not connect to its local target -> the server renders
                         DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED (the ERR_NGROK_8012 analogue). ADDED
                         beyond the pre-filled list: without it the server cannot tell
                         "couldn't dial localhost" (tunnel alive, do not tear down) from
                         "stream refused, safe to retry", which is exactly the distinction the
                         existing tunnelDisposition policy is built on.
  7 REVOKED              tunnel ended for good (revoked, or past its hard max lifetime). GOAWAY/
                         close only. The client MUST NOT reconnect with this token; re-provision.
                         ADDED so a revoke doesn't become a reconnect loop that 401s.
  0 reserved, never sent. Codecs accept ANY u16 on the wire (forward compat); a session maps an
  unknown code to RESET (in RST) or GOING_AWAY (in GOAWAY) and never errors on it.
WS close codes: 1000 after a fully drained graceful close; otherwise 4000+code
  (4003 TIMEOUT, 4004 PROTOCOL_ERROR, 4005 GOING_AWAY, 4007 REVOKED). Dead-peer detection
  terminates the socket instead of closing it (no handshake is possible with a dead peer).

=== 4. STREAMS ===
- Only the SERVER opens streams (one per inbound browser connection; nginx does not keepalive the
  tunnel upstream, so one browser request == one connection == one stream).
- The server allocates streamIds: strictly increasing u32 from 1, never reused in a session.
  An OPEN whose id is <= a previously used id is a session-fatal PROTOCOL_ERROR. Exhausting
  0xFFFFFFFF -> GOAWAY(GOING_AWAY) and reconnect.
- No OPEN ack: the opener may send DATA immediately after OPEN. The client either starts dialing
  or refuses with RST(REFUSED) / RST(UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE).
- END = half close ("no more DATA from me"); each direction closes independently. A stream is
  fully closed when END has been both sent and received, or when RST is sent or received; it is
  freed at that instant and stops counting toward the cap.
- DATA or END after the peer's END -> RST(PROTOCOL_ERROR) on that stream (stream-scoped, not fatal).
- Frames for an id that was used and is now closed are silently DISCARDED (they race with RST).
  Frames for an id that was never opened are session-fatal PROTOCOL_ERROR.
- MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS = 256 per session, confirmed against the 1.4 integration test that opens
  200 at once, and against the measured ~54 requests of one Next.js dev page (the internal ALB
  speaks HTTP/2 to the browser, so a page's requests can arrive nearly all at once). The server
  MUST NOT exceed it (its ingress queues or fails the browser request); a receiver that gets a
  257th concurrent OPEN answers RST(REFUSED) and never surfaces the stream. Because frames are
  ordered and each side frees a stream no later than the peer does, a conforming server never
  trips the receiver's cap.

=== 5. FLOW CONTROL (per stream, per direction, credit based) ===
- INITIAL_WINDOW = 262144 bytes (256 KiB), fixed in v1, not negotiated. Each stream direction
  starts with that much credit at OPEN.
- MAX_DATA_PAYLOAD = 65536 per DATA frame.
- A sender MUST NOT send DATA exceeding its remaining credit; at 0 it waits for WINDOW.
- WINDOW(increment) adds credit. A resulting window > 2147483647 -> RST(PROTOCOL_ERROR) on that stream.
- A receiver MUST NOT grant credit for bytes its application hasn't consumed: outstanding credit
  (granted - received) never exceeds INITIAL_WINDOW, so per-stream receive buffering is <= 256 KiB
  and total receive buffering <= 256 * 256 KiB = 64 MiB per tunnel, worst case.
- DATA exceeding the receive window -> RST(PROTOCOL_ERROR) on that stream; the excess is not buffered.
- Recommended receiver policy (pinned by tests, not by the wire): send WINDOW once
  consumed-but-unannounced bytes reach WINDOW_UPDATE_THRESHOLD = 65536 (1/4 window), so the sender
  never stalls while >= 3/4 of the window is still in flight.
- Per-stream throughput is capped at window/RTT (~2.5 MB/s at 100 ms RTT). Aggregate scales with
  concurrency. RISK recorded for 3.1: if one big dev-server chunk is too slow, raise INITIAL_WINDOW
  in v2 or add a negotiated window — do NOT hand-tune one side.
- Send-side bounding: the session hands frames to the socket only while fewer than
  MAX_UNACKED_SEND_BYTES = 262144 are un-acked (ws send callback pending), so a peer that stops
  reading cannot inflate the ws send buffer.

=== 6. SCHEDULING / FAIRNESS ===
- DATA is scheduled round-robin across streams that have both pending bytes and credit, one frame
  (<= 64 KiB) at a time. A stream with a 10 MB backlog delays another stream's next frame by at
  most ONE frame.
- Control frames (WINDOW, PING, PONG, RST, GOAWAY, PROBE, PROBE_RESULT) jump ahead of queued DATA.
  OPEN and END keep their stream's order (OPEN before that stream's first DATA; END after its last).

=== 7. LIVENESS ===
- PING_INTERVAL_MS = 20000. Each side sends PING every 20 s. 20 s is under the public ALB's
  idle_timeout = 60 (verified: sentinal terraform/alb.tf:15) and under nginx's 60 s
  proxy_send_timeout on the /ws/ block that `location /tunnel/` is copied from.
- Every PING MUST be answered with PONG carrying the same nonce, ahead of queued DATA. A PONG with
  an unknown nonce is ignored, never an error.
- DEAD_PEER_TIMEOUT_MS = 60000. If NO frame of any type arrives for 60 s, the peer is dead:
  terminate the socket, fail every open stream with TIMEOUT, report close code 4003.

=== 8. GOAWAY ===
- GOAWAY(code, reason) = "I will open no more streams, and I will RST(REFUSED) any OPEN that
  arrives after this". Open streams keep running.
- Server on SIGTERM: GOAWAY(GOING_AWAY) -> the client immediately dials a NEW connection
  (make-before-break) while old streams drain -> the server closes with 1000 once all streams
  finish, or at its drain deadline (ECS stopTimeout) RSTs the rest with GOING_AWAY and closes 4005.
- GOAWAY(PROTOCOL_ERROR) is sent best-effort immediately before a 4004 close; GOAWAY(REVOKED)
  before a 4007 close. A second GOAWAY is legal; the latest code wins.

=== 9. PROBE (replaces probeTunnelHealth's public fetch) ===
- Client -> server: PROBE(probeId, `{"path":"/..."}`) . probeIds are client-allocated non-zero u32
  counters in their OWN id space (the frame type disambiguates them from streamIds).
- Server -> client: exactly one PROBE_RESULT(probeId, {...}). OWNER DECISION (2026-09-19): the
  server issues the GET through its REAL INGRESS PATH — `https://<id>.tunnel.debugg.ai<path>`,
  so the probe proves DNS, the internal ALB and nginx as well as the tunnel, rather than
  short-cutting straight down the client's websocket. The request therefore comes back to the
  client as an ordinary ingress stream; `kind:"probe"` on the OPEN is optional labelling, and
  neither side may assume a probe stream looks different from browser traffic. It reports:
    status      HTTP status the local app returned
    marker      a DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* marker when the tunnel itself failed
    error       "TIMEOUT" | "RESET" | ... when there was no HTTP response at all
    elapsedMs   required
- PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000 client-side (matches today's TunnelHealthProbeOptions.timeoutMs default).
  On timeout the client resolves {error:"TIMEOUT", elapsedMs} — the probe API never throws, which
  is probeTunnelHealth's existing contract. A late PROBE_RESULT is ignored; so is one for an
  unknown probeId. A session close resolves pending probes with `{error:"CLOSED"}`.
- Mapping to utils/localReachability.ts TunnelHealthProbeResult, for the client arc (do not re-derive):
    {status, no marker, status not 502/504} -> {healthy:true, status, elapsedMs}
    {status 502|504, no marker}             -> {healthy:false, code:'BAD_GATEWAY', status, elapsedMs}
       (this is the common "app is down" case: Caddy answers 502 with no marker)
    {marker}                                -> {healthy:false, code:'NGROK_ERROR' (rename later),
                                                ngrokErrorCode: marker, status, elapsedMs}
    `{error:"TIMEOUT"}`                       -> {healthy:false, code:'TIMEOUT', elapsedMs}
    {error: anything else}                  -> {healthy:false, code:'NETWORK_ERROR', detail, elapsedMs}

=== 10. SERVER ERROR MARKERS (shared constants; server emits, client parses) ===
  DEBUGG_TUNNEL_OFFLINE          (404) no client connected  — the ERR_NGROK_3200 analogue
  DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN          (404) unknown or revoked tunnel id
  DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UPSTREAM_REFUSED (502) client could not dial its local target — ERR_NGROK_8012 analogue
- Placement: in the response body AND in the `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Error` header. BODY placement is
  load-bearing and normative: probeTunnelHealth reads only the body (readCapped 4096 ->
  extractNgrokErrorCode), so the marker MUST appear within the first 4096 bytes of the body.
- RECONNECT_GRACE_MS = 5000, NORMATIVE for the server: a browser request for a tunnel whose client
  is reconnecting is HELD up to 5 s before OFFLINE is rendered, so a deploy or a network blip
  doesn't fail a run.
- Even so, the client MUST keep confirming OFFLINE across its retry ladder before treating it as
  teardown-authorising, exactly as localReachability does for ERR_NGROK_3200 today: a reconnect
  that outlasts the grace window would otherwise evict a live tunnel that we are paying for.
  DEBUGG_TUNNEL_UNKNOWN is definitive (the id is gone) and is the one that joins
  tunnelDisposition's ENDPOINT_GONE allowlist. UPSTREAM_REFUSED NEVER authorises teardown.

=== 11. CONSTANTS (services/tunnel/protocol/constants.ts — one source of truth for both repos) ===
  PROTOCOL_VERSION 1 · SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS [1] · HEADER_SIZE 5
  MAX_DATA_PAYLOAD 65536 · MAX_FRAME_SIZE 65541 · MAX_JSON_PAYLOAD 16384
  MAX_GOAWAY_REASON_BYTES 1024 · MAX_PROBE_PATH_LENGTH 2048 · MAX_REQUEST_ID_LENGTH 128
  INITIAL_WINDOW 262144 · MAX_WINDOW 2147483647 · WINDOW_UPDATE_THRESHOLD 65536
  MAX_UNACKED_SEND_BYTES 262144 · MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS 256 · MAX_STREAM_ID 4294967295
  PING_INTERVAL_MS 20000 · DEAD_PEER_TIMEOUT_MS 60000 · PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS 5000
  RECONNECT_GRACE_MS 5000
  FrameType / ErrorCode / CloseCode / Header / TunnelErrorMarker as frozen `as const` objects.

=== 12. NON-FUNCTIONAL ===
- Pure TypeScript, Node built-ins only (node:stream, node:events, node:buffer). The protocol module
  imports NOTHING else from this repo — no utils/logger, no config (config/index.ts validates
  DEBUGGAI_API_KEY at import time and would break a server embedding it), and no `ws` at runtime;
  `ws` only appears in the thin WebSocket adapter, behind a structural interface.
- Conformance vectors: services/tunnel/protocol/vectors/{frames,invalid-frames,handshake}.json.
  ANY copy of this module (see 3.2) must pass them byte-for-byte.

=== DECISIONS I MADE AS PROTOCOL OWNER (recorded, not open questions) ===
  one frame per WS binary message · streamId 0 reserved for session frames · permessage-deflate off
  · ws maxPayload pinned · X-Debugg-Tunnel-* header naming · version header is a list + 101 echo
  · stream cap 256 · error codes 6 (UPSTREAM_UNREACHABLE) and 7 (REVOKED) added · unknown codes
  map to RESET/GOING_AWAY · unknown JSON fields dropped / wrong-typed known fields fatal
  · RECONNECT_GRACE_MS 5000 and body placement of markers made normative.

=== ANSWERED (were open questions at 1.2) ===
Both questions raised at 1.2 have been ANSWERED by the owner (2026-09-19):
 1. CORPORATE PROXIES: accepted risk. No HTTPS_PROXY support; outbound 443 to the tunnel host
    must be allowed. Requirement this places on the mcp-client arc (xkoh.5): where a connect
    fails in a way consistent with blocked egress, the error message must SAY PLAINLY that
    outbound 443 to the tunnel host has to be allowed, so a proxied user is not left guessing.
    Nothing in the protocol module changes; connect-time failures are the client's to phrase.
 2. PROBE: goes through the real ingress path — see section 9 above, now normative.
 3. Rollout selection is an on/off switch plus named accounts, with a percentage available but
    defaulting to off. No protocol impact; recorded for context.

=== WHERE THE TYPESCRIPT SURFACE IS (for the test-writing beads gated on this one) ===
- The API is frozen at `services/tunnel/protocol/index.ts` (stubs exist today, every
  function throws `not implemented`) and written out signature by signature in
  `bd show debugg_ai_mcp-xkoh.1.6` section B.
- A working server-side upgrade harness — validateHandshakeRequest in an http
  'upgrade' handler, the 426 response, handleUpgrade + webSocketTransport, and the
  101 version echo — is `startTunnelServer()` in
  `__tests__/integration/tunnelProtocol.test.ts`.
- Cross-checked 2026-09-19 against the mcp-client arc's red tests: they already use
  `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Id` / `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Protocol` / `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Client-Version` /
  `X-Debugg-Tunnel-Supported`, the three DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* markers with 404/404/502, and
  the PROBE_RESULT `{status, marker, elapsedMs}` shape. No contradiction between the
  two arcs' tests.
close_reason: Wire protocol v1 pinned in notes: frame layout + all 10 frame types, 7 error codes with numeric values, WS close-code mapping, stream id allocation and the 256 cap, 256 KiB credit flow control with 64 KiB frames, 20s PING / 60s dead-peer, GOAWAY drain, PROBE/PROBE_RESULT and its mapping onto TunnelHealthProbeResult, handshake headers + 426/400/401 shapes, and the DEBUGG_TUNNEL_* markers with normative body placement. Verified against alb.tf idle_timeout=60, the nginx /ws/ block, localReachability/tunnelDisposition, and the provision response shape. Unblocks xkoh.3.3 and xkoh.5.3. Two non-blocking open questions for other arcs recorded in notes (MCP proxy support; whether the server's PROBE goes through ingress).

title: [epic] Debugg tunnel server — replace ngrok with our own tunnel server
description:
Replace ngrok with a debugg-owned tunnel server. The architecture keeps ngrok's shape: the MCP's tunnel service connects out to a tunnel server, and the debugg API issues and scopes the tokens (it used to mint ngrok keys; it now mints its own). The server runs in the debugg API server group (debuggai-api rc stack), NOT in browser-mgr, and is fronted by the existing nginx. Hostnames are <id>.tunnel.debugg.ai (only that subdomain is delegated to Route53). Tunnels are private to our VPC for now.

Design: debugg-ai-mcp/docs/debugg-tunnel-server-design-2026-09-19.md

Owner decisions (2026-09-19): same architecture as ngrok; built in-house; DNS in AWS; subdomain under debugg.ai; private for now; server lives in the debuggai-api stack, not browser-mgr (which should need no changes); reuse nginx.

Each arc is a test-first chain of 12 phases (feature-lifecycle): requirements → failing tests → strategy/architecture → implementation → validation → harden and ship. Arcs:
- protocol: shared wire protocol (MCP repo)
- tokens: token management in the debugg API (sentinal)
- server: the tunnel server (new service, platform repo)
- infra: DNS, cert, internal ALB, nginx, rc (sentinal deploy)
- mcp-client: the MCP tunnel client (this repo)

title: [bug] A single transient status-poll failure loses the whole run — pollExecution's getExecution is unguarded
description:
Rescued from PR #5 (fix/poll-transient-failures, opened 2026-05-29, branch SHA 12725fc), which rotted 98 commits behind main and now conflicts. The BUG IS STILL LIVE ON MAIN — re-verified 2026-08-19.

EVIDENCE (origin/main @ 7a7a4a5):
  services/workflows.ts, inside pollExecution's `while (Date.now() < deadline)` loop:
      const execution = await service.getExecution(executionUuid);
  That call is unguarded. It is the ONLY thing between a transient blip and
  losing a run that the server is still happily executing.

AND THE TRANSPORT DOES NOT COVER IT:
  utils/axiosTransport.ts:48 installs a response interceptor that only RESHAPES
  the error and re-rejects — no axios-retry, no retryCondition anywhere in the
  repo (grep 'axios-retry|retryCondition' returns nothing). The client axios
  timeout is 30_000ms while EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS gives the run a 10-minute
  server-side budget, so a slow backend, a 5xx during a deploy, or one ECONNRESET
  throws straight out of the poll loop and aborts the check.

USER-VISIBLE SHAPE: caller sees 'DebuggAI error: timeout of 30000ms exceeded'
on a multi-step run; the run keeps going server-side and the result is thrown
away. Originally reported from the MCR-iOS app agent.

FIX SHAPE (from the rotted PR, re-apply fresh onto main — do NOT resurrect the branch):
  tolerate up to MAX_CONSECUTIVE_POLL_FAILURES (5) CONSECUTIVE failed polls,
  retry on the existing backoff schedule, keep going until the deadline. Reset
  the counter on any successful poll. Only give up when the run is genuinely
  unreachable, not on a single blip. Note pollExecution has since gained
  lastExecution/timedOut partial-result handling (bead 56kd.3) — the retry has
  to compose with that, which is exactly why the old branch cannot be replayed.

title: Hallucination guard rejects assertions by keyword-overlap with the GOAL, not against the page — honest 'the app is not in the expected state' is unrepresentable
description:
The hallucination guard requires the agent's assertion to share keywords with the
TASK GOAL. So when the page is not what the caller expected, an agent that reports
that honestly is rejected — three times — and the run grades `fail`.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-02, execution 00c1214b-827c-4d72-a550-38793fc6ab21:

  task: url http://localhost:3011/login
        "Report the page title and whether a login form is visible. Nothing else."
  what actually happened: the session was already authenticated, so /login redirected
        to the Dashboard. The browser worked; the screenshot shows the Dashboard fully
        rendered; the agent took 3 steps.
  agent's assertion: text_visible('Dashboard')   <- TRUE, and the correct observation
  guard: rejected x3 —
     "assertion does not reference any goal token. goal tokens=['else','form','logi…']"
     final: "hallucination guard: assertion rejected 3 times, last reason=keyword_overlap"
  outcome: fail

The guard's premise is inverted. A hallucination guard should reject claims the PAGE
does not support. This one rejects claims the GOAL does not mention — which is a
different thing, and it fails in exactly the case that matters most: **the app is not
in the state you assumed.** "You asked about a login form; there isn't one, this is
the Dashboard" is the single most useful thing a browser agent can tell you, and it
is unrepresentable.

WORSE, IT BIASES TOWARD CONFIRMATION. The only way past the guard is an assertion
built from the goal's own vocabulary. That pressures the agent toward asserting what
was asked about rather than what is present — the precise behaviour a hallucination
guard exists to prevent. An agent that invented "login form is visible" would have
passed the guard; the honest one did not.

DISTINCT FROM debugg_ai_mcp-0cyr. That bead is "a read-only describe task is graded
by a forced assertion". This is narrower and mechanical: the assertion is checked for
KEYWORD OVERLAP WITH THE GOAL, not against the page. Fixing 0cyr by making assertions
optional would mask this rather than fix it.

FIX DIRECTION:
 1. Validate an assertion against the PAGE, not against the goal string. Page evidence
    is already gathered — `text_visible('Dashboard')` was verifiable and true.
 2. Allow an explicit "expectation not met" outcome carrying what WAS found, and grade
    it a successful observation, not `fail`. A redirect away from the requested URL is
    a finding, not a tooling failure.
 3. If goal-overlap is kept as a heuristic, it must be a WARNING, never a rejection —
    and never a terminal one after N retries.

Related: debugg_ai_mcp-zf4g (supplied URLs not treated as authoritative — here the
redirect away from /login was also never surfaced as a finding).

comments.author: Quinn
comments.text:
FIXED (platform side, sentinal) 2026-08-02. Unit-verified; live-agent verification BLOCKED on environment — detail at the end, please read it before treating this as closed.

REPRODUCED FIRST, exactly. Ran the real validate_keyword_overlap against the filed
repro inputs. Goal tokenizes to ['else','form','login','nothing','page','report',
'title','visible','whether'] — matching the truncated ['else','form','logi...'] in
the bead character-for-character.

TWO ROOT CAUSES, and the second is the one that matters.

(a) MECHANICAL: 'report' was absent from _READ_ONLY_VERBS (hallucination_guard.py
:71). 'Report the page title...' is as read-only as a goal gets, but with no
read-only verb matched it took the STRICT path, and 'Dashboard' shares no token
with the goal -> hard reject.

(b) ARCHITECTURAL, and this is the bead's actual complaint: at browser_use.py the
keyword check runs at :791 and run_assertion runs at :815. The guard rejects for
not matching the GOAL *before it ever asks the PAGE*. Page evidence was available
and would have said TRUE. The premise really is inverted, exactly as filed.

THE CONFIRMATION BIAS IS NOW MEASURED, not just argued. Same goal, two targets:
  text_visible('Dashboard')   honest, TRUE on the page  -> REJECTED (pre-fix)
  text_visible('login form')  invented, FALSE on page   -> ACCEPTED (pre-fix)
The guard actively preferred the hallucination. That is now a regression test.

    is ONLY the goal-keyword check, which was never evidence about the page. A
    fabricated observation still dies on text_not_found — so the case where this
    guard earned its keep (20 green jest tests against a component that was not in
    the live DOM) is untouched.
  * it cannot manufacture a pass on an ACTION goal: success is derived from
    is_observational_goal(goal), not from the agent. On 'open the admin console' an
    observation means the action did not happen and it terminates success=False.
  * observations recorded under Done.output['observations'], SEPARATE from
    verified_assertions, so a caller can tell 'this is what the page shows' from
    'the goal was achieved' structurally instead of by reading prose.
  * 'report'/'identify'/'enumerate'/'observe'/'summarize' added to the read-only
    verbs. Deliberately NOT added: state/note/record/detail/capture — each is a far
    more common NOUN in this product's task text ('the state detail dock').

VERIFIED:

both pre-existing and neither caused by this change:

     set. root conftest.py:41 already says 'a skip is not a pass' and enforces it

     canaries have been quietly not-running in this environment.

So: the guard logic is unit-verified and the canaries are protected at the unit
level, but nothing here has been driven end-to-end through a real browser agent.
That should happen before this closes. Filing (1) is probably worth its own bead —
a canary suite that skips by default is the failure mode this batch is about.

title: check_app_in_browser: auth.entryUrl/deepUrl bypass the localhost tunnel — offscope_host + ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED on the documented login path
description:
Passing an `auth` precondition block makes the remote browser resolve localhost to
ITSELF — the tunnel is never used for the entry navigation.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-01, twice, with a clean A/B minutes apart against the same app:

  FAILS — with the auth block:
    check_app_in_browser({
      url: "http://localhost:3011/projects/<uuid>/validation?...",
      username, password,
      auth: { precondition: "login",
              entryUrl: "http://localhost:3011/login",
              deepUrl:  "http://localhost:3011/projects/<uuid>/validation?..." }
    })
    -> outcome fail. reason: "Chrome error screen ... 'This site can't be reached',
       'localhost refused to connect.', 'ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED'"
    -> logins[0] = { reason: "offscope_host", source: "explicit",
                     submitted: false, authenticated: false }

  WORKS — same URL, same credentials, auth block REMOVED, ~2 min later:
    check_app_in_browser({ url: <same>, username, password })
    -> outcome pass, logins[0].authenticated = true, full page rendered.

The dev server was serving 200 on localhost throughout (curl-verified before each
run). So this is not the app and not tunnel provisioning in general — the plain path
tunnels correctly. It is the AUTH-PRECONDITION path specifically: `entryUrl` (and
presumably `deepUrl`) appear to be navigated without the localhost rewrite the top-
level `url` gets, so the remote browser dials its OWN localhost. `offscope_host` is
the tool telling us it considered the host out of scope.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE WORKAROUND: the auth block is the documented way to
say "log in THEN deep-navigate", and the tool's own description recommends it over
"hoping the agent signs itself in at a login wall". So the recommended path is the
broken one on localhost, and the workaround (drop the block, let the agent find the
login form) is the thing the docs warn against.

FIX DIRECTION: every URL the run may navigate — `url`, `auth.entryUrl`,
`auth.deepUrl` — must go through the same localhost→tunnel rewrite, and the scope
allowlist must include the tunneled host for all of them. A test that passes an
auth block with a localhost entryUrl and asserts the browser reached the tunnel
host (not 127.0.0.1) would have caught it.

Sibling filed in the wrong repo while triaging: sentinal-yuft8 (a downstream
"canvas never browser-verified" bead). Cross-referenced there.
close_reason: Fixed and shipped. PR #21 merged to main as ff41391 (rebased onto current main, 72/72 suites / 1088 tests green, tsc --noEmit clean, Boot Smoke green), published as npm 4.2.2. retargetAuxiliaryUrl() now puts auth.entryUrl/auth.deepUrl through the same localhost->tunnel rewrite as the top-level url; a cross-port aux URL is refused fast with AuthUrlPortMismatch instead of dialling the remote browser's own loopback. NOT yet exercised by a live localhost-tunnel run through auth.entryUrl — that surface remains unverified.

comments.author: Quinn
comments.text:
FIXED (MCP side) + verified live 2026-08-02.

ROOT CAUSE, exact: handlers/testPageChangesHandler.ts built the whole tunnel
context from input.url ALONE —
  :162  const originalUrl = resolveTargetUrl(input)   // reads input.url only
  :163  let ctx = buildContext(originalUrl)
  :411  targetUrl: ctx.targetUrl ?? originalUrl       // <- rewritten
  :427  auth.entryUrl = input.auth.entryUrl           // <- VERBATIM, never rewritten
  :428  auth.deepUrl  = input.auth.deepUrl            // <- VERBATIM
So a localhost entryUrl reached the remote browser as a literal localhost:PORT and
it dialled its own loopback. Confirms the bead's diagnosis precisely.

run may navigate now goes through the same localhost->tunnel rewrite as url. The
primitive already existed (retargetTunnelUrl) and already preserved
pathname+search+hash, so the query string survives (relevant to zf4g).

CROSS-PORT IS REFUSED, NOT REWRITTEN. Under the session-tunnel + Caddy model one
call pins exactly ONE upstream port (acquirePortRoute reads ctx.originalUrl's
port). Retargeting a different-port auth URL onto the same origin would dispatch
the login to whichever port Caddy holds — the silent misdirection the port lock
exists to prevent. That path returns a structured AuthUrlPortMismatch and
dispatches nothing.

LIVE A/B, same URL + same auth block + same prod backend, ~10 min apart:
  BEFORE  8ceac3be-3ea4-40d2-b85f-74196bc53ec0  outcome=fail, 1 step

          Debugger', Email + Password fields visible

Dev server curl/fetch-verified 200 on :3011 immediately before each run.
